workedExample.problem: A torch does not light. Find the fault step by step.
steps: Check that the cells are placed the right way round, positive to negative
Check whether the cells are used up by trying new ones
Check that the bulb's filament is not broken
Check that the switch and the metal contacts touch properly and are not rusty or dirty
Fix the break you find; once the circuit is closed again, the bulb lights
fadedVersion: Check that the cells are placed ___ to negative
Check whether the cells are ___ by trying new ones
Check that the bulb's ___ is not broken
Check that the ___ and metal contacts touch properly
Fix the break; once the circuit is ___ again, the bulb lights

skills.title: Recognise and draw standard circuit symbols: cell, battery, bulb, switch (open and closed) and connecting wire
Draw a circuit diagram from a real circuit, and build or read a circuit from a diagram
Explain that a switch only opens or closes the path and does not make electricity
Predict the effects of where a switch is placed and of the number of cells in a battery

expectations: Circuit diagrams use standard symbols so anyone can read them: a cell is a long thin line (positive) beside a short thick line (negative); a battery is two or more cell symbols joined; a bulb is a circle with a cross; a switch is shown as a gap that can be bridged.
In the ON position a switch closes the gap and completes the circuit; in the OFF position it opens the gap and breaks the circuit.
A switch does not make or store electricity; the cell is the source, and the switch only controls whether the path is complete.
In a single loop, a switch works wherever it is placed, before or after the bulb, because a break anywhere stops the current everywhere.
In a battery, the positive terminal of one cell is joined to the negative terminal of the next; more cells push a bigger current and make a bulb brighter.

misconceptions.belief: A switch makes electricity.
signs: Says 'the switch gives the bulb electricity'
Thinks a torch with a broken switch has no electricity in it

diagnostic.prompt_en: In a circuit with a cell, a bulb and a switch, what does pressing the switch to ON do?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Cell, bulb aur switch wale circuit mein switch ON karne se kya hota hai?

options.text: It makes electricity, which then travels to the bulb
It closes the gap so current from the cell can flow around the loop
It stores electricity for later

remediation.representation: A drawbridge animation: the switch as a bridge that lets the moving dots cross, with the cell as the engine that moves them
remediation.moveShape: Remove the switch and join the wires directly; ask the child where the electricity came from now

misconceptions.belief: A switch only works if it is placed before the bulb, between the + terminal and the bulb.
signs: Says a switch after the bulb cannot turn it off because current 'already reached' the bulb
Reasons about current step by step as if it travels in a queue

diagnostic.prompt_en: A switch is put in the wire going from the bulb back to the − terminal. When the switch is turned OFF, does the bulb go off?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Switch us taar mein lagaya gaya jo bulb se − terminal tak waapas jaata hai. Switch OFF karne pe kya bulb bujhega?

options.text: No, the current already reached the bulb before the switch
Yes, a break anywhere in the loop stops current everywhere
It only gets a little dimmer

remediation.representation: A bicycle-chain picture: break the chain at any link and the whole chain stops moving
remediation.moveShape: Move the switch to three different places in a simulated loop and ask the child to predict each time before toggling

misconceptions.belief: In the cell symbol, the short thick line is the positive terminal.
signs: Labels the short thick line '+'
Draws batteries with cells joined + to +

diagnostic.prompt_en: In the circuit symbol for a cell, which line stands for the positive terminal?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Cell ke circuit symbol mein kaunsi line positive terminal ko dikhati hai?

options.text: The longer, thinner line
The shorter, thicker line
Both lines mean the same thing

remediation.representation: A real cell photo lined up with its symbol: the cap end matched to the long line
remediation.moveShape: Have the child trace from the real cap to the long line and say 'long is plus' while drawing three cells in a row

items.prompt_en: Describe the circuit symbol for an electric cell. Which side is positive?
items.prompt_hi: Electric cell ka circuit symbol kaisa hota hai? Kaunsi side positive hai?
items.answer: Two parallel lines: a longer thin line and a shorter thick line; the longer line is the positive terminal.
hints: Ask how many lines the symbol has
Point to their different lengths
Prompt: the ___ line is positive and the ___ line is negative
Assert: long thin line is positive, short thick line is negative

verified.solverAnswer: Long thin line is positive, short thick line is negative.

items.prompt_en: How is an open switch drawn differently from a closed switch in a circuit diagram?
items.prompt_hi: Circuit diagram mein khula (open) switch band (closed) switch se alag kaise banaya jaata hai?
items.answer: An open switch is drawn with a gap in the line (the lever not touching across); a closed switch is drawn with the gap bridged so the line is continuous.
hints: Ask what an open door leaves in a wall
Point to the gap in the symbol
Prompt: an open switch has a ___; a closed switch has the gap ___
Assert: open switch shows a gap; closed switch completes the line

verified.solverAnswer: Open switch is drawn with a gap/raised arm; closed switch shows the line complete with no gap.

items.prompt_en: A circuit has a cell, a bulb and a switch that is OFF. Predict: if we take the switch out completely and join the two wires directly, will the bulb glow?
items.prompt_hi: Ek circuit mein cell, bulb aur OFF switch hai. Guess karo: agar switch poora nikaal ke dono taar seedhe jod dein, toh kya bulb jalega?
items.answer: Yes. The switch does not make electricity; joining the wires completes the loop just as an ON switch does.
hints: Ask where the electricity really comes from
Point to the cell as the source
Prompt: joining the wires ___ the loop, just like an ___ switch
Assert: it glows; the switch only opens or closes the path

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, it glows (circuit closed).

items.prompt_en: Predict: in a single loop, if the switch is moved from before the bulb to after the bulb, will it still turn the bulb on and off?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: ek single loop mein agar switch ko bulb se pehle wali jagah se hata ke bulb ke baad laga dein, toh kya wo phir bhi bulb ko on-off karega?
items.answer: Yes. A break anywhere in a single loop stops the current everywhere in it.
hints: Ask what happens to a bicycle chain broken at any link
Point to the loop having only one path
Prompt: a break ___ in the loop stops current ___
Assert: yes; a switch works anywhere in a single loop

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, a switch works anywhere in a single loop.

items.prompt_en: A circuit diagram shows a battery of two cells joined + to −, a bulb and a closed switch. If the battery is replaced by just one cell, predict what changes.
items.prompt_hi: Ek circuit diagram mein do cell ki battery (+ se −), ek bulb aur band switch hai. Agar battery ki jagah sirf ek cell laga dein, toh guess karo kya badlega?
items.answer: The bulb still glows, but more dimly, because one cell pushes a smaller current than two.
hints: Ask what the second cell was adding
Point to the push from each cell
Prompt: with one cell the current is ___ so the bulb is ___
Assert: it glows more dimly with one cell

verified.solverAnswer: Bulb glows more dimly with one cell.

items.prompt_en: Why do we say a switch 'controls' a circuit but is not a 'source' of electricity?
items.prompt_hi: Hum kyon kehte hain ki switch circuit ko 'control' karta hai par bijli ka 'source' nahi hai?
items.answer: Because the cell provides the energy that drives the current; the switch only opens or closes the path, deciding whether current can flow.
acceptable: switch sirf rasta kholta-band karta hai
hints: Ask what happens when you press a switch with no cell in the circuit
Point to the cell as the energy supplier
Prompt: the ___ supplies energy; the switch only ___ the path
Assert: the switch controls the path; the cell is the source

verified.solverAnswer: The cell supplies energy; the switch only opens or closes the path.

items.prompt_en: Two circuit diagrams each have a cell and a bulb. In diagram A the switch symbol shows a gap; in diagram B it shows no gap. In which will the bulb glow, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Do circuit diagram mein cell aur bulb hain. Diagram A mein switch symbol mein gap hai; diagram B mein gap nahi hai. Kismein bulb jalega, aur kyon?
items.answer: In B, because the closed switch completes the circuit; in A the switch is open, so the circuit is broken.
hints: Ask what the gap means for the current
Point to the switch symbol in each
Prompt: the switch in ___ is closed, so its circuit is ___
Assert: B glows; A's open switch breaks the circuit

verified.solverAnswer: B glows (no gap = closed circuit); A has an open switch, circuit broken.

items.prompt_en: Turn this description into a circuit diagram: 'A battery of three cells, a switch and two bulbs, all in one loop.' Then say what each symbol in your drawing looks like.
items.prompt_hi: Is description ko circuit diagram mein badlo: 'Teen cell ki battery, ek switch aur do bulb, sab ek hi loop mein.' Phir batao tumhare drawing ka har symbol kaisa dikhta hai.
items.answer: Three cell symbols in a row, with the long line of each next to the short line of the next; a switch symbol; two bulb symbols (circles with crosses); all joined by straight lines into one closed loop.
hints: Invite them to draw the battery first
Point to joining long line to short line between cells
Prompt: three cells joined ___ to ___, then switch, two bulbs, back to the battery
Assert: one loop with a three-cell battery, a switch and two bulb symbols

verified.solverAnswer: Draw one loop: three cell symbols in series (long line of one next to short line of next), switch, two bulb symbols (circle with cross), back to battery.

items.prompt_en: In your room, a switch on the switchboard controls the fan. Where is the circuit, and what does the switch do when you turn it OFF?
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare kamre mein switchboard ka ek switch pankha chalata hai. Circuit kahaan hai, aur switch OFF karne pe wo kya karta hai?
items.answer: Wires inside the walls connect the supply to the fan and back, forming a circuit; turning the switch OFF opens the circuit, so current stops and the fan stops. (Never open a switchboard yourself.)
hints: Ask where the fan's wires go
Point to wires hidden inside the walls
Prompt: OFF ___ the circuit, so current ___
Assert: OFF breaks the loop through the fan; never open a switchboard

verified.solverAnswer: Circuit runs through wires in wall to the fan; OFF opens the circuit so no current flows. (Don't open switchboards.)

items.prompt_en: A refrigerator's light turns on when you open the door and off when you close it. What device is hidden there, and how does it work?
items.prompt_hi: Fridge ki light darwaza kholne pe jalti hai aur band karne pe bujh jaati hai. Wahaan kaunsa device chhupa hai, aur wo kaise kaam karta hai?
items.answer: A small push switch. When the door is closed it presses the switch and opens (breaks) the light's circuit; when the door opens, the switch is released and the circuit closes, so the light glows.
hints: Ask what must happen to the circuit when the door opens
Point to a small button near the door's edge
Prompt: the door presses a ___ that ___ the circuit
Assert: a door-pressed switch opens the circuit when shut and closes it when open

verified.solverAnswer: A push-button/door switch; door closed presses it, circuit open and light off; door open releases it, circuit closes, light on.

items.prompt_en: Kiran drew a cell with the short thick line labelled '+' and the long thin line labelled '−'. What is the mistake?
items.prompt_hi: Kiran ne cell ka symbol banaya jismein chhoti moti line pe '+' aur lambi patli line pe '−' likha. Galti kya hai?
items.answer: The labels are swapped: the long thin line is positive and the short thick line is negative.
hints: Ask which end of a real cell has the cap
Point to the long line matching the cap
Prompt: the ___ line is positive
Assert: long thin line is positive; Kiran swapped the labels

verified.solverAnswer: Reversed: the long thin line is positive, short thick is negative.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend why scientists use circuit diagrams with symbols instead of drawing real-looking pictures of cells and bulbs.
items.prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao ki scientists cell aur bulb ki asli jaisi picture banaane ki bajaye symbols wale circuit diagram kyon use karte hain.
items.answer: Symbols are quick to draw, simple and standard everywhere, so anyone can read the diagram and build exactly the same circuit.
hints: Invite them to compare drawing a real bulb with drawing its symbol
Point to electricians in different cities reading the same diagram
Prompt: symbols are ___, simple and ___ for everyone
Assert: standard symbols let anyone read and build the same circuit

verified.solverAnswer: Symbols are quick to draw, simple, and standard so anyone anywhere can read and build the circuit.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what does the longer line in a cell symbol stand for?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: cell ke symbol mein lambi line kis cheez ko dikhati hai?
items.answer: The positive terminal.
hints: Ask which end of a real cell has the cap
Point to long matching the cap
Prompt: the long line is the ___ terminal
Assert: the longer line is positive

verified.solverAnswer: The positive terminal.

workedExample.problem: Draw the circuit diagram of a torch that has two cells, a switch and a bulb, with the torch switched on.
steps: Draw two cell symbols side by side, with the long line of the first next to the short line of the second (positive to negative)
From the free positive end of the battery, draw a wire to a switch symbol
From the switch, draw a wire to a bulb symbol
From the bulb, draw a wire back to the free negative end of the battery, closing the loop
Draw the switch closed, because the torch is on
fadedVersion: Draw two cell symbols joined ___ to negative
From the free positive end, draw a wire to a ___ symbol
From the switch, draw a wire to a ___ symbol
From the bulb, draw a wire back to the free ___ end, closing the loop
Draw the switch ___, because the torch is on

skills.title: Test materials with a simple tester (a cell, a bulb and wires with a gap) and classify them as conductors or insulators
Recall that metals are good conductors; rubber, plastic, wood, glass, paper and dry cloth are insulators; graphite is a non-metal that conducts
Explain the uses of conductors and insulators: copper or aluminium wires covered in plastic, insulated tool handles, rubber gloves
Explain that tap water, salt water and the human body can conduct, so electrical things must never be touched with wet hands

expectations: A conductor lets electric current pass through it easily; an insulator does not let current pass (or hardly at all).
A simple tester made of a cell, a bulb and two wires with a gap shows this: if the bulb glows when a material bridges the gap, the material is a conductor.
Metals such as copper, aluminium and iron are good conductors; plastic, rubber, wood, glass, paper and dry cloth are insulators; graphite (pencil lead) is a non-metal that conducts.
Electric wires are made of copper or aluminium (conductors) covered with plastic (an insulator), so current flows only where we want and we stay safe.
Tap water, salty water and the human body can conduct electricity, especially at the high voltage of the mains, so switches and appliances must never be touched with wet hands.
A torch-bulb tester may not glow with tap water because the current is too small to light it, but that does not mean water is safe with mains electricity.

misconceptions.belief: Water and the human body never conduct electricity.
signs: Thinks touching a switch with wet hands is harmless
Says our body is like rubber

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why must you never touch a switch with wet hands?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Geele haathon se switch kabhi kyon nahi chhoona chahiye?

options.text: There is no real reason; water does not conduct electricity
Water on the skin can let current pass through your body, giving a dangerous shock
Wet hands only make the switch rusty

remediation.representation: An LED tester glowing in salt water, next to a picture of a wet hand on a switch with a warning sign
remediation.moveShape: Show the LED in salt water first, then ask what that means for wet skin at 230 volts

misconceptions.belief: If tap water does not light the torch-bulb tester, water must be a perfect insulator and safe near the mains.
signs: Uses one 'no glow' result to say water is safe
Thinks a tester shows all-or-nothing

diagnostic.prompt_en: In a torch-bulb tester, the bulb did not glow when its wires were dipped in tap water. What is the right conclusion?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Torch-bulb tester ke taar nal ke paani mein daale toh bulb nahi jala. Sahi nateeja kya hai?

options.text: Tap water is a perfect insulator, so it is safe near mains electricity
Tap water conducts only a little, too little to light this bulb, but it can carry dangerous current from the mains
The tester must be broken

remediation.representation: Side-by-side testers: torch bulb (dark) and LED (faint glow) in the same tap water
remediation.moveShape: Contrast 'too small to see' with 'none'; ask what a much bigger push (230 volts) would do

misconceptions.belief: Only metals can conduct electricity.
signs: Predicts pencil lead will not light the tester
Says every non-metal is an insulator

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which of these will make the tester glow?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Inmein se kaun tester ko jalaayega?

options.text: Only metal objects, never a non-metal
An iron nail, and also pencil lead (graphite), which is a non-metal
A rubber eraser

remediation.representation: Tester demo with a mechanical-pencil lead between the wires, LED glowing
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to predict first, then sort graphite into the right box after seeing it

items.prompt_en: Sort these into conductors and insulators: steel spoon, plastic scale, iron key, rubber band, aluminium foil, wooden ice-cream stick.
items.prompt_hi: Inhe conductor aur insulator mein baanto: steel ka chammach, plastic ka scale, lohe ki chaabi, rubber band, aluminium foil, lakdi ki ice-cream stick.
items.answer: Conductors: steel spoon, iron key, aluminium foil. Insulators: plastic scale, rubber band, wooden ice-cream stick.
hints: Ask which of these are metals
Point to what the shiny ones have in common
Prompt: the ___ ones are conductors; plastic, rubber and wood are ___
Assert: metals conduct; plastic, rubber and wood are insulators

verified.solverAnswer: Conductors: steel spoon, iron key, aluminium foil. Insulators: plastic scale, rubber band, wooden ice-cream stick.

items.prompt_en: How does a tester made of a cell, a bulb and two wires with a gap tell you whether a material is a conductor?
items.prompt_hi: Cell, bulb aur gap wale do taar se bana tester kaise batata hai ki koi material conductor hai?
items.answer: Touch the two free wire ends to the material: if the bulb glows, current passes through the material and closes the circuit, so it is a conductor; if not, it is an insulator.
hints: Ask what the gap does to the circuit
Point to the material filling the gap
Prompt: if the bulb glows, the material ___ the circuit and is a ___
Assert: glowing bulb means the material conducts and closes the gap

verified.solverAnswer: Put the material in the gap between the wires; if the bulb glows the material completes the circuit, so it is a conductor; no glow means insulator.

items.prompt_en: Predict, then check with your cell-and-bulb tester: will a steel hairpin make the bulb glow? A plastic button? A one-rupee coin?
items.prompt_hi: Pehle guess karo, phir apne cell-bulb tester se check karo: kya steel ka hairpin bulb jalaayega? Plastic ka button? Ek rupaye ka sikka?
items.answer: The hairpin and the coin make it glow because they are metals; the plastic button does not, because plastic is an insulator.
acceptable: hairpin and coin yes, button no
hints: Ask for a guess for each before testing
Point to which ones are metal
Prompt: the ___ ones conduct; plastic does ___
Assert: hairpin and coin conduct; the plastic button does not

verified.solverAnswer: Hairpin and coin glow (metals conduct); plastic button does not.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if you touch the tester's two wire ends to the two ends of a lead from a mechanical pencil, will the bulb glow?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar tester ke dono taar ke sire mechanical pencil ki lead ke dono siron se chhuaao, toh kya bulb jalega?
items.answer: Yes, it conducts: graphite is a non-metal that conducts electricity. The bulb may glow dimly; an LED tester shows it more clearly.
hints: Ask what pencil lead is really made of
Point to graphite being a special non-metal
Prompt: graphite is a ___ that ___ electricity
Assert: yes; graphite is a non-metal conductor

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, bulb glows; graphite is a non-metal that conducts (may be dim).

items.prompt_en: Your tester uses an LED instead of a torch bulb, because an LED lights up with a much smaller current. Dip its two wire ends in a glass of tap water, not touching each other. Predict what happens. Then predict what happens after you stir in two spoons of salt.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare tester mein torch bulb ki jagah LED hai, kyonki LED bahut kam current mein bhi jal jaata hai. Iske dono taar nal ke paani ke glass mein daalo, ek doosre ko chhue bina. Guess karo kya hoga. Phir do chammach namak ghol ke guess karo kya hoga.
items.answer: In tap water the LED stays dark or glows very faintly; after salt is dissolved it glows clearly, because salt water conducts much better. Either way, water can conduct, which is why water and mains electricity are dangerous together.
hints: Ask what dissolved salt adds to the water
Point to the difference between tap water and salt water
Prompt: salt water ___ better than tap water
Assert: faint or none in tap water, clear glow in salt water; water can conduct

verified.solverAnswer: In tap water, LED glows faintly or not at all (very little conduction); after salt, LED glows clearly because salt water conducts better.

items.prompt_en: Why are electric wires made of copper inside and covered with plastic outside?
items.prompt_hi: Bijli ke taar andar se copper ke aur bahar se plastic se dhake kyon hote hain?
items.answer: Copper is a good conductor and carries current easily; plastic is an insulator that keeps the current inside the wire and protects us from shocks.
hints: Ask what job each layer does
Point to the plastic as the part we touch
Prompt: copper ___ the current; plastic ___ us
Assert: copper conducts; plastic insulates and keeps us safe

verified.solverAnswer: Copper conducts current well; plastic is an insulator that keeps current in and protects us from shock.

items.prompt_en: Why do electricians wear rubber gloves and rubber-soled shoes while working?
items.prompt_hi: Electrician kaam karte waqt rubber ke gloves aur rubber sole wale joote kyon pehente hain?
items.answer: Rubber is an insulator; it blocks current from passing through their body to the ground, protecting them from electric shock.
hints: Ask what rubber does to electric current
Point to the path from the hand through the body to the ground
Prompt: rubber is an ___ that stops current passing through the ___
Assert: rubber insulates and protects electricians from shock

verified.solverAnswer: Rubber is an insulator; stops current passing through their body to the ground, preventing shock.

items.prompt_en: Two screwdrivers: one with a plastic handle, one made all of metal. Which is safer for an electrician, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Do screwdriver: ek plastic handle wala, ek poora metal ka. Electrician ke liye kaunsa zyada safe hai, aur kyon?
items.answer: The one with the plastic handle, because plastic is an insulator and stops current from reaching the hand; an all-metal one would conduct it.
hints: Ask what the hand touches on each tool
Point to which material conducts
Prompt: the plastic handle is an ___
Assert: the plastic-handled one, because the handle insulates the hand

verified.solverAnswer: Plastic-handled one; handle is insulator, protecting the hand from shock.

items.prompt_en: During a storm, an electric wire has fallen on a wet road near your school. Why should you stay far away and tell an adult, even if it looks harmless?
items.prompt_hi: Toofan ke dauraan school ke paas geeli sadak pe bijli ka taar gir gaya hai. Wo bekaar dikhe phir bhi tumhe door kyon rehna chahiye aur kisi bade ko kyon batana chahiye?
items.answer: The wire may still be live; current can pass through wet ground and water and through your body, giving a deadly shock. Keep away and tell an adult, who can call the electricity department.
hints: Ask whether you can see if a wire is live
Point to the wet road conducting
Prompt: the wire may be ___ and wet ground can ___
Assert: stay away; a live wire on a wet road can kill; tell an adult

verified.solverAnswer: A fallen wire may be live and you can't tell; wet ground conducts and can carry current to you, risking fatal shock; tell an adult.

items.prompt_en: Cooking pans in Indian kitchens have metal bodies but often wooden or plastic handles. Is this the same idea as electric wires? Explain.
items.prompt_hi: Indian kitchen ke bartan metal ke hote hain par handle aksar lakdi ya plastic ke. Kya ye bijli ke taar wala hi idea hai? Samjhao.
items.answer: It is a similar idea, but for heat: metal conducts heat well to cook the food, while wood and plastic are poor conductors of heat, so the handle stays cool. Many good conductors of electricity, like metals, are also good conductors of heat.
acceptable: wood and plastic don't conduct heat
hints: Ask what flows from the flame into the pan
Point to the handle staying cool
Prompt: metal ___ heat; wood and plastic are ___ conductors of heat
Assert: same idea for heat: metal body conducts, handle insulates

verified.solverAnswer: Similar idea but for heat: metal conducts heat to food; wood/plastic handles are poor conductors (insulators) so the handle stays cool.

items.prompt_en: Sameer tested tap water with a torch-bulb tester, saw no glow, and wrote: 'Water is an insulator, so it's fine to use a hair dryer in the bathroom with wet hands.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Sameer ne nal ke paani ko torch-bulb tester se test kiya, bulb nahi jala, aur likha: 'Paani insulator hai, toh geele haathon se bathroom mein hair dryer chalaana theek hai.' Kya galat hai?
items.answer: Tap water conducts weakly: too little current for a torch bulb with one cell, but mains voltage can push a dangerous current through water and wet skin. Never use electrical appliances with wet hands.
hints: Ask how strong the cell's push is compared with the mains
Point to the LED that glowed faintly
Prompt: tap water conducts ___; mains can push a ___ current
Assert: water does conduct; wet hands and appliances are dangerous

verified.solverAnswer: Water (tap water has dissolved salts) conducts; a weak cell can't light bulb but mains can drive dangerous current; wet hands + appliance in bathroom is dangerous.

items.prompt_en: Make a two-column chart from these test results, 'bulb glowed' and 'bulb did not glow': iron nail, rubber eraser, aluminium foil, glass bangle, steel spoon, paper, pencil lead. Then label the columns with the right science words.
items.prompt_hi: In test results se do column ka chart banao, 'bulb jala' aur 'bulb nahi jala': lohe ki keel, rubber eraser, aluminium foil, kaanch ki choodi, steel ka chammach, kaagaz, pencil lead. Phir columns pe sahi science ke shabd likho.
items.answer: Bulb glowed (conductors): iron nail, aluminium foil, steel spoon, pencil lead. Bulb did not glow (insulators): rubber eraser, glass bangle, paper.
hints: Invite them to place the metals first
Point to pencil lead as the surprise
Prompt: the glowed column is ___; the other is ___
Assert: conductors are the nail, foil, spoon and pencil lead; insulators are the eraser, bangle and paper

verified.solverAnswer: Glowed (conductors): iron nail, aluminium foil, steel spoon, pencil lead. Did not glow (insulators): rubber eraser, glass bangle, paper.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your grandmother why she should dry her hands before switching on the mixer-grinder.
items.prompt_hi: Apni daadi ya naani ko samjhao ki mixer-grinder ka switch on karne se pehle haath kyon sukhaane chahiye.
items.answer: Water on the hands can conduct electricity, so if current leaks it could pass through the wet skin and body and give a shock; dry hands and the switch's plastic cover keep her safe.
hints: Invite them to start with what water can do
Point to the switch and the wet hand
Prompt: water can ___ electricity, so current could pass through her ___
Assert: water conducts; dry hands prevent shocks

verified.solverAnswer: Water (with dissolved salts) conducts electricity; wet hands can let current pass through her body giving a shock; dry hands are safer.

items.prompt_en: From last time: name one non-metal that conducts electricity.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek aisi non-metal ka naam batao jo bijli conduct karti hai.
items.answer: Graphite (pencil lead).
hints: Ask what is inside a pencil
Point to the tester test with pencil lead
Prompt: the non-metal in pencil lead is ___
Assert: graphite conducts electricity

verified.solverAnswer: Graphite (in pencil lead).
verified.note: HINT LEAK: hint 1-2 ('what is inside a pencil', 'pencil lead') give the answer away before any prompt.

steps: Join wire 1 from the cell's + terminal to one terminal of the bulb
Join wire 2 to the bulb's other terminal, leaving its other end free

Join wire 2 to the bulb's other terminal, leaving its other end ___
Join wire 3 to the cell's ___ terminal; the two free ends make a ___
Touch the two free ends to the two ends of the ___
The bulb glows, so the hairpin is a ___

skills.title: Describe properties of metals: lustre, hardness, malleability, ductility, sonority, and conduction of heat and electricity
Describe properties of non-metals: dull, brittle, not sonorous, poor conductors

Recognise exceptions: mercury (liquid metal), sodium and potassium (soft metals), graphite (conducting non-metal), iodine (lustrous non-metal), diamond (very hard form of carbon); and that magnets attract only some metals
Use properties to explain everyday uses: bells, wires, foil, silver varq, cooking vessels

expectations: Metals are usually shiny (lustrous), hard, malleable (can be beaten into thin sheets), ductile (can be drawn into wires), sonorous (ring when struck) and good conductors of heat and electricity.
Non-metals are usually dull, brittle (break or crumble when hit or bent), not sonorous and poor conductors of heat and electricity.

There are exceptions: mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature; sodium and potassium are metals soft enough to cut with a knife; graphite is a non-metal that conducts electricity; iodine is a shiny non-metal; diamond, a form of carbon, is extremely hard.
Uses follow from properties: copper and aluminium wires (ductile, good conductors), aluminium foil and silver varq (malleable), temple bells (sonorous), cooking vessels (good conductors of heat).
A magnet does not attract all metals; it attracts iron, nickel, cobalt and things made with them, like steel nails.

misconceptions.belief: All metals are hard solids.
signs: Says mercury cannot be a metal because it is a liquid
Thinks every metal is as hard as iron

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which statement is true?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsi baat sahi hai?

options.text: Every metal is a hard solid
Mercury, once used in thermometers, is a metal that is liquid at room temperature
Mercury must be a non-metal because it is a liquid

remediation.representation: An exceptions card set: mercury droplets, a soft sodium block in kerosene, graphite, iodine crystals, diamond
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to sort each card using properties first, then reveal its real class and discuss the surprise

misconceptions.belief: Magnets attract all metals.
signs: Predicts that a magnet will pick up aluminium foil or copper wire
Uses 'sticks to a magnet' as the test for a metal

diagnostic.prompt_en: A magnet is brought near an iron nail, a ball of aluminium foil and a copper wire. Which will it attract?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek magnet ko lohe ki keel, aluminium foil ki goli aur copper ke taar ke paas laaya gaya. Wo kisko kheenchega?

options.text: All three, because all metals stick to magnets
Only the iron nail
None, because magnets only attract other magnets

remediation.representation: A magnet-test tray: iron nail, brass key, aluminium foil, copper wire, all shiny metals
remediation.moveShape: Have the child predict each, then test; conclude that 'metal' and 'magnetic' are different questions

misconceptions.belief: Anything shiny is a metal, and all non-metals are dull.
signs: Calls iodine crystals or a polished stone a metal
Uses shine as the only test

diagnostic.prompt_en: Iodine crystals are shiny and dark purple-grey. Is iodine a metal?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Iodine ke crystals chamakdaar aur gehre baingani-grey hote hain. Kya iodine ek metal hai?

options.text: Yes, because it is shiny
No, iodine is a non-metal even though it is lustrous; it is brittle and does not conduct well
Yes, all crystals are metals

remediation.representation: A property checklist where shine is only one tick among five (ring, bend, conduct heat, conduct electricity)
remediation.moveShape: Score iodine on all five ticks with the child and decide by the total, not by one tick

items.prompt_en: Which property of metals lets aluminium be made into thin foil for wrapping rotis?
items.prompt_hi: Metals ki kaunsi property ki wajah se aluminium ko roti lapetne wali patli foil mein banaya ja sakta hai?
items.answer: Malleability: metals can be beaten or pressed into thin sheets.
hints: Ask how the foil got so thin
Point to beating or rolling metal flat
Prompt: the property of being beaten into sheets is ___
Assert: malleability lets aluminium become thin foil

verified.solverAnswer: Malleability.

items.prompt_en: Which property lets copper be drawn into thin wires, and which property makes a temple bell ring?
items.prompt_hi: Kaunsi property ki wajah se copper ko patle taar mein kheencha ja sakta hai, aur kaunsi property mandir ki ghanti ko bajaati hai?
items.answer: Ductility lets copper be drawn into wires; sonority makes a metal bell ring.
hints: Ask what happens when you strike a steel plate
Point to wires being pulled long and thin
Prompt: drawn into wires is ___; ringing is ___
Assert: ductility for wires, sonority for bells

verified.solverAnswer: Ductility for wires; sonority for bell ringing.

items.prompt_en: Gently tap a steel glass, then a wooden block and a plastic box, with a steel spoon. Predict which will ring.
items.prompt_hi: Ek steel ke glass, phir ek lakdi ke tukde aur plastic ke dibbe ko steel ke chammach se halke se thapthapaao. Guess karo kaun bajega, yaani kaun ki aawaaz goonjegi?
items.answer: The steel glass rings because metals are sonorous; the wooden block and plastic box give only a dull thud.
hints: Ask for a guess before tapping
Point to the temple bell
Prompt: ___ objects ring because they are sonorous
Assert: only the steel glass rings; wood and plastic thud

verified.solverAnswer: Only the steel glass rings (sonorous metal); wood and plastic make dull thud.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if you bring a fridge magnet near an iron nail, a ball of aluminium foil, a copper wire and a brass key, which ones will it pull?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar fridge wala magnet lohe ki keel, aluminium foil ki goli, copper ke taar aur peetal ki chaabi ke paas laao, toh wo kis-kisko kheenchega?
items.answer: Only the iron nail. Aluminium, copper and brass are metals too, but magnets attract only iron, nickel, cobalt and things made with them.
hints: Ask for a guess for each object
Point to the fact that all four are metals
Prompt: magnets attract ___, nickel and cobalt, not all metals
Assert: only the iron nail is pulled

verified.solverAnswer: Only the iron nail.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if you gently bend a piece of pencil lead (graphite) and a piece of aluminium wire, which one bends and which one snaps?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar pencil ki lead (graphite) ka tukda aur aluminium ke taar ka tukda halke se modo, toh kaun mud jaayega aur kaun toot jaayega?
items.answer: The aluminium wire bends because metals are ductile and malleable; the graphite snaps because non-metals are brittle.
hints: Ask which is a metal and which is a non-metal
Point to brittleness of non-metals
Prompt: the ___ bends; the ___ snaps
Assert: metal wire bends; brittle graphite snaps

verified.solverAnswer: Aluminium wire bends; graphite is brittle and snaps.

items.prompt_en: Why are cooking vessels like a kadhai or pateela usually made of iron, steel or aluminium?
items.prompt_hi: Kadhai ya pateela jaise khaana banane ke bartan aksar lohe, steel ya aluminium ke kyon bante hain?
items.answer: Metals are good conductors of heat, so heat passes quickly from the flame to the food; they are also strong and can be shaped because they are malleable.
hints: Ask what must travel from the flame to the food
Point to metals passing heat quickly
Prompt: metals are good ___ of heat
Assert: metal vessels conduct heat well to cook food

verified.solverAnswer: Metals are good conductors of heat (and strong, high melting point).

items.prompt_en: Compare graphite and diamond. Both are made only of carbon. How are they different, and which one conducts electricity?
items.prompt_hi: Graphite aur diamond ki tulna karo. Dono sirf carbon se bane hain. Ye alag kaise hain, aur inmein se kaun bijli conduct karta hai?
items.answer: Graphite is soft, dark grey and slippery and conducts electricity (it is used in pencils); diamond is extremely hard and transparent and does not conduct electricity.
hints: Ask which one can leave a mark on paper
Point to diamond cutting glass
Prompt: ___ is soft and conducts; ___ is very hard and does not
Assert: soft conducting graphite, very hard non-conducting diamond

verified.solverAnswer: Graphite soft, grey, slippery, conducts electricity; diamond very hard, transparent, does not conduct. Same carbon, different arrangement.

items.prompt_en: Silver varq on mithai is a sheet thinner than paper. Which property of silver makes this possible?
items.prompt_hi: Mithai pe lagne wala chaandi ka varq kaagaz se bhi patla hota hai. Chaandi ki kaunsi property se ye mumkin hai?
items.answer: Malleability: silver can be beaten into extremely thin sheets.
hints: Ask how varq makers make it so thin
Point to beating the silver between sheets
Prompt: silver is very ___
Assert: malleability lets silver become varq

verified.solverAnswer: Malleability.

items.prompt_en: You must choose a material for the bells on a dancer's ghungroo. Would you pick plastic or brass? Explain using properties.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhe ek dancer ke ghungroo ki ghantiyon ke liye material chunna hai. Plastic chunoge ya peetal? Properties use karke samjhao.
items.answer: Brass, a metal alloy, because metals are sonorous and make a ringing sound when struck; plastic would only click dully.
hints: Ask which sound a ghungroo needs
Point to temple bells made of metal
Prompt: brass is a metal, so it is ___
Assert: brass, because sonorous metals ring

verified.solverAnswer: Brass; metals are sonorous and ring when struck, plastic does not.

items.prompt_en: Ritu writes: 'All metals are hard and solid, and none can be cut with a knife.' Correct her.
items.prompt_hi: Ritu likhti hai: 'Saare metals sakht aur thos hote hain, aur kisi ko chaaku se nahi kaat sakte.' Use sahi karo.
items.answer: Mercury is a metal that is liquid at room temperature, and sodium and potassium are metals soft enough to be cut with a knife (they react with air and water, so they are kept under kerosene and never handled at home).
hints: Ask what was inside old thermometers
Point to sodium kept in kerosene in labs
Prompt: ___ is a liquid metal; ___ is a soft metal
Assert: mercury is liquid; sodium and potassium are soft

verified.solverAnswer: Not all metals are hard solids: mercury is liquid at room temperature; sodium and potassium are soft and can be cut with a knife.

items.prompt_en: Make a table with rows for lustre, malleability, ductility, sonority and conduction, and columns for copper and sulphur. Fill it in and say what pattern you see.
items.prompt_hi: Ek table banao jismein rows ho chamak, malleability, ductility, sonority aur conduction, aur columns ho copper aur sulphur. Bharo aur batao kya pattern dikhta hai.
items.answer: Copper: lustrous, malleable, ductile, sonorous, good conductor. Sulphur: dull yellow, brittle, not ductile, not sonorous, poor conductor. Pattern: metals and non-metals have opposite properties.
hints: Invite them to fill the copper column first
Point to sulphur being a yellow powder that crumbles
Prompt: copper has ___ properties; sulphur has the ___
Assert: copper ticks every metal property; sulphur shows the opposite

verified.solverAnswer: Copper: lustrous, malleable, ductile, sonorous, conducts. Sulphur: dull, brittle, not ductile, not sonorous, does not conduct. Metals show all the properties; non-metals mostly the opposite.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend how you could tell whether an unknown shiny solid is a metal, using three safe tests. Why is shine alone not enough?
items.prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao ki kisi anjaan chamakdaar thos cheez ko metal hai ya nahi, teen safe tests se kaise pata karoge. Sirf chamak kaafi kyon nahi hai?
items.answer: Tap it to hear if it rings (sonority); try bending a thin piece to see if it bends or crumbles (malleable or brittle); put it in a cell-and-bulb tester to see if it conducts. Shine is not enough because some non-metals, like iodine, are shiny too.
hints: Invite them to list the tests one by one
Point to iodine as the shiny trap
Prompt: tap it, bend it, and test it in a ___
Assert: use several properties; shine alone can fool you

verified.solverAnswer: Tap it for ringing, bend/hammer it to see if it bends or crumbles, test in a circuit for conduction. Shine alone isn't enough: some non-metals like iodine are shiny.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what is ductility? Give one example.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ductility kya hai? Ek example do.
items.answer: Ductility is the property of being drawn into thin wires, for example copper or aluminium wires.
hints: Ask what electric wires are made from
Point to stretching metal into a wire
Prompt: ductility means being drawn into ___
Assert: ductility is being drawn into wires, like copper wire

verified.solverAnswer: Ductility is the ability to be drawn into wires; e.g. copper wire.

workedExample.problem: Decide whether an unknown grey rod is a metal or a non-metal.
steps: Look: does it shine when its surface is rubbed clean?
Tap it gently: does it ring?
Try to bend it gently: does it bend or snap?
Put it in a cell-and-bulb tester: does the bulb glow?
If most answers match metal properties, it is a metal; one test alone, like shine, is not enough
fadedVersion: Look: does it ___ when rubbed clean?
Tap it gently: does it ___?
Try to bend it: does it bend or ___?
Put it in a cell-and-bulb ___: does the bulb glow?
If most answers match ___ properties, it is a metal

skills.title: Describe rust as a new reddish-brown, flaky substance formed when iron reacts with oxygen and water
Show with a fair test that both air (oxygen) and water (moisture) are needed for rusting
Describe ways to prevent rusting: painting, oiling or greasing, galvanising with zinc, chromium plating, making stainless steel, keeping dry
Describe how air and moisture affect other metals: copper turns green, silver turns black, gold stays shiny

expectations: Rust is a new substance (an iron oxide, reddish-brown and flaky) formed when iron reacts with oxygen from the air and water (moisture); rusting is a chemical change.
Both oxygen and water are needed: iron kept in dry air, or in water with no air, hardly rusts.
Rusting is faster in humid and coastal places (salty air) and during the monsoon.
Rust flakes off, exposing fresh iron underneath, so the iron is slowly eaten away and becomes weak.
Rusting is prevented by keeping air and water away from iron: paint, oil or grease, a coating of zinc (galvanising) or chromium, or by making stainless steel.
Other metals react too: copper gets a green coating, silver turns black (tarnishes), while gold stays shiny.

misconceptions.belief: Rust is just dirt on iron.
signs: Says rust can be washed off with soap to get the same iron back
Calls rust 'mud' or 'dust' stuck on the gate

diagnostic.prompt_en: Can you wash the rust off an old iron gate with soap and water and get all the original iron back?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kya purane lohe ke gate ka jung sabun-paani se dho ke saara original loha waapas mil sakta hai?

options.text: Yes, rust is just dirt stuck on the iron
No, rust is a new substance made from the iron itself; the iron underneath has become thinner
Yes, rust is only old paint that changed colour

remediation.representation: A cut-away picture of a rusted rod: thinner iron core, flaky rust layer that used to be iron
remediation.moveShape: Weigh-and-compare story: scrape the rust off a nail and show it is thinner than a new nail

misconceptions.belief: Iron rusts with only water, or with only air; both are not needed.
signs: Says a nail in a dry box will rust because air has oxygen
Says iron underwater with no air will rust fastest

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which iron nail is most likely to rust in a week?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Kaunsi lohe ki keel ek hafte mein sabse zyada jung khaayegi?

options.text: A nail in a dry, closed plastic box (air but no water)
A nail half-dipped in water in an open cup (air and water)
A nail in boiled water sealed with a layer of oil (water but no air)

remediation.representation: Three-cup picture with an 'air' tick and a 'water' tick on each cup
remediation.moveShape: Have the child tick each cup and predict; only the cup with both ticks rusts

misconceptions.belief: When iron rusts, it gets lighter because the iron is destroyed.
signs: Predicts a rusted nail plus its rust weighs less
Says the iron 'disappears' into rust

diagnostic.prompt_en: An iron nail is weighed, left to rust while keeping all its rust, and weighed again. What happens to its mass?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek lohe ki keel ko tola gaya, phir use jung lagne diya aur saara jung sambhaal ke rakha, phir dobara tola. Uske wazan ka kya hua?

options.text: It becomes lighter because iron is destroyed
It becomes heavier because oxygen and water from the air have joined with the iron
It stays exactly the same

remediation.representation: A balance animation: nail on one side, slowly tipping heavier as tiny oxygen and water particles join it
remediation.moveShape: Ask where the extra mass could come from if nothing was added by hand

misconceptions.belief: All metals rust in the same way as iron.
signs: Says copper and silver also get reddish-brown rust
Expects gold jewellery to rust

diagnostic.prompt_en: Which statement about metals left in damp air is true?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Nam hawa mein rakhe metals ke baare mein kaunsi baat sahi hai?

options.text: Copper, silver and gold all get reddish-brown rust
Only iron and steel rust; copper turns green, silver turns black and gold stays shiny
No metal ever changes in air

remediation.representation: A photo gallery: rusty iron gate, green copper lota, blackened silver payal, shiny old gold coin
remediation.moveShape: Let the child match each metal to its look and name the change

items.prompt_en: Which two things from the surroundings does iron need in order to rust?
items.prompt_hi: Lohe ko jung lagne ke liye aas-paas ki kaunsi do cheezon ki zaroorat hoti hai?
items.answer: Oxygen (from the air) and water (moisture).
hints: Ask when bicycles rust the most
Point to air all around and water in the monsoon
Prompt: rusting needs ___ and ___
Assert: iron needs both oxygen and water to rust

verified.solverAnswer: Oxygen (air) and water (moisture).
verified.note: HINT LEAK (mild): hint 2 names both answer parts (air, water).

items.prompt_en: Name three ways to stop an iron gate from rusting.
items.prompt_hi: Lohe ke gate ko jung se bachaane ke teen tareeke batao.
items.answer: Paint it; apply oil or grease; galvanise it with a coating of zinc; keep it dry.
hints: Ask what is done to new gates before they are put up
Point to keeping air and water away
Prompt: cover it with ___, ___ or zinc
Assert: paint, oil or grease, or a zinc coating keep air and water away

verified.solverAnswer: Painting, oiling/greasing, galvanising (zinc coating), also chrome plating.

items.prompt_en: Ask an adult for three iron nails. Nail A goes into a dry, closed plastic box. Nail B goes half into water in an open cup. Nail C goes into water that an adult has boiled and cooled, with a thin layer of cooking oil poured on top. Predict which nail will rust in a week.
items.prompt_hi: Kisi bade se teen lohe ki keel maango. Keel A ko sukhe band plastic ke dibbe mein rakho. Keel B ko khule cup ke paani mein aadha daalo. Keel C ko us paani mein daalo jise kisi bade ne ubaal ke thanda kiya ho, aur upar se khaane ke tel ki patli parat daal do. Guess karo kaunsi keel ek hafte mein jung khaayegi.
items.answer: Nail B rusts the most because it has both air and water; nail A has no water and nail C has no air (boiling removed it and the oil keeps it out), so they stay almost rust-free.
acceptable: the one with air and water
hints: Ask which cups have air, and which have water
Point to nail B being the only one with both
Prompt: only nail ___ has both air and water
Assert: nail B rusts; A lacks water and C lacks air

verified.solverAnswer: Only nail B rusts (has both air and water).
verified.note: ACCURACY (minor): nail A 'dry, closed plastic box' still contains humid air; 'no water' is an idealisation (a desiccant is needed for a true dry control). Key answer B is correct.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if an iron nail rusts completely and you collect every bit of the rust, will the rust weigh more than, less than or the same as the original nail?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar ek lohe ki keel poori tarah jung kha jaaye aur tum saara jung ikattha kar lo, toh jung ka wazan original keel se zyada hoga, kam hoga ya barabar?
items.answer: More, because oxygen and water from the air have combined with the iron to make the rust.
hints: Ask what joined the iron to make rust
Point to oxygen and water coming from the air
Prompt: rust = iron + ___ + water, so it weighs ___
Assert: the rust weighs more because oxygen and water joined the iron

verified.solverAnswer: More; oxygen and water combine with iron.

items.prompt_en: Two identical iron bicycles are left outside: one in Mumbai near the sea, one in dry Jaipur. Predict which rusts faster, and why.
items.prompt_hi: Do bilkul ek jaisi lohe ki cycle bahar chhodi gayi: ek Mumbai mein samudra ke paas, ek sukhe Jaipur mein. Guess karo kaunsi jaldi jung khaayegi, aur kyon?
items.answer: The one in Mumbai, because the air near the sea is humid and salty, and moisture and salt speed up rusting.
hints: Ask which city's air has more moisture
Point to salty sea air
Prompt: humid, ___ air speeds up rusting
Assert: Mumbai's humid, salty air rusts iron faster

verified.solverAnswer: Mumbai's: humid, salty sea air speeds rusting.

items.prompt_en: Why does painting an iron grill stop it from rusting, and why does rust start again where the paint gets scratched?
items.prompt_hi: Lohe ki grill pe paint karne se jung kyon nahi lagta, aur jahaan paint chhil jaata hai wahaan phir se jung kyon lagne lagta hai?
items.answer: Paint keeps air and water away from the iron; where it is scratched, the iron is exposed to air and moisture again and starts to rust.
acceptable: paint keeps air and water away
paint hawa aur paani rokta hai
hints: Ask what the paint layer is blocking
Point to the bare iron at the scratch
Prompt: paint keeps ___ and ___ away; a scratch ___ the iron
Assert: paint blocks air and water; scratches let them reach the iron

verified.solverAnswer: Paint blocks air and water from reaching iron; scratch exposes bare iron so rust begins there.

items.prompt_en: Compare an old copper vessel and an old iron kadhai left in a damp storeroom for months. What will each look like?
items.prompt_hi: Ek purana copper ka bartan aur ek purani lohe ki kadhai mahino tak nam store room mein rakhe gaye. Dono kaise dikhenge?
items.answer: The copper vessel gets a green coating; the iron kadhai gets reddish-brown, flaky rust.
hints: Ask what colour old copper lotas turn
Point to rust being only on iron
Prompt: copper turns ___; iron gets ___-brown rust
Assert: green coating on copper, reddish-brown rust on iron

verified.solverAnswer: Copper vessel gets a green coating; iron kadhai gets reddish-brown flaky rust.

items.prompt_en: Why are iron buckets and water pipes often coated with zinc, which is called galvanising?
items.prompt_hi: Lohe ki baaltiyon aur paani ke pipe pe aksar zinc ki parat kyon chadhaayi jaati hai, jise galvanising kehte hain?
items.answer: The zinc coating keeps air and water away from the iron so it does not rust; even if scratched, the zinc still protects the iron.
acceptable: zinc keeps air and water away
hints: Ask what a bucket is always touching
Point to the zinc layer as a shield
Prompt: zinc keeps ___ and ___ off the iron
Assert: galvanising with zinc protects iron from rusting

verified.solverAnswer: Zinc coat keeps air and water off the iron (and zinc corrodes in preference), preventing rust.

items.prompt_en: Railway tracks are made of iron and steel and stay outdoors in the rain. The tops of the rails look shiny, but their sides look rusty. Why might that be?
items.prompt_hi: Railway ki patriyan lohe aur steel ki hoti hain aur baarish mein bahar padi rehti hain. Patri ka upar wala hissa chamakdaar dikhta hai, par side jung lagi dikhti hai. Aisa kyon?
items.answer: Train wheels keep rubbing the top of the rails, scraping off any rust as soon as it forms and keeping the metal shiny; the sides are not rubbed, so the rust stays there.
hints: Ask what touches the top of the rail many times a day
Point to the sides that nothing touches
Prompt: the wheels ___ the rust off the top
Assert: wheels keep rubbing rust off the top; the sides keep their rust

verified.solverAnswer: Wheels rubbing on the top scrape rust off and keep it shiny; sides untouched so rust stays.

items.prompt_en: Neha says, 'Rust is only dust that sticks to wet iron, so just wipe it off and the gate is as good as new.' What is the mistake?
items.prompt_hi: Neha kehti hai, 'Jung bas dhool hai jo geele lohe pe chipak jaati hai, toh bas poochh do aur gate naya jaisa ho jaayega.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Rust is a new substance formed from the iron itself reacting with oxygen and water; wiping it off removes some of the iron, so the gate is thinner and weaker, not as good as new.
hints: Ask where the rust came from
Point to the gate getting thinner over the years
Prompt: rust is made from the ___ itself, so wiping it leaves the gate ___
Assert: rust is iron turned into a new substance; the gate is weakened

verified.solverAnswer: Rust is a new substance formed from the iron itself, so wiping it off leaves thinner, weaker iron.

items.prompt_en: Draw the three-nail experiment as three cups, each labelled with whether it has air and whether it has water, and mark which nail rusts. Then say in one sentence what the drawing proves.
items.prompt_hi: Teen-keel wala experiment teen cup ke roop mein banao, har cup pe likho ki usmein hawa hai ya nahi aur paani hai ya nahi, aur jis keel ko jung laga use mark karo. Phir ek line mein batao drawing kya saabit karti hai.
items.answer: Cup with air but no water: no rust. Cup with water but no air: no rust. Cup with both air and water: rusty nail. It proves that iron needs both air and water to rust.
hints: Invite them to draw the three cups first
Point to the cup with both labels
Prompt: only the cup with ___ and ___ has a rusty nail
Assert: rust appears only with both air and water

verified.solverAnswer: Cup1 air and water: rusts; cup2 air only (dry): no rust; cup3 water only (boiled with oil): no rust. Proves both air and water are needed for rusting.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your cousin why his new bicycle should be wiped dry and oiled during the monsoon.
items.prompt_hi: Apne cousin ko samjhao ki monsoon mein uski nayi cycle ko poochh ke sukhaana aur tel lagaana kyon zaroori hai.
items.answer: Iron rusts when both oxygen and water reach it, and the monsoon brings lots of water and moisture; wiping removes water, and oil makes a layer that keeps air and water away, so the cycle does not rust and weaken.
hints: Invite them to start with what rust needs
Point to rain and damp air in the monsoon
Prompt: wiping removes ___, oil keeps ___ and water away
Assert: drying and oiling keep water and air off the iron

verified.solverAnswer: Water and air rust iron; wipe it dry and oil it to keep moisture off the metal.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what happens to silver anklets (payal) over time, and what happens to gold jewellery?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: chaandi ki payal ka samay ke saath kya hota hai, aur sone ke gehnon ka kya hota hai?
items.answer: Silver turns black (tarnishes); gold stays shiny.
hints: Ask what an old silver coin looks like
Point to gold that looks new after years
Prompt: silver turns ___; gold stays ___
Assert: silver tarnishes black; gold stays shiny

verified.solverAnswer: Silver tarnishes (turns black); gold stays shiny.
