items.prompt_en: Name two emotional changes that many people notice during adolescence.
items.prompt_hi: Do aise bhaavnaatmak badlav batao jo bahut log adolescence mein mehsoos karte hain.
items.answer: Any two of: quick mood changes, wanting more independence, caring more about looks, caring more about what friends think, feeling more sensitive or worried.
hints: Ask how their feelings change during a day
Point to wanting to decide things for themselves
Prompt: moods can ___ quickly, and many want more ___
Assert: mood swings and wanting independence are common

verified.solverAnswer: Mood swings, wanting independence/privacy, new feelings, being sensitive to peers.

items.prompt_en: Name three trusted people a student could talk to about worries while growing up.
items.prompt_hi: Teen aise bharosemand logon ke naam batao jinse ek student badhte waqt apni chintaon ke baare mein baat kar sakta hai.
items.answer: For example: a parent, a class teacher, a school counsellor, a doctor, an elder sibling or another trusted adult in the family.
hints: Ask who they would go to if they felt unwell
Point to people at home and at school
Prompt: a ___ at home, a ___ at school, and a doctor
Assert: parents, teachers, counsellors and doctors are trusted people

verified.solverAnswer: Parents/family elder, teacher, school counsellor, doctor.

items.prompt_en: A class puts up an anonymous question box about growing up. Predict: will most questions be very different from each other, or will many students ask similar things? What does that tell you?
items.prompt_hi: Ek class mein badhne ke baare mein bina naam ka question box rakha gaya. Guess karo: zyadatar sawaal ek doosre se bilkul alag honge, ya bahut se students milte-julte sawaal poochhenge? Isse kya pata chalta hai?
items.answer: Many students will ask similar questions. Most people share the same worries, so nobody is alone and asking is normal.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to how many people are growing up at the same time
Prompt: many students have ___ worries, so asking is ___
Assert: questions are often similar; everyone wonders about the same things

verified.solverAnswer: Many students ask similar questions; so everyone shares the same worries and it is normal to ask.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if someone keeps a worry completely to themselves for weeks, will it usually feel bigger or smaller over time? And what usually happens after they share it with a trusted adult?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar koi apni chinta hafton tak bilkul apne tak rakhe, toh samay ke saath wo aksar badi lagegi ya chhoti? Aur bharosemand bade se share karne ke baad aksar kya hota hai?
items.answer: Kept inside, a worry often feels bigger; after sharing it with a trusted adult it usually feels lighter, and together they can find a way to deal with it.
hints: Ask for a guess about both parts
Point to how talking can bring help and ideas
Prompt: hidden worries often feel ___; sharing makes them ___
Assert: keeping worries in can make them grow; sharing helps

verified.solverAnswer: It usually feels bigger; sharing with a trusted adult makes it smaller and helps find solutions.

items.prompt_en: Why is it normal to have strong or changing feelings during adolescence?
items.prompt_hi: Adolescence ke dauraan tez ya badalti bhaavnaayein hona normal kyon hai?
items.answer: Hormones and many big changes in the body, school and friendships all happen at once, and the brain is still developing; everyone goes through this.
hints: Ask how many things are changing at this age
Point to hormones affecting feelings too
Prompt: ___ and many life changes affect feelings
Assert: hormones and big changes make mood swings normal

verified.solverAnswer: Hormones and many changes (school, body, friends) affect emotions; it's a normal part of growing.

items.prompt_en: Why is it better to check information about growing up with a trusted adult, a doctor or a textbook rather than only with a friend or a random online video?
items.prompt_hi: Badhne ke baare mein jaankari kisi dost ya random online video ki bajaye bharosemand bade, doctor ya textbook se check karna kyon behtar hai?
items.answer: Friends and random videos can spread myths and wrong information; trusted adults, doctors and textbooks give correct and safe information.
hints: Ask how a friend would know if a video was right
Point to doctors and textbooks being checked sources
Prompt: rumours can be ___; doctors and books are ___
Assert: check with trusted adults and good sources because rumours mislead

verified.solverAnswer: Friends/videos may spread rumours or wrong info; trusted adults, doctors, textbooks give checked correct information.

items.prompt_en: Compare two ways Kabir handles stress before exams: (A) staying up all night on his phone and skipping meals; (B) sleeping on time, playing for half an hour and talking to his elder sister. Which helps more, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Exam se pehle tension sambhaalne ke Kabir ke do tareekon ki tulna karo: (A) poori raat phone pe jaagna aur khaana chhodna; (B) time pe sona, aadha ghanta khelna aur badi behen se baat karna. Kaunsa zyada madad karta hai, aur kyon?
items.answer: B, because sleep, physical activity and talking reduce stress and help the brain focus and remember; A makes tiredness, mood and concentration worse.
hints: Ask how they feel after a night of little sleep
Point to play and talking easing stress
Prompt: ___, activity and talking help; skipping sleep and meals makes it ___
Assert: B helps; sleep, play and talking lower stress

verified.solverAnswer: B helps more: sleep, play and talking reduce stress and keep brain working; A harms health and focus.

items.prompt_en: Some friends dare Ishaan to try tobacco 'just once'. What is a healthy way for him to respond?
items.prompt_hi: Kuch dost Ishaan ko 'bas ek baar' tobacco try karne ki challenge dete hain. Uske liye accha jawaab kya hoga?
items.answer: Say no firmly, walk away or suggest doing something else, and tell a trusted adult if the pressure continues. Tobacco is harmful and addictive, and real friends respect a no.
hints: Ask what a real friend would do after hearing no
Point to walking away as a strong choice
Prompt: say ___, walk ___, and tell a trusted adult
Assert: a firm no, walking away and telling an adult; tobacco harms and hooks

verified.solverAnswer: Firmly say no, walk away, tell a trusted adult; tobacco harms health and is addictive.

items.prompt_en: A friend tells you they have felt very sad for weeks and don't want to do anything. What could you do to help?
items.prompt_hi: Ek dost tumhe batata hai ki wo hafton se bahut udaas hai aur kuch karne ka mann nahi karta. Uski madad ke liye tum kya kar sakte ho?
items.answer: Listen kindly without making fun, encourage them to tell a trusted adult such as a parent, teacher or counsellor, and offer to go with them; if they seem unsafe, tell an adult straight away. Tele-MANAS (14416) and Childline (1098) are free helplines.
hints: Ask what the friend needs first
Point to a trusted adult who can really help
Prompt: listen, and help them tell a ___; helplines like ___ exist
Assert: listen kindly and get a trusted adult involved; helplines 14416 and 1098

verified.solverAnswer: Listen kindly, don't judge, encourage and help them tell a trusted adult/parent/counsellor; helplines like Tele-MANAS 14416 or Childline 1098.

items.prompt_en: Neel says, 'Talking about body changes is shameful; grown-up people never ask questions.' What is wrong?

items.answer: These changes are natural and happen to everyone; asking trusted adults or doctors is a sensible, grown-up thing to do, and it prevents myths and worry.

Point to everyone going through these changes

items.prompt_en: Draw a 'circle of trust' with yourself in the centre and at least four trusted people or places around you. Next to each, write one thing you could talk to them about.
items.prompt_hi: Ek 'circle of trust' banao jismein beech mein tum ho aur charon taraf kam se kam chaar bharosemand log ya jagah. Har ek ke paas likho ki unse kis baare mein baat kar sakte ho.
items.answer: For example: parent (body changes, worries); class teacher or school counsellor (school stress, bullying); doctor (health questions); elder sibling or cousin (friendships); Childline 1098 (if ever unsafe).

Point to people at home, at school and in health care

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger cousin who is about to start Class 7 what kinds of feelings might change and who they can talk to.

items.answer: Moods can change quickly, you may want more independence and care more about looks and friends; this is normal. Talk to parents, teachers, a counsellor or a doctor, and use sleep, play and hobbies to feel better.
hints: Invite them to start with what feelings may change
Point to the circle of trust
Prompt: moods may ___; talk to ___
Assert: changing feelings are normal; trusted adults and healthy habits help

verified.solverAnswer: Moods may swing, feel shy or sensitive; it's normal; talk to parents, teachers, counsellor; sleep and play help.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what number can a child in India call for free if they are in trouble or unsafe?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Bharat mein agar koi bachcha musibat mein ho ya surakshit na ho, toh wo kaunsa number free mein call kar sakta hai?
items.answer: Childline 1098 (and Tele-MANAS 14416 for emotional and mental health support).

skills.title: Explain why adolescents need a balanced diet with enough energy, protein, calcium and iron for rapid growth
Identify iron-rich foods, explain anaemia, and how vitamin C helps the body absorb iron
Plan hygiene routines suited to adolescence: daily bath, clean clothes, washing the face, brushing teeth, menstrual hygiene
Plan daily physical activity and enough sleep, and avoid skipping meals and too much junk food

expectations: Adolescents grow fast, so they need a balanced diet with enough energy (cereals like rice, roti, millets), proteins (dal, milk, eggs, paneer), calcium (milk, curd, ragi), iron (green leafy vegetables, jaggery, chana, dates), vitamins and minerals (fruits and vegetables) and water.

Lack of iron causes anaemia, which makes a person tired, pale and short of breath; eating iron-rich foods with vitamin C (lemon, amla, guava, orange) helps the body absorb iron, while tea with meals reduces it.
Skipping meals, especially breakfast, leaves the body short of energy and nutrients and does not make anyone fitter; junk food is high in fat, sugar and salt but low in nutrients.

Hygiene matters more now because sweat and oil glands are more active: a daily bath, clean clothes and socks, washing the face gently, brushing teeth twice a day, and for girls changing sanitary pads regularly during periods.
About an hour of physical activity every day and enough sleep (around 9 hours or more at this age) keep the body and mind healthy.

Thinks eating less is the same as being healthy

items.prompt_en: Why do adolescents need more protein and calcium in their diet?
items.prompt_hi: Adolescents ko apne khaane mein zyada protein aur calcium ki zaroorat kyon hoti hai?
items.answer: For fast growth: protein builds muscles and other body parts, and calcium builds strong bones and teeth.
hints: Ask what is growing fastest at this age
Point to muscles and bones
Prompt: protein builds ___; calcium builds ___
Assert: protein for muscles, calcium for bones, both needed for growth

verified.solverAnswer: Rapid growth: protein builds muscles/body tissues, calcium builds strong bones and teeth.

items.prompt_en: Name three iron-rich foods that are common in Indian homes.
items.prompt_hi: Teen aise iron se bharpoor khaane batao jo Indian gharon mein aam hain.
items.answer: For example: spinach (palak), methi and other green leafy vegetables, jaggery (gur), chana, rajma, dates, bajra, and eggs for those who eat them.
hints: Ask which green sabzi is famous for iron
Point to gur and chana
Prompt: palak, ___ and ___
Assert: palak, gur and chana are iron-rich

verified.solverAnswer: Palak (spinach), gur (jaggery), chana (chickpeas); also methi, dals, beetroot.

items.prompt_en: Two lunches have the same palak dal. One is eaten with a glass of lemon water, the other with a cup of tea. Predict which helps the body take in more iron.
items.prompt_hi: Do lunch mein ek jaisi palak dal hai. Ek ke saath nimbu-paani piya jaata hai, doosre ke saath ek cup chai. Guess karo kaunsa shareer ko zyada iron lene mein madad karega.
items.answer: The one with lemon water: vitamin C helps the body absorb iron, while substances in tea reduce iron absorption.
hints: Ask for a guess and a reason
Point to vitamin C in lemon
Prompt: vitamin ___ helps absorb iron; tea ___ it
Assert: lemon water helps; tea with meals reduces iron absorption

verified.solverAnswer: Lemon water: vitamin C helps iron absorption; tea (tannins) reduces it.

items.prompt_en: Count your pulse while sitting quietly: count the beats at your wrist for 30 seconds and double it. Predict: after one minute of skipping or jumping on the spot, will it go up, go down or stay the same? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Shaanti se baith ke apni nabz gino: kalaai pe 30 second tak dhadkan gino aur do se guna karo. Guess karo: ek minute rassi koodne ya jagah pe uchhalne ke baad nabz badhegi, ghategi ya utni hi rahegi? Kyon?
items.answer: It goes up, because working muscles need more oxygen and food energy, so the heart pumps faster to deliver them.
hints: Ask for a guess before jumping
Point to muscles needing more oxygen
Prompt: working muscles need more ___, so the heart beats ___
Assert: the pulse rises because muscles need more oxygen

verified.solverAnswer: Pulse goes up because muscles need more oxygen and energy so the heart pumps faster.

items.prompt_en: Predict which breakfast will keep you full and active longer until lunch: a packet of chips with a cola, or poha with peanuts and a glass of milk.
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo kaunsa nashta tumhe lunch tak zyada der bhara aur active rakhega: chips ka packet aur cola, ya moongfali wala poha aur ek glass doodh.
items.answer: Poha with peanuts and milk: it gives carbohydrates, protein and some fat that release energy steadily; chips and cola give a quick sugar rush, little nutrition, and hunger again soon.
hints: Ask how they feel an hour after a cola
Point to protein in peanuts and milk
Prompt: poha with peanuts and milk gives ___ energy
Assert: poha, peanuts and milk keep you going; chips and cola do not

verified.solverAnswer: Poha with peanuts and milk: carbs, protein, fat, calcium give lasting energy; chips and cola give quick sugar/empty calories and leave you hungry.

items.prompt_en: Why are adolescent girls in India at greater risk of anaemia, and what helps?
items.prompt_hi: Bharat mein kishor ladkiyon ko anaemia ka khatra zyada kyon hota hai, aur kya madad karta hai?
items.answer: They are growing fast and lose some blood during periods each month, so they need more iron. Iron-rich foods eaten with vitamin C, and iron tablets when a doctor or a school health programme gives them, help.
hints: Ask what is lost each month during periods
Point to iron being needed to make blood
Prompt: growth and ___ increase the need for ___
Assert: growth and monthly blood loss raise iron needs; iron foods and tablets help

verified.solverAnswer: Growth plus blood loss in periods raises iron need; iron-rich foods, vitamin C, and iron-folic acid tablets given by doctor/school programme help.
verified.note: SAFETY (low): hint 4 says 'iron foods and tablets help' with no 'only as given by a doctor / school programme' caveat (iron tablets are a child-poisoning hazard); the key answer itself is correctly caveated.

items.prompt_en: Compare two routines: Raju bathes daily and changes his socks every day; Manu bathes every three days and wears the same socks. Who is more likely to have body odour and skin problems, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Do routine ki tulna karo: Raju roz nahaata hai aur roz moze badalta hai; Manu teen din mein ek baar nahaata hai aur wahi moze pehenta hai. Kisko shareer ki gandh aur skin ki pareshaani hone ki zyada sambhavna hai, aur kyon?
items.answer: Manu, because sweat builds up on his skin and socks and bacteria grow on it, causing odour and skin infections; Raju's daily washing removes the sweat and bacteria.
hints: Ask what collects in socks during the day
Point to bacteria feeding on sweat
Prompt: sweat and ___ build up on Manu's skin
Assert: Manu, because sweat and bacteria build up without daily washing

verified.solverAnswer: Manu; sweat and bacteria build up without washing and clean socks, causing odour and skin problems/infection.

items.prompt_en: Simran says, 'I'll skip lunch and dinner so I become fit fast.' What is the problem with her plan?
items.prompt_hi: Simran kehti hai, 'Main lunch aur dinner chhod doongi taaki jaldi fit ho jaaun.' Uske plan mein kya gadbad hai?
items.answer: Her growing body needs regular, balanced meals; skipping them makes her tired and weak, harms growth and concentration, and is not fitness. Fitness comes from balanced food, daily activity and good sleep.
hints: Ask what her body uses for energy and growth
Point to activity as the real route to fitness
Prompt: a growing body needs ___ meals; fitness comes from ___
Assert: skipping meals harms a growing body; balanced food and exercise build fitness

verified.solverAnswer: Skipping meals deprives growing body of energy and nutrients, tiredness, harm; fitness comes from balanced meals plus exercise and sleep.

items.prompt_en: A vegetarian hostel serves rice, aloo sabzi and tea every day. Suggest two changes that would give the students more iron and protein.
items.prompt_hi: Ek shaakahari hostel mein roz chawal, aloo ki sabzi aur chai milti hai. Do aise badlav sujhao jisse students ko zyada iron aur protein mile.
items.answer: For example: add dal, chana or rajma for protein and iron; add green leafy vegetables like palak or methi with lemon; give milk, curd or paneer; serve tea away from meals; include millets like bajra or ragi.
hints: Ask which foods on the menu give protein
Point to missing dal and green sabzi
Prompt: add ___ for protein and ___ for iron
Assert: add dal or chana and green leafy sabzi with lemon; keep tea away from meals

verified.solverAnswer: Add dal/chana/rajma/curd/milk for protein, green leafy sabzi (palak/methi) and gur for iron with lemon/amla for vitamin C; avoid tea with meals.

items.prompt_en: Design a one-day plan for a Class 7 student that fits in school, homework, play and sleep, and meets the needs of a growing body.
items.prompt_hi: Class 7 ke ek student ke liye ek din ka plan banao jismein school, homework, khelna aur sona sab ho, aur badhte shareer ki zaroorat poori ho.
items.answer: It should include three balanced meals and healthy snacks (with dal, vegetables, milk or curd, fruit), about an hour of active play, around 9 or more hours of sleep, a daily bath and brushing twice, and limited screen time.
hints: Ask what time they would need to sleep to get about 9 hours
Point to meals, play, hygiene and sleep slots
Prompt: three ___ meals, an hour of ___, about ___ hours of sleep
Assert: balanced meals, an hour of play, enough sleep and hygiene every day

verified.solverAnswer: Sleep about 9 hours, three balanced meals, about an hour of play/exercise, school, homework, bath and clean clothes, limited screen time.

items.prompt_en: Draw a thali divided into parts showing what a growing adolescent's lunch should include. Label one food in each part and what it gives the body.
items.prompt_hi: Ek thaali banao jo hisson mein bati ho aur dikhaaye ki badhte adolescent ke lunch mein kya hona chahiye. Har hisse mein ek khaana aur wo shareer ko kya deta hai, label karo.
items.answer: For example: roti or rice (energy), dal, chana, paneer or egg (protein), green leafy sabzi (iron and vitamins), curd (calcium), salad or fruit (vitamins and fibre), and a glass of water.
hints: Invite them to draw the big parts first
Point to energy, protein, iron and calcium
Prompt: roti for ___, dal for ___, palak for ___, curd for ___
Assert: a balanced thali has cereals, pulses, greens, dairy and fruit

verified.solverAnswer: Roti/rice: energy (carbohydrate); dal: protein; palak/green sabzi: iron and vitamins; curd: calcium; fruit: vitamins; some salad/water.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger cousin why personal hygiene becomes more important during adolescence, and give two habits to follow.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko samjhao ki adolescence mein saaf-safaai zyada zaroori kyon ho jaati hai, aur do aadatein batao.
items.answer: Sweat and oil glands become more active, so bacteria on sweaty skin cause body odour and skin problems. Habits: bathe daily, wear clean clothes and socks, wash the face gently, brush twice a day, and for girls change pads regularly during periods.
hints: Invite them to start with what changes in the skin
Point to sweat, oil and bacteria
Prompt: glands get more ___, so bathe ___ and wear ___ clothes
Assert: more sweat and oil make daily washing and clean clothes important

verified.solverAnswer: Sweat and oil glands become more active so bacteria cause odour/pimples; bathe daily, wear clean clothes, wash hands.

items.prompt_en: From last time: which fruits or vegetables help your body absorb iron from palak?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: kaunse phal ya sabziyan palak ka iron shareer mein lene mein madad karte hain?
items.answer: Foods rich in vitamin C, such as lemon, amla, guava, orange or tomato.
hints: Ask what was squeezed on the dal in the experiment
Point to vitamin C
Prompt: foods with vitamin ___
Assert: vitamin C foods like lemon and amla help absorb iron

verified.solverAnswer: Vitamin C foods: lemon, amla, orange, tomato, guava.

steps: Notice the clue: tiredness can come from skipped meals or from low iron (anaemia)

Lunch: roti, dal or chana, a green leafy sabzi with lemon squeezed on it, and curd

Lunch: roti, dal, a green leafy sabzi with ___, and curd

skills.title: Explain that heat flows from a hotter object to a colder one, and that in solids it passes from particle to particle (conduction)
Classify materials as good conductors of heat (metals) or poor conductors/insulators (wood, plastic, clay, cloth, wool, air)
Explain everyday uses: metal pans with wooden handles, woollens and feathers trapping air, ice boxes
Explain why a metal object feels colder than a wooden one at the same temperature

expectations: Heat always flows from a hotter object to a colder one until both reach the same temperature.
In solids, heat travels by conduction: it is passed along from particle to particle, from the hot end towards the cold end, while the material itself stays in place.
Metals such as steel, aluminium, copper and iron are good conductors of heat; wood, plastic, clay, cloth, wool and air are poor conductors (insulators).
Woollen clothes do not make heat; they trap air between their fibres, and because air is a poor conductor, body heat escapes slowly.
A metal object at room temperature feels colder than a wooden one at the same temperature because the metal conducts heat away from our hand much faster.
Uses: cooking pots of metal with handles of wood or plastic; ice boxes and flasks with insulating layers that slow heat flow.

misconceptions.belief: Woollen clothes produce heat.
signs: Says a sweater 'gives' heat
Expects a sweater to melt an ice cube faster

diagnostic.prompt_en: One ice cube is wrapped in a woollen sweater and another is left unwrapped on a plate in the same room. What happens?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek barf ke tukde ko oon ke sweater mein lapeta gaya aur doosre ko usi kamre mein plate pe khula chhoda gaya. Kya hoga?

options.text: The wrapped one melts faster because wool makes heat
The wrapped one melts more slowly because wool traps air and slows the heat flowing in from the room
Both melt at exactly the same time

remediation.representation: A side-by-side time-lapse of the wrapped and unwrapped ice cubes with a clock
remediation.moveShape: Get the prediction first; after the reveal, ask what the sweater did to the heat flow in both cases

misconceptions.belief: Metals feel cold because they are colder than other things in the same room.
signs: Says the steel railing is colder than the wooden bench beside it
Thinks a steel plate cools things down

diagnostic.prompt_en: A steel plate and a wooden board have both been on the same table all night. Which one is colder?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek steel ki plate aur ek lakdi ka board dono raat bhar ek hi mez pe rakhe rahe. Kaun zyada thanda hai?

options.text: The steel plate, because it feels colder, so it must be colder
Both are at the same temperature; steel feels colder because it carries heat away from your hand faster
The wooden board

remediation.representation: A thermometer reading both surfaces the same, beside a heat-arrow animation leaving a hand faster into steel
remediation.moveShape: Run the ice-cube-on-steel versus ice-cube-on-wood race to turn 'feels cold' into 'moves heat fast'

misconceptions.belief: Cold flows from cold things into warm things.
signs: Says 'the cold from the ice goes into my hand'
Says a fridge 'puts cold' into food

diagnostic.prompt_en: When you hold an ice cube, why does your hand feel cold?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Jab tum barf ka tukda pakadte ho toh haath thanda kyon lagta hai?

options.text: Cold flows from the ice into your hand
Heat flows from your warm hand into the ice
The ice gives off cold rays

remediation.representation: Arrow diagrams that only ever point from hot to cold, with 'cold' shown as 'less heat'
remediation.moveShape: Have the child redraw their own arrows for ice in hand, fridge and chai, always from hotter to colder

items.prompt_en: In which direction does heat always flow between two objects?
items.prompt_hi: Do cheezon ke beech garmi hamesha kis disha mein behti hai?
items.answer: From the hotter object to the colder one.
hints: Ask what happens to a cup of chai left on the table
Point to the chai cooling and the room warming slightly
Prompt: heat flows from ___ to ___
Assert: heat flows from hotter to colder

verified.solverAnswer: From hotter to colder.

items.prompt_en: Sort these into good and poor conductors of heat: steel spoon, wooden ladle, aluminium pan, plastic handle, woollen cloth, copper wire.
items.prompt_hi: Inhe garmi ke acche aur kharaab conductor mein baanto: steel ka chammach, lakdi ki karchhi, aluminium ka pan, plastic ka handle, oon ka kapda, copper ka taar.
items.answer: Good conductors: steel spoon, aluminium pan, copper wire. Poor conductors: wooden ladle, plastic handle, woollen cloth.
hints: Ask which ones are metals
Point to handles that stay cool
Prompt: the ___ are good conductors; wood, plastic and wool are ___
Assert: metals conduct heat well; wood, plastic and wool do not

verified.solverAnswer: Good: steel spoon, aluminium pan, copper wire. Poor: wooden ladle, plastic handle, woollen cloth.

items.prompt_en: Wrap one ice cube in a woollen sweater and leave another unwrapped on a plate in the same room. Predict which one will melt first.
items.prompt_hi: Ek barf ke tukde ko oon ke sweater mein lapeto aur doosre ko usi kamre mein plate pe khula chhodo. Guess karo kaunsa pehle pighlega.
items.answer: The unwrapped one melts first. The sweater does not make heat; the air trapped in it slows the room's heat from reaching the ice, so the wrapped one melts more slowly.
hints: Ask for a guess and a reason before wrapping
Point to where the heat to melt the ice comes from
Prompt: wool ___ heat flow; it does not ___ heat
Assert: the unwrapped cube melts first; wool slows heat flow

verified.solverAnswer: The unwrapped cube melts first; wool is an insulator that slows heat flowing in from the room.

items.prompt_en: Ask an adult to pour warm water (not boiling) into a mug. Stand a steel spoon, a plastic spoon and a wooden spoon in it. Predict: after two minutes, which handle will feel warmest?
items.prompt_hi: Kisi bade se mug mein garam (ubalta hua nahi) paani daalne ko kaho. Usme steel ka, plastic ka aur lakdi ka chammach khada karo. Guess karo: do minute baad kiska handle sabse garam lagega?
items.answer: The steel spoon's handle, because steel is a good conductor and passes heat up from the water quickly; plastic and wood are poor conductors.
hints: Ask for a guess before touching
Point to which material is a metal
Prompt: ___ conducts heat up the handle fastest
Assert: the steel spoon warms up; plastic and wood stay cool

verified.solverAnswer: Steel spoon handle warmest; plastic and wood stay cool.

items.prompt_en: Place two equal ice cubes at the same moment: one on a steel plate and one on a wooden chopping board, both at room temperature. Predict which melts faster.
items.prompt_hi: Do barabar barf ke tukde ek hi samay rakho: ek steel ki plate pe aur ek lakdi ke chopping board pe, dono kamre ke taapmaan pe. Guess karo kaun jaldi pighlega.
items.answer: The one on the steel plate melts faster: steel conducts heat from the plate and the room into the ice much faster than wood does, even though steel feels colder to touch.
hints: Ask which surface feels colder, and then which melts ice faster
Point to heat having to reach the ice
Prompt: steel ___ heat into the ice faster
Assert: ice melts faster on steel because steel conducts heat quickly

verified.solverAnswer: Ice melts faster on steel because steel conducts heat from room/ air to the ice faster.

items.prompt_en: Why are a kadhai and a tawa made of iron or aluminium, but their handles made of wood or plastic?
items.prompt_hi: Kadhai aur tawa lohe ya aluminium ke kyon hote hain, par unke handle lakdi ya plastic ke kyon?
items.answer: The metal conducts heat quickly from the flame to the food; wood and plastic are poor conductors, so the handle stays cool enough to hold.
hints: Ask what each part needs to do
Point to the flame below and the hand on the handle
Prompt: the body ___ heat; the handle is a ___ conductor
Assert: metal body conducts heat; wooden or plastic handle insulates the hand

verified.solverAnswer: Metal body conducts heat to food; wood/plastic handle is poor conductor so hand doesn't get burnt.

items.prompt_en: On a winter morning, the steel railing on the school stairs feels much colder than the wooden bench next to it. Why, if both are at the same temperature?
items.prompt_hi: Sardi ki subah school ki seedhiyon ki steel railing paas ki lakdi ki bench se bahut zyada thandi lagti hai. Agar dono ka taapmaan same hai, toh aisa kyon?
items.answer: Steel conducts heat away from your hand much faster than wood does, so your hand loses heat quickly and feels cold, even though both are at the same temperature.
acceptable: haath ki garmi jaldi kheenchti hai
hints: Ask which way heat is flowing when you touch the railing
Point to how fast each material carries heat
Prompt: steel carries heat away from your hand ___
Assert: steel feels colder because it conducts heat away from your hand faster

verified.solverAnswer: Same temperature, but steel conducts heat away from your hand faster so feels colder; wood is poor conductor.

items.prompt_en: Compare a cotton shirt and a woollen sweater on a cold day. Why does the sweater keep you warmer, even though neither makes any heat?
items.prompt_hi: Thande din pe cotton ki shirt aur oon ke sweater ki tulna karo. Sweater zyada garam kyon rakhta hai, jabki dono mein se koi garmi nahi banata?
items.answer: The sweater's fluffy fibres trap much more air, and air is a poor conductor, so body heat escapes slowly; the thin cotton shirt traps little air.
hints: Ask where the warmth in both cases comes from
Point to air trapped between wool fibres
Prompt: wool traps ___, which is a ___ conductor
Assert: trapped air in wool slows heat loss; your body is the heater

verified.solverAnswer: Wool traps air between fibres, air is poor conductor, so body heat is not lost quickly; sweater insulates, your body is the heat source.

items.prompt_en: When you hold an ice-cream cone, your hand gets cold and the ice-cream starts melting. Describe which way heat is flowing.
items.prompt_hi: Jab tum ice-cream cone pakadte ho, haath thanda hota hai aur ice-cream pighalne lagti hai. Batao garmi kis taraf beh rahi hai.
items.answer: Heat flows from your warm hand (and the air) into the ice-cream; your hand loses heat and feels cold, and the ice-cream gains heat and melts.
hints: Ask which is hotter, the hand or the ice-cream
Point to the ice-cream melting as it gains heat
Prompt: heat flows from the ___ to the ___
Assert: heat flows from the hand into the ice-cream

verified.solverAnswer: Heat flows from your warmer hand into the cold ice cream (hotter to colder), so hand loses heat and feels cold.

items.prompt_en: In winter, birds often fluff up their feathers. Using the idea of conduction, why does this help them stay warm?
items.prompt_hi: Sardi mein pakshi aksar apne pankh phula lete hain. Conduction ke idea se samjhao ki isse unhe garam rehne mein madad kyon milti hai.
items.answer: Fluffing up traps more air between the feathers; air is a poor conductor, so less body heat escapes.
hints: Ask what gets trapped when feathers fluff up
Point to the sweater idea
Prompt: fluffed feathers trap more ___
Assert: trapped air insulates the bird, like a sweater

verified.solverAnswer: Fluffed feathers trap more air that insulates, reducing heat loss from the body.

items.prompt_en: Ananya writes: 'The fridge puts cold into the food.' Correct the science.
items.prompt_hi: Ananya likhti hai: 'Fridge khaane mein thand daal deta hai.' Science ko sahi karo.
items.answer: The fridge takes heat out of the food: heat flows from the warmer food into the colder inside of the fridge, and the fridge pumps that heat outside, so the food cools.
acceptable: heat flows out of the food
hints: Ask which way heat always flows
Point to the warm back of the fridge
Prompt: the fridge takes ___ out of the food
Assert: there is no flow of cold; the fridge removes heat

verified.solverAnswer: Fridge doesn't add cold; it removes heat from the food and releases it outside (back).

items.prompt_en: Draw a steel rod with one end dipped in a pot of hot water and three markers stuck along its length. Show with arrows how heat moves, and number the markers in the order they would warm up.
items.prompt_hi: Ek steel ki rod banao jiska ek sira garam paani ke bartan mein dooba ho aur uski lambaai pe teen marker lage hon. Teer se dikhao ki garmi kaise chalti hai, aur markers ko us kram mein number do jis kram mein wo garam honge.
items.answer: Arrows go from the end in the hot water along the rod towards the dry end. The marker nearest the hot water warms first (1), then the middle one (2), then the farthest one (3).
hints: Invite them to draw the rod and the water first
Point to the end where heat enters
Prompt: heat travels from the ___ end towards the ___ end
Assert: heat moves along the rod from hot to cold; the nearest marker warms first

verified.solverAnswer: Hot end in water, heat flows by conduction along rod to the cooler end; marker nearest the hot water warms first (1), then middle (2), then farthest (3).

items.prompt_en: Explain to your grandfather why his steel tumbler of hot chai is hard to hold, but a kulhad (clay cup) is easy to hold.
items.prompt_hi: Apne daada ya naana ko samjhao ki garam chai wala steel ka gilaas pakadna mushkil kyon hota hai, par kulhad pakadna aasaan kyon.
items.answer: Steel is a good conductor, so heat flows quickly from the chai through the tumbler into his fingers; clay is a poor conductor, so the outside of the kulhad stays cooler.
hints: Invite them to start with which material conducts heat well
Point to the fingers touching the outside
Prompt: steel is a ___ conductor; clay is a ___ conductor
Assert: steel passes heat to the fingers quickly; clay does not

verified.solverAnswer: Steel is a good conductor and quickly passes heat from chai to fingers; clay is poor conductor so stays comfortable.

items.prompt_en: From last time: name one good conductor of heat and one poor conductor of heat.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: garmi ka ek accha conductor aur ek kharaab conductor batao.
items.answer: Good: a metal such as steel, copper, iron or aluminium. Poor: wood, plastic, wool, clay, cloth or air.
hints: Ask what pans are made of
Point to handles
Prompt: a good conductor like ___, a poor one like ___
Assert: metals conduct heat well; wood and plastic do not

verified.solverAnswer: Good: steel/copper/aluminium; poor: wood/plastic/wool.

skills.title: Explain convection in liquids and gases: the heated part expands, becomes lighter and rises, while the cooler, heavier part sinks, forming a current
Explain that heat flows from hot to cold in every direction, while in convection it is warm fluid that rises and cool fluid that sinks
Explain the sea breeze in the day and the land breeze at night
Apply convection to everyday design: ventilators and exhaust fans placed high, ACs high and heaters low

expectations: In liquids and gases, heat is mainly carried by convection: the heated part expands, becomes lighter and rises, while cooler, heavier liquid or air sinks to take its place, setting up a circulating current.

Heat itself flows from hot to cold in every direction (for example sideways through a spoon by conduction, or from a heater to your side by radiation); in convection it is the warm liquid or air that rises and the cool part that sinks.
During the day, land heats up faster than the sea; air over the land warms and rises, and cooler air from the sea moves in to take its place: the sea breeze.
At night, land cools faster than the sea; air over the warmer sea rises, and cooler air from the land moves out towards the sea: the land breeze.
Ventilators and kitchen exhausts are placed high to let hot air out; ACs are fitted high and heaters work best low down because cool air sinks and warm air rises.

misconceptions.belief: Heat only moves upward.
signs: Says the floor beside a heater cannot get warm
Says heat in a spoon only rises

diagnostic.prompt_en: You sit beside a room heater, not above it, and feel warm. How does the heat reach you?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tum room heater ke bagal mein baithe ho, upar nahi, aur garmi mehsoos hoti hai. Garmi tum tak kaise pahunchi?

options.text: It can't; heat only goes up, so you must be imagining it
Heat flows from hot to cold in all directions; here it reaches you mostly by radiation
The heater pushes the cold air away

remediation.representation: A room diagram with heat arrows going sideways and down from a heater and only the warm-air arrows going up

misconceptions.belief: In the daytime the breeze at the beach blows from the hot land towards the cool sea.
signs: Says warm air 'moves to' cooler places across the ground
Gets the sea and land breeze directions swapped

diagnostic.prompt_en: On a sunny afternoon at Marina beach, which way does the breeze near the ground blow?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Marina beach pe dhoop wali dopahar mein zameen ke paas hawa kis taraf behti hai?

options.text: From land to sea, because hot air moves towards the cooler sea
From sea to land, because air over the hot land rises and cooler sea air moves in
There is no breeze in the daytime

remediation.representation: A two-panel animated loop: rising air over the hot land, sinking air over the sea, and the ground-level arrow from sea to land
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to place the 'rising' arrow first, then work out where replacement air must come from

misconceptions.belief: Cold air rises, so cooling devices should be placed near the floor.
signs: Suggests putting an AC near the floor
Thinks cold air from a fridge floats up

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why is an AC usually fitted high on the wall?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: AC aksar deewar pe oonchaai pe kyon lagaya jaata hai?

options.text: So the cold air can rise up to the ceiling
Because cool air is heavier and sinks, spreading down through the room
Only so that children can't reach it

remediation.representation: The coloured-ice-cube experiment: cold coloured water sinking in warm water
remediation.moveShape: Link the sinking colour to cool air falling from a high AC, then ask where a heater should go

items.prompt_en: What is the transfer of heat by the movement of a heated liquid or gas called?
items.prompt_hi: Garam liquid ya gas ke chalne se garmi ke pahunchne ko kya kehte hain?
items.answer: Convection.
hints: Ask what happens to warm water at the bottom of a pot
Point to the moving warm water carrying heat
Prompt: heat carried by moving liquid or gas is ___
Assert: it is called convection

verified.solverAnswer: Convection.

items.prompt_en: When does a sea breeze blow, in the day or at night, and in which direction?
items.prompt_hi: Sea breeze kab chalti hai, din mein ya raat mein, aur kis disha mein?
items.answer: During the day, from the sea towards the land.
acceptable: din mein, samudra se zameen ki taraf
hints: Ask which heats faster in sunlight, land or sea
Point to air rising over the land
Prompt: in the ___, from the sea to the ___
Assert: the sea breeze blows from sea to land in the daytime

verified.solverAnswer: In the daytime, from the sea to the land.

items.prompt_en: Freeze water with a few drops of food colour to make a coloured ice cube. Gently drop it into a clear glass of warm water. Predict where the coloured water will go as the ice melts.
items.prompt_hi: Paani mein khaane ka rang daal ke rangeen barf ka tukda jamaao. Use dheere se garam paani ke saaf glass mein daalo. Guess karo barf pighalne pe rangeen paani kahaan jaayega.
items.answer: The cold coloured water sinks to the bottom, because cold water is heavier (denser) than warm water; the warm water stays above. This sinking and rising is convection.
hints: Ask for a guess before dropping the cube
Point to the colour as a way to see the cold water
Prompt: cold water is ___, so it ___
Assert: cold coloured water sinks; warm water stays on top

verified.solverAnswer: Cold coloured water sinks to the bottom as it melts, while warm water rises/stays on top (convection currents).

items.prompt_en: A room has a window near the floor and a ventilator near the ceiling. On a hot day, predict which way air will move through each opening.
items.prompt_hi: Ek kamre mein zameen ke paas ek khidki hai aur chhat ke paas ek ventilator. Garam din pe guess karo har khule hisse se hawa kis taraf chalegi.
items.answer: Warm air rises and leaves through the ventilator near the ceiling; cooler air from outside comes in through the lower window.
acceptable: out through the ventilator, in through the window
hints: Ask where the warmest air in a room collects
Point to the opening near the ceiling
Prompt: warm air leaves through the ___; cooler air enters through the ___
Assert: hot air escapes high; cool air comes in low

verified.solverAnswer: Warm air rises and leaves through the ventilator near the ceiling; cooler air enters through the low window.

items.prompt_en: Predict: at 10 at night on a beach in Chennai, which way will the breeze near the ground blow, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: Chennai ke beach pe raat 10 baje zameen ke paas hawa kis taraf chalegi, aur kyon?
items.answer: From the land towards the sea (a land breeze): at night the land cools faster than the sea, so the air over the warmer sea rises and cooler air from the land moves out to replace it.
hints: Ask which cools faster at night, land or water
Point to air rising over the warmer sea
Prompt: at night air rises over the ___, so air flows from the ___
Assert: a land breeze blows from land to sea at night

verified.solverAnswer: Land breeze: from land to sea, since land cools faster at night, and warmer air over sea rises.

items.prompt_en: Why does all the water in a pot on the stove get hot, even though only the bottom of the pot touches the flame?
items.prompt_hi: Chulhe pe rakhe bartan ka saara paani garam kyon ho jaata hai, jabki sirf bartan ki tali aag ko chhooti hai?
items.answer: Water at the bottom warms, expands, becomes lighter and rises, while cooler water from the top sinks to be heated; these convection currents mix the heat through all the water.
hints: Ask what warm water does that cold water does not
Point to the circular current in the pot
Prompt: warm water ___ and cool water ___, carrying heat around
Assert: convection currents spread heat through the whole pot

verified.solverAnswer: Water near the bottom heats, becomes lighter and rises; cooler water sinks; convection currents spread heat throughout.

items.prompt_en: Why is an AC fitted high on the wall, while a room heater works best placed on the floor?
items.prompt_hi: AC deewar pe oonchaai pe kyon lagta hai, jabki room heater zameen pe rakhne pe sabse accha kaam karta hai?
items.answer: Cool air from the AC is heavier and sinks, spreading through the room; warm air from a heater on the floor rises and spreads upward, so both set up convection currents that mix the room's air.
acceptable: cool air sinks, warm air rises
hints: Ask which way cool air moves
Point to the sinking coloured ice water
Prompt: cool air ___ from high up; warm air ___ from the floor
Assert: AC high because cool air sinks; heater low because warm air rises

verified.solverAnswer: Cool air is denser and sinks so AC high cools whole room; warm air rises so heater low warms air that circulates upwards.

items.prompt_en: Compare how heat reaches your hand when (a) you hold it above a cup of hot tea, and (b) you touch the top of a steel spoon resting in hot tea. Name the way of heat transfer in each.
items.prompt_hi: Tulna karo ki garmi tumhare haath tak kaise pahunchti hai jab (a) tum haath garam chai ke cup ke upar rakhte ho, aur (b) garam chai mein rakhe steel ke chammach ka upar wala hissa chhoote ho. Har ek mein garmi pahunchne ka tareeka batao.
items.answer: (a) Mostly convection: warm air and steam rise up to your hand. (b) Conduction: heat travels through the metal of the spoon to your fingers.
hints: Ask what is moving in case (a)
Point to the solid spoon in case (b)
Prompt: rising warm air is ___; heat through the metal is ___
Assert: above the cup is convection; through the spoon is conduction

verified.solverAnswer: (a) Convection (rising hot air; some radiation); (b) conduction through the solid spoon.

items.prompt_en: Fishermen in coastal Kerala often sail out to sea early in the morning and return in the afternoon. How could land and sea breezes help their sailboats?
items.prompt_hi: Kerala ke tatiya ilaakon ke machhuaare aksar subah jaldi samudra mein jaate hain aur dopahar ko laut-te hain. Land breeze aur sea breeze unki naav ki kaise madad kar sakti hai?
items.answer: The land breeze that blows from land to sea through the night and early morning helps push boats out; the afternoon sea breeze blowing from sea to land helps bring them back.
acceptable: land breeze out, sea breeze back
subah land breeze, dopahar sea breeze
hints: Ask which breeze blows early in the morning
Point to the afternoon sea breeze
Prompt: the ___ breeze carries them out, the ___ breeze brings them back
Assert: land breeze out in the morning, sea breeze home in the afternoon

verified.solverAnswer: Land breeze at night/early morning blows toward sea, carrying boats out; sea breeze in afternoon blows toward land, bringing them back.

items.prompt_en: Kitchen exhaust fans are fixed high on the wall, and many old houses had openings near the roof of the kitchen. Explain why.
items.prompt_hi: Kitchen ke exhaust fan deewar pe oonchaai pe lagte hain, aur kai purane gharon mein kitchen ki chhat ke paas khule hisse hote the. Kyon?
items.answer: Hot air, steam and smoke from cooking rise; openings high up let them escape, while cooler fresh air comes in lower down, keeping the kitchen cooler and less smoky.
hints: Ask where the smoke from cooking goes
Point to warm air rising
Prompt: hot air and ___ rise, so openings are placed ___
Assert: rising hot air and smoke escape through high openings

verified.solverAnswer: Hot air, smoke and fumes rise, so high openings/exhaust fans let them out.

items.prompt_en: Dev says, 'Heat only moves up, so the floor next to a heater can't get warm.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Dev kehta hai, 'Garmi sirf upar jaati hai, isliye heater ke bagal ka farsh garam nahi ho sakta.' Kya galat hai?
items.answer: Heat flows from hot to cold in all directions; the heater warms things beside it and below it by radiation and conduction. Only the warm air rises by convection.
hints: Ask whether your feet warm up near a heater
Point to the difference between heat flow and warm air rising
Prompt: heat flows in ___ directions; only warm ___ rises
Assert: heat spreads every way; convection is just warm air rising

verified.solverAnswer: Heat flows in all directions from hot to cold (conduction/radiation); only warm air rises by convection; floor near heater is warmed by radiation/conduction.

items.prompt_en: Draw two pictures of a beach, one for the afternoon and one for the night. Use arrows to show air rising, sinking and moving across, and label which is the sea breeze and which is the land breeze.
items.prompt_hi: Beach ki do picture banao, ek dopahar ki aur ek raat ki. Teer se dikhao hawa kahaan upar uth rahi hai, kahaan neeche aa rahi hai aur kahaan aar-paar chal rahi hai, aur label karo kaunsi sea breeze hai aur kaunsi land breeze.
items.answer: Afternoon: air rises over the hot land, sinks over the cooler sea, and near the ground moves from sea to land (sea breeze). Night: air rises over the warmer sea, sinks over the cooler land, and near the ground moves from land to sea (land breeze).
hints: Invite them to start with where air rises in each picture
Point to the ground-level arrow filling the gap
Prompt: in the afternoon air rises over the ___; at night over the ___
Assert: the breeze near the ground always flows towards where air is rising

verified.solverAnswer: Afternoon: land hot, air rises over land, sea breeze sea to land near ground. Night: sea warmer, air rises over sea, land breeze land to sea.

items.prompt_en: Explain convection to a younger child using the coloured ice cube experiment.
items.prompt_hi: Rangeen barf wale experiment se ek chhote bachche ko convection samjhao.
items.answer: When the coloured ice melts, the cold coloured water sinks because it is heavier, and warmer water stays on top or rises; liquids and gases carry heat by moving like this, and that is convection.
hints: Invite them to describe what the colour did
Point to cold sinking and warm rising
Prompt: cold water ___, warm water ___, and that moving is called ___
Assert: cold sinks, warm rises; moving fluid carrying heat is convection

verified.solverAnswer: Coloured cold water from melting ice sinks, warm water rises; this movement of liquid carrying heat is convection.

items.prompt_en: From last time: why does land heat up faster than the sea during the day?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: din mein zameen samudra se jaldi garam kyon hoti hai?
items.answer: Land (soil and rock) heats up and cools down faster than water, which needs much more heat to warm up and also mixes the heat deep down.
acceptable: paani der se garam hota hai
hints: Ask which feels hotter at noon on a beach, sand or sea water
Point to water needing more heat
Prompt: water needs ___ heat to warm up than land
Assert: land heats and cools faster than water

verified.solverAnswer: Water has high specific heat/needs more heat to warm up than land, and it mixes; land heats and cools faster.

workedExample.problem: Explain step by step why a sea breeze blows at Marina beach on a sunny afternoon.
steps: The Sun heats both the land and the sea
Land heats up faster than water
Air over the hot land becomes warm, expands, gets lighter and rises
Cooler, heavier air over the sea moves in to take its place
This flow of cool air from the sea to the land is the sea breeze

Air over the land becomes warm and ___
Cooler air over the ___ moves in to take its place
This flow from sea to land is the ___

skills.title: Explain radiation as heat transfer that needs no material in between and can travel through empty space
Explain that dark, dull surfaces absorb more radiation while light-coloured, shiny surfaces reflect more
Apply this: light clothes in summer, dark clothes in cold sunny places, black-painted solar cookers, white roofs and tanks

expectations: Radiation is the transfer of heat without needing any material in between; it can travel even through empty space.
Heat from the Sun reaches the Earth through space by radiation; we also feel radiation from the side of a heater or a hot stove without touching it.
All objects give out some radiation; hotter objects give out more.
Dark and dull surfaces absorb more radiation, so they heat up faster in sunlight; light-coloured and shiny surfaces reflect more and stay cooler.
So light-coloured clothes are comfortable in summer and dark clothes in cold sunny places; solar cookers are painted black inside; white roofs and silver or white tanks stay cooler.

misconceptions.belief: Heat cannot travel through empty space.
signs: Says the Sun's heat must come by air
Cannot explain how sunlight warms a spacecraft

diagnostic.prompt_en: Between the Sun and the Earth there is almost empty space. How does the Sun's heat reach us?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Sun aur Earth ke beech lagbhag khaali space hai. Sun ki garmi hum tak kaise pahunchti hai?

options.text: It can't; the heat we feel is made by the air itself
By radiation, which needs no material to travel through
By conduction through space

remediation.representation: A three-lane diagram (conduction, convection, radiation) where only the radiation lane continues across an empty gap
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child which lanes need particles, then which one could cross empty space

misconceptions.belief: Black colour 'attracts' heat like a magnet, and white clothes are cold in themselves.
signs: Says 'black pulls heat'
Says white cloth 'makes you cold'

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why does a black car get hotter in the sun than a white car?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Dhoop mein kaali car safed car se zyada garam kyon ho jaati hai?

options.text: Black attracts heat like a magnet pulls iron
Black absorbs more of the sunlight falling on it, while white reflects more of it
White cars have cold paint

remediation.representation: An arrow diagram: equal sunlight arrows hit both cars; most bounce off white, most are soaked up by black
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child whether the black car pulls in extra sunlight or just keeps more of the same sunlight

misconceptions.belief: Radiation heat comes only from the Sun, not from everyday hot objects.
signs: Says warmth beside a heater must be convection
Does not connect a hot tawa's warmth on the face to radiation

diagnostic.prompt_en: You stand a little to the side of a room heater, not above it, and your face feels warm. How did the heat reach you?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tum room heater ke thoda bagal mein khade ho, upar nahi, aur chehre pe garmi lagti hai. Garmi kaise pahunchi?

options.text: Only the Sun gives radiation, so it must be convection
All hot objects give out radiation, so the heater warms your face by radiation
Heat travelled up through your feet from the floor

remediation.representation: A thermal-camera style picture showing a glowing heater, a hot cup of chai and a person all giving out radiation
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to rank which gives out the most and connect 'hotter' with 'more radiation'

items.prompt_en: How does heat from the Sun reach the Earth?
items.prompt_hi: Sun ki garmi Earth tak kaise pahunchti hai?
items.answer: By radiation.
hints: Ask what lies between the Sun and the Earth
Point to almost empty space
Prompt: heat crosses empty space by ___
Assert: the Sun's heat reaches us by radiation

verified.solverAnswer: By radiation (through empty space).

items.prompt_en: Which colour of clothes is better to wear on a hot summer afternoon, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Garmi ki dopahar mein kis rang ke kapde pehenna behtar hai, aur kyon?
items.answer: Light colours such as white, because they reflect more sunlight and absorb less heat.
hints: Ask what colour clothes cricketers wear in test matches
Point to reflecting versus absorbing
Prompt: light colours ___ more sunlight
Assert: light-coloured clothes reflect sunlight and keep you cooler

verified.solverAnswer: Light colours (white): reflect more sunlight, absorb less heat, keeping you cooler.

items.prompt_en: Take two identical steel tumblers with the same amount of water. Wrap one in black cloth and one in white cloth, and keep both in the sun for 30 minutes. Predict which water will be warmer.
items.prompt_hi: Barabar paani wale do ek jaise steel ke gilaas lo. Ek ko kaale kapde mein aur ek ko safed kapde mein lapeto, aur dono ko 30 minute dhoop mein rakho. Guess karo kiska paani zyada garam hoga.
items.answer: The water in the black-wrapped tumbler, because black cloth absorbs more of the Sun's radiation.
hints: Ask for a guess and a reason
Point to which colour soaks up more sunlight
Prompt: black ___ more radiation
Assert: the black-wrapped water gets warmer

verified.solverAnswer: Water in black-wrapped tumbler is warmer; black absorbs more radiation.

items.prompt_en: Put one ice cube on a sheet of black paper and another on a sheet of white paper in the sun. Predict which melts first.
items.prompt_hi: Ek barf ka tukda kaale kaagaz pe aur doosra safed kaagaz pe dhoop mein rakho. Guess karo kaunsa pehle pighlega.
items.answer: The one on black paper, because the black paper absorbs more sunlight, warms up and passes heat into the ice.
hints: Ask for a guess before placing them
Point to which paper heats up more
Prompt: black paper ___ more sunlight and gets ___
Assert: the cube on black paper melts first

verified.solverAnswer: Ice on black paper melts first; black absorbs more heat.

items.prompt_en: On a spacewalk, an astronaut's suit faces the Sun on one side. There is no air in space. Predict: will the side of the suit facing the Sun get hot?
items.prompt_hi: Spacewalk ke dauraan astronaut ke suit ka ek hissa Sun ki taraf hai. Space mein hawa nahi hai. Guess karo: kya suit ka Sun wala hissa garam hoga?
items.answer: Yes, very hot, because radiation travels through empty space; that is why spacesuits are white and reflective, to reflect much of it.
hints: Ask whether heat needs air to travel by radiation
Point to why spacesuits are white
Prompt: radiation travels through ___ space
Assert: yes; radiation heats the suit even with no air

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, it gets hot; radiation travels through vacuum and is absorbed by the suit (suits are white/reflective to limit it).

items.prompt_en: Why is the inside of a solar cooker painted black, and why does it have a glass lid and a shiny reflector?
items.prompt_hi: Solar cooker ka andar ka hissa kaala kyon rang kiya jaata hai, aur usme kaanch ka dhakkan aur chamakdaar reflector kyon hota hai?
items.answer: Black absorbs as much sunlight as possible; the shiny reflector sends extra sunlight into the box; the glass lid lets sunlight in but traps the warm air so heat is not carried away.
hints: Ask what each part does to the sunlight
Point to black, shiny and glass parts
Prompt: black ___, the reflector ___, the glass ___
Assert: black absorbs, the reflector adds light, the glass traps the heat

verified.solverAnswer: Black absorbs maximum heat radiation; reflector directs more sunlight into the box; glass lid lets sunlight in and traps heat (greenhouse effect), cooking food.

items.prompt_en: Compare two identical houses in Rajasthan, one with a white-painted roof and one with a dark roof. Which stays cooler inside, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Rajasthan ke do ek jaise gharon ki tulna karo, ek ki chhat safed rang ki aur ek ki gehre rang ki. Kaunsa andar se zyada thanda rahega, aur kyon?
items.answer: The house with the white roof, because the white surface reflects more sunlight and absorbs less heat.
hints: Ask which roof would feel hotter to touch at noon
Point to reflection
Prompt: the white roof ___ more sunlight
Assert: the white-roofed house stays cooler

verified.solverAnswer: White-roofed house stays cooler as white reflects most sunlight, dark roof absorbs and heats the house.

items.prompt_en: In Ladakh's cold but sunny winters, many people like dark-coloured woollens. Why?
items.prompt_hi: Ladakh ki thandi par dhoop wali sardiyon mein bahut log gehre rang ke oonee kapde pasand karte hain. Kyon?
items.answer: Dark colours absorb more sunlight and warm the wearer, and wool traps air that keeps the body's heat in.
hints: Ask what dark colours do in sunlight
Point to wool trapping air too
Prompt: dark colours ___ more sunlight
Assert: dark woollens absorb sunlight and wool keeps heat in

verified.solverAnswer: Dark colours absorb more sunlight heat; wool traps body heat; so warmer in sun.

items.prompt_en: Why are petrol and oil storage tanks often painted white or silver?
items.prompt_hi: Petrol aur tel ke bade storage tank aksar safed ya silver rang ke kyon hote hain?
items.answer: To reflect sunlight and stay cooler, so the fuel inside does not heat up too much and evaporate or build up pressure.
hints: Ask what would happen to fuel in a hot black tank
Point to reflection
Prompt: white and silver ___ sunlight, keeping the fuel ___
Assert: light, shiny tanks reflect radiation and keep the fuel cool

verified.solverAnswer: White/silver reflects sunlight so fuel stays cool, preventing evaporation/fire hazard.

items.prompt_en: Lata writes: 'The Sun heats the air near it, and that hot air travels all the way to Earth.' What is the mistake?
items.prompt_hi: Lata likhti hai: 'Sun apne paas ki hawa ko garam karta hai, aur wo garam hawa Earth tak aati hai.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Space between the Sun and the Earth is almost empty, with no air to carry heat; the Sun's heat reaches us by radiation, which needs no material.
hints: Ask what is between the Sun and the Earth
Point to radiation needing no air
Prompt: space has no ___, so heat comes by ___
Assert: heat crosses empty space by radiation, not by hot air

verified.solverAnswer: Heat from Sun reaches Earth by radiation through empty space, not via hot air (no air in space).

items.prompt_en: Draw one kitchen scene that shows conduction, convection and radiation, and label each.
items.prompt_hi: Ek hi kitchen ka scene banao jismein conduction, convection aur radiation teeno dikhen, aur har ek pe label lagao.
items.answer: Conduction: heat passing through a tawa to a roti, or up a steel spoon in hot dal. Convection: hot water or steam rising in a pot. Radiation: warmth felt on your face standing beside (not over) the stove, or sunlight through the window.
hints: Invite them to draw the stove and a pot first
Point to a spoon, steam and a face nearby
Prompt: spoon shows ___, steam shows ___, warm face shows ___
Assert: conduction through solids, convection in rising fluids, radiation across the gap

verified.solverAnswer: Spoon in hot pot (conduction), steam/boiling water or hot air rising (convection), warmth felt on face/hand near stove flame without touching (radiation).

items.prompt_en: Explain to your younger sibling why her white school shirt feels cooler in the sun than her black jacket.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ya behen ko samjhao ki dhoop mein uski safed school shirt kaali jacket se thandi kyon lagti hai.
items.answer: The Sun's heat comes as radiation; white cloth reflects most of it while black cloth absorbs most of it and heats up, so the white shirt stays cooler.
hints: Invite them to start with how the Sun's heat travels
Point to reflect versus absorb
Prompt: white ___ and black ___ the radiation
Assert: white reflects, black absorbs, so white feels cooler

verified.solverAnswer: White reflects most sunlight, black absorbs more radiation and heats up, so white shirt feels cooler.

items.prompt_en: From last time: which way of heat transfer can work through empty space?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: garmi pahunchne ka kaunsa tareeka khaali space mein bhi kaam karta hai?
items.answer: Radiation.
hints: Ask how the Sun's heat reaches us
Point to the empty space between them
Prompt: only ___ crosses empty space
Assert: radiation

verified.solverAnswer: Radiation.

items.prompt_en: You sit a little to the side of a room heater, not above it, and still feel your face get warm. How does the heat reach you?
items.prompt_hi: Tum room heater ke thoda bagal mein baithe ho, upar nahi, phir bhi chehra garam lagta hai. Garmi tum tak kaise pahunchti hai?
items.answer: By radiation: the hot heater gives out radiation in all directions, which reaches your face directly.
hints: Ask whether warm air was rising towards your face from the side
Point to radiation spreading in all directions
Prompt: hot objects give out ___ in all directions
Assert: radiation from the heater warms your face

verified.solverAnswer: By radiation: hot heater gives out heat radiation in all directions; absorbed by your face.

So the black car gets hotter; in hot places, light colours keep cars cooler
