skills.title: Describe the water cycle: evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation and collection
Explain infiltration: rainwater seeping through soil into gaps in sand, gravel and rock to become groundwater; the water table and aquifers
Explain why groundwater levels fall (over-pumping, less recharge under concrete, fewer trees) and how to recharge them (rainwater harvesting, recharge pits, ponds)

expectations: Water keeps moving in a cycle: the Sun's heat evaporates water from seas, rivers and soil; plants give out water vapour (transpiration); the vapour rises, cools and condenses into tiny droplets that form clouds; and it falls as rain, snow or hail.
Some rainwater flows over the ground into streams, rivers and the sea; some seeps down through the soil (infiltration).

Infiltrated water fills tiny gaps between grains of sand and gravel and cracks in rocks; this is groundwater. The top of the water-filled layer is the water table, and a layer of rock or sand that holds usable groundwater is an aquifer.
Groundwater is mostly water held in the pores of soil and rock, like water in a sponge, not one big underground lake.
Wells and borewells draw up groundwater; when more is pumped out than rain puts back, the water table falls and wells dry up, especially in summer.
Rainwater harvesting, recharge pits, ponds, open soil and trees help recharge groundwater; concrete and tarred surfaces stop rain from soaking in.

misconceptions.belief: Underground water is a big lake under the ground.
signs: Draws groundwater as a blue cave lake
Thinks a borewell drills into an underground tank

diagnostic.prompt_en: If you could see the groundwater under a village, what would it mostly look like?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Agar tum gaon ke neeche ka groundwater dekh sakte, toh wo zyadatar kaisa dikhta?

options.text: A huge open lake inside a cave under the village
Water filling tiny gaps between grains of sand and gravel and cracks in rock, like water in a sponge
An underground river flowing like the Ganga

remediation.representation: A clear-bottle model with gravel, sand and soil layers, water visible only between the grains
remediation.moveShape: Pour water in and let the child point to where the 'groundwater' is: in the gaps, not in an open pool

misconceptions.belief: Groundwater never runs out.
signs: Says you can always just dig deeper
Is surprised that wells dry up

diagnostic.prompt_en: A town pumps out more groundwater every year than the rain puts back. What happens?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek shehar har saal jitna groundwater nikaalta hai, baarish usse kam waapas bharti hai. Kya hoga?

options.text: Nothing; groundwater is unlimited
The water table falls, and wells and borewells may dry up
The groundwater instantly becomes salty

remediation.representation: A 'bank account' slider: rain deposits versus pumping withdrawals, with the water table line moving
remediation.moveShape: Let the child set pumping higher than rain and watch the well bottom come above the water table

misconceptions.belief: Clouds are made of water vapour gas.
signs: Says clouds are 'steam' or 'vapour' floating
Cannot say what condensation makes

diagnostic.prompt_en: What are clouds made of?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Baadal kis cheez se bane hote hain?

options.text: Invisible water vapour gas
Tiny droplets of water (or bits of ice) formed when vapour cools
Smoke

remediation.representation: Kettle-spout comparison: the clear gap right at the spout (vapour) and the white mist a little above (droplets)
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child which part is like a cloud and why it became visible

items.prompt_en: Name the main steps of the water cycle.
items.prompt_hi: Jal chakra ke mukhya kadam batao.
items.answer: Evaporation (and transpiration from plants), condensation into clouds, precipitation as rain, snow or hail, and collection in rivers, seas and groundwater.
hints: Ask what the Sun does to puddles
Point to clouds and rain
Prompt: ___, condensation, ___, collection
Assert: evaporation, condensation, precipitation and collection

verified.solverAnswer: Evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection (runoff/infiltration).

items.prompt_en: What is groundwater, and what is the water table?
items.prompt_hi: Groundwater kya hota hai, aur water table kya hai?
items.answer: Groundwater is water stored in the tiny gaps in soil, sand, gravel and rock under the ground; the water table is the top level of the layer in which all those gaps are filled with water.
hints: Ask where well water comes from
Point to the gaps between sand grains
Prompt: groundwater fills the ___; the water table is the ___ of that layer
Assert: groundwater fills underground gaps; the water table is its top level

verified.solverAnswer: Groundwater is water stored in gaps between soil, sand, rock underground; water table is the upper level of that saturated zone.

items.prompt_en: Ask an adult to make a few small holes in the bottoms of three plastic cups. Fill one with gravel (small stones), one with sand and one with clay soil. Pour the same amount of water into each. Predict which lets the water through fastest and which slowest.
items.prompt_hi: Kisi bade se teen plastic ke cup ki tali mein kuch chhote chhed karwao. Ek mein bajri (chhote patthar), ek mein ret aur ek mein chikni mitti bharo. Har ek mein barabar paani daalo. Guess karo kaun paani sabse jaldi aur kaun sabse dheere nikaalega.
items.answer: Gravel fastest, then sand, and clay slowest, because bigger gaps between the pieces let water seep through faster.
hints: Ask for a guess before pouring
Point to the size of the gaps in each
Prompt: bigger gaps let water through ___
Assert: gravel fastest, sand next, clay slowest

verified.solverAnswer: Gravel fastest, sand next, clay slowest.

items.prompt_en: In a clear plastic bottle with its top cut off by an adult, make layers: gravel at the bottom, then sand, then soil. Pour water slowly on top. Predict where the water will collect and what it will look like.
items.prompt_hi: Ek saaf plastic ki bottle lo jiska upar ka hissa kisi bade ne kaat diya ho, aur usme parat banao: neeche bajri, phir ret, phir mitti. Upar se dheere dheere paani daalo. Guess karo paani kahaan ikattha hoga aur kaisa dikhega.
items.answer: It seeps down through the soil and sand and collects in the gaps between the stones at the bottom, filling the spaces, like an aquifer; no open lake forms.
acceptable: in the gravel at the bottom
hints: Ask for a guess before pouring
Point to the gaps between the stones
Prompt: water collects in the ___ between the stones
Assert: water fills the gaps at the bottom, like real groundwater

verified.solverAnswer: Water seeps down and collects in gaps at the bottom among gravel, visible as water level layer (muddy/filtered) like groundwater, not an underground lake.

items.prompt_en: Two neighbourhoods get the same rain. One has open soil, gardens and trees; the other is fully covered with concrete and roads. Predict where groundwater will be refilled more, and where more water will flood the streets.
items.prompt_hi: Do mohallon mein ek jaisi baarish hoti hai. Ek mein khuli mitti, bageeche aur ped hain; doosra poora concrete aur sadkon se dhaka hai. Guess karo kahaan groundwater zyada bharega, aur kahaan sadkon pe zyada paani bharega.
items.answer: The open-soil neighbourhood refills more groundwater because rain soaks in; in the concrete one, rain runs off, floods the streets and very little reaches the groundwater.
hints: Ask where rain can soak in
Point to concrete as a lid on the ground
Prompt: open soil lets water ___; concrete makes it ___ off
Assert: open soil recharges groundwater; concrete causes runoff and flooding

verified.solverAnswer: Open soil neighbourhood refills groundwater (infiltration); concrete one has runoff and floods streets.

items.prompt_en: Why do many borewells go dry in summer?
items.prompt_hi: Kai borewell garmi mein kyon sookh jaate hain?
items.answer: There is no rain for months to recharge the groundwater, while people pump out more water for drinking and farming; the water table falls below the bottom of the borewell.
acceptable: water table neeche chala jaata hai
hints: Ask what fills groundwater back up
Point to heavy pumping in summer
Prompt: no ___ and more pumping make the water table ___
Assert: without rain and with heavy pumping, the water table drops below the borewell

verified.solverAnswer: Little recharge (no rain) and heavy pumping lower the water table below the borewell depth.

items.prompt_en: Compare the clear gap right at the spout of a boiling kettle with the white mist a little above it. Which one is like a cloud, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Ubalti ketli ki tonti ke theek paas ke saaf hisse aur thoda upar dikhne wali safed dhundh ki tulna karo. Inmein se baadal jaisa kaun hai, aur kyon?
items.answer: The white mist is like a cloud: it is made of tiny water droplets that formed when the invisible water vapour cooled and condensed. The clear part right at the spout is water vapour gas, which we cannot see.
hints: Ask which part you can actually see
Point to vapour cooling a little way up
Prompt: the visible mist is tiny ___ formed when vapour ___
Assert: the white mist, made of condensed droplets, is like a cloud

verified.solverAnswer: The white mist above is like cloud: water vapour (invisible, clear gap) condenses into tiny water droplets as it cools.
verified.note: SAFETY (low): prompt has the child observe a boiling kettle's spout; add 'only with an adult, from a distance, never put hand/face in steam'.

items.prompt_en: A school collects rainwater from its roof through pipes into a recharge pit filled with stones and sand. How does this help the school's borewell?
items.prompt_hi: Ek school apni chhat ka baarish ka paani pipe se patthar aur ret bhare recharge pit mein ikattha karta hai. Isse school ke borewell ko kaise madad milti hai?
items.answer: Instead of running off, the rainwater seeps through the pit into the ground, adding to the groundwater and raising the water table near the borewell.
hints: Ask where the roof water went before the pit
Point to water seeping down through the pit
Prompt: the pit lets rainwater ___ and raises the ___
Assert: rainwater harvesting refills the groundwater the borewell uses

verified.solverAnswer: Rainwater percolates through pit into ground, recharging groundwater and raising water table so borewell gets water.

items.prompt_en: In parts of Punjab and Rajasthan, farmers now have to drill borewells much deeper than their grandparents' wells. Why might this be?
items.prompt_hi: Punjab aur Rajasthan ke kuch hisson mein kisaanon ko ab apne daada-pardaada ke kuon se kahin zyada gehre borewell khodne padte hain. Aisa kyon ho sakta hai?
items.answer: For years more groundwater has been pumped out, for example to irrigate thirsty crops, than rain has put back, so the water table has fallen deeper.
hints: Ask what happens when withdrawals exceed deposits
Point to irrigation pumps running for years
Prompt: more water was ___ than rain ___, so the water table ___
Assert: over-pumping has lowered the water table

verified.solverAnswer: Over-pumping for irrigation has exceeded recharge, lowering the water table.

items.prompt_en: Meenu's drawing shows a big blue lake in a cave under her village, labelled 'groundwater'. What would you change?
items.prompt_hi: Meenu ki drawing mein gaon ke neeche ek gufa mein bada neela taalab dikhaya gaya hai jis pe 'groundwater' likha hai. Tum kya badloge?
items.answer: Groundwater is mostly water filling the tiny gaps between grains of soil, sand and gravel and the cracks in rocks; she should draw layers of soil and rock with water in their spaces, with the water table as the top of the wet layer.
hints: Ask what the bottle model looked like
Point to water between the stones
Prompt: groundwater fills ___ between grains, like a ___
Assert: draw water in the pores of soil and rock, not a cave lake

verified.solverAnswer: Groundwater isn't a cave lake; it fills tiny spaces between sand, soil and rock (like water in a sponge); draw water level in porous layers.

items.prompt_en: Draw the water cycle as a loop with arrows linking the sea, the Sun, clouds, rain, a river, the soil, groundwater and a tree. Label each arrow with the right process.
items.prompt_hi: Jal chakra ko ek loop ke roop mein banao jismein teer samudra, Sun, baadal, baarish, nadi, mitti, groundwater aur ek ped ko jodein. Har teer pe sahi prakriya likho.
items.answer: Evaporation (sea to air), transpiration (tree to air), condensation (vapour to clouds), precipitation (clouds to land), runoff (land to river to sea), infiltration (soil to groundwater), and groundwater seeping into wells and rivers.
hints: Invite them to draw the sea and the Sun first
Point to the arrow going down into the soil
Prompt: sea to air is ___; soil to groundwater is ___
Assert: evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, runoff and infiltration complete the loop

verified.solverAnswer: Sea to air evaporation; plants transpiration; air to clouds condensation; clouds to ground precipitation; river runoff; soil to groundwater infiltration/percolation; back to sea.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your grandmother where the water in her village well comes from, and why the level rises after the monsoon.
items.prompt_hi: Apni daadi ya naani ko samjhao ki unke gaon ke kuen ka paani kahaan se aata hai, aur monsoon ke baad paani ka level kyon badh jaata hai.
items.answer: Rain seeps into the soil and fills the gaps in sand and rock underground; the well is dug below the water table, so groundwater seeps into it. The monsoon rain recharges the groundwater and raises the water table, so the well's level rises.
hints: Invite them to start with the raindrop soaking in
Point to the water table and the well bottom
Prompt: rain ___ into the ground and the monsoon raises the ___
Assert: wells fill from groundwater recharged by rain

verified.solverAnswer: Rain soaks into the ground and fills groundwater; well taps the water table; monsoon recharges it so level rises.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what is it called when rainwater seeps down into the ground?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jab baarish ka paani zameen mein ris ke neeche jaata hai, use kya kehte hain?
items.answer: Infiltration.
hints: Ask what happened in the gravel-sand-soil bottle
Point to water soaking in
Prompt: water soaking into the ground is ___
Assert: infiltration

verified.solverAnswer: Infiltration (percolation).

steps: The raindrop falls on the field: precipitation
It soaks into the soil through tiny gaps: infiltration

It reaches the layer where all the gaps are already full of water, below the water table, and becomes groundwater
The well is dug below the water table, so groundwater seeps into it and the family can draw it up

skills.title: Recall units of time (the second as the SI unit; minute, hour, day, year) and early timekeepers such as sundials, water clocks (ghati) and sand clocks
Define one oscillation and the time period of a pendulum, and measure the time period by timing many oscillations and dividing
Predict how thread length, bob mass and the size of the swing affect the time period

expectations: The SI unit of time is the second (s); 60 seconds make a minute and 60 minutes make an hour.
Before clocks, people measured time with sundials (like the giant Samrat Yantra at Jantar Mantar), water clocks such as the ghati, sand clocks and the movement of the Sun, Moon and stars.
A simple pendulum is a small heavy bob hanging from a thread; one complete to-and-fro swing, from one end to the other and back, is one oscillation, and the time it takes is the time period.
To measure the time period accurately, time 10 or 20 oscillations and divide the total time by that number.

The time period depends on the length of the thread: a longer pendulum swings more slowly (longer time period). It does not depend on the mass of the bob, and for small swings it hardly depends on how far the bob is pulled aside.
Because a pendulum of fixed length keeps a steady time period, pendulums were used to keep time in clocks.

misconceptions.belief: A heavier bob makes a pendulum swing faster.
signs: Predicts two keys will swing faster than one
Explains swing speed only by weight

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two pendulums have the same thread length; one has a light eraser as its bob and the other a heavy key. Which has the shorter time period?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Do pendulum ki dhaage ki lambaai barabar hai; ek mein halka rubber laga hai aur doosre mein bhaari chaabi. Kiska time period chhota hoga?

options.text: The heavy key, because heavier things swing faster
Both have about the same time period, because the bob's mass does not change it
The light eraser, because it is lighter

remediation.representation: Side-by-side pendulum simulation with a mass slider and a length slider, each showing the time period
remediation.moveShape: Let the child move only the mass slider first and watch the time period stay put, then move the length slider

misconceptions.belief: Pulling the bob farther aside makes the time period much longer (or much shorter).
signs: Says a bigger swing must take longer because it travels farther
Expects a small push to give a much quicker swing

diagnostic.prompt_en: You start a pendulum with a small pull to the side, then with a slightly bigger pull (still a small swing). What happens to the time period?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tum pendulum ko pehle thoda sa side mein kheench ke chhodte ho, phir thoda zyada (par abhi bhi chhota jhoola). Time period ka kya hota hai?

options.text: It becomes much longer because the bob travels farther
It stays nearly the same, because the bob also moves faster on the bigger swing
It becomes much shorter

remediation.representation: Two pendulums released together, one with a bigger swing, staying in step for many swings
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to count both together aloud and notice they keep the same beat

misconceptions.belief: One oscillation is a swing from one side to the other (only half the full to-and-fro).
signs: Counts 'one' each time the bob reaches either end
Gets a time period half the true value

diagnostic.prompt_en: What counts as one complete oscillation of a pendulum?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Pendulum ka ek poora oscillation kya kehlaata hai?

options.text: Going from the left end to the right end once
Going from one end to the other end and back again to the start
Any small movement of the bob

remediation.representation: A slowed animation of the bob that leaves a coloured trail for one full there-and-back, with the count ticking only at the return
remediation.moveShape: Have the child say 'and back' before counting each oscillation

items.prompt_en: What is the SI unit of time?
items.prompt_hi: Samay ki SI unit kya hai?
items.answer: The second (s).
hints: Ask what the shortest unit on a wall clock is
Point to the thin, fast hand
Prompt: the SI unit of time is the ___
Assert: the second

verified.solverAnswer: Second.

items.prompt_en: A pendulum completes 20 oscillations in 30 seconds. What is its time period?
items.prompt_hi: Ek pendulum 30 second mein 20 oscillations poore karta hai. Uska time period kitna hai?
items.answer: 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 seconds.
hints: Ask what the time period means
Point to dividing the total time by the number of oscillations
Prompt: time period = ___ ÷ ___
Assert: 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5 s

verified.solverAnswer: 1.5 seconds.

items.prompt_en: Tie a key to a 50 cm thread, hang it from a table edge and time 10 swings. Now tie two keys together on the same length of thread. Predict: will the time for 10 swings be shorter, longer or about the same?
items.prompt_hi: Ek chaabi ko 50 cm ke dhaage se baandho, mez ke kinaare se latkaao aur 10 jhoolon ka samay naapo. Ab do chaabiyan saath baandh ke wahi lambaai ka dhaaga rakho. Guess karo: 10 jhoolon ka samay kam hoga, zyada hoga ya lagbhag utna hi?
items.answer: About the same (around 14 seconds for 10 swings), because the bob's mass does not change the time period.
hints: Ask for a guess and a reason first
Point to the length staying the same
Prompt: changing the ___ does not change the time period
Assert: about the same; mass does not affect the time period

verified.solverAnswer: About the same; mass doesn't change the time period.

items.prompt_en: Now shorten the thread from 50 cm to 25 cm. Predict: will the pendulum swing faster or slower than before?
items.prompt_hi: Ab dhaage ko 50 cm se chhota karke 25 cm kar do. Guess karo: pendulum pehle se tez jhoolega ya dheere?
items.answer: Faster: a shorter pendulum has a shorter time period (about 1 second instead of about 1.4 seconds).
hints: Ask for a guess before shortening
Point to length being the thing that matters
Prompt: a ___ pendulum has a shorter time period
Assert: the shorter pendulum swings faster

verified.solverAnswer: Faster (shorter time period).

items.prompt_en: Predict: if you start the pendulum with a small pull versus a slightly bigger pull (still a small swing), will the time period change much?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar pendulum ko thoda sa kheench ke chhodo ya thoda zyada kheench ke (par abhi bhi chhota jhoola), toh kya time period mein zyada farak aayega?
items.answer: Hardly at all: for small swings the time period stays nearly the same, because on a bigger swing the bob also moves faster.
hints: Ask for a guess before releasing
Point to the bob speeding up on a bigger swing
Prompt: for small swings the time period stays ___
Assert: it barely changes for small swings

verified.solverAnswer: No, it stays nearly the same for small swings.

items.prompt_en: Why do we time 20 oscillations and divide by 20, instead of timing just one?
items.prompt_hi: Hum sirf ek oscillation ki jagah 20 oscillations ka samay naap ke 20 se bhaag kyon dete hain?
items.answer: One swing is too quick to time accurately because of our reaction time in starting and stopping the stopwatch; timing many swings spreads that error over all of them and gives a more accurate result.
hints: Ask how quickly they can press start and stop
Point to the same small error being shared by 20 swings
Prompt: timing many swings makes the result more ___
Assert: timing many oscillations reduces the effect of reaction-time errors

verified.solverAnswer: Reduces error from reaction time in starting and stopping the stopwatch, giving a more accurate average.

items.prompt_en: Compare a sundial and a pendulum clock. What does each depend on, and when would each fail?
items.prompt_hi: Sundial aur pendulum ghadi ki tulna karo. Har ek kis cheez pe nirbhar hai, aur kab kaam nahi karega?
items.answer: A sundial depends on the Sun's shadow, so it fails at night and on cloudy days; a pendulum clock depends on steady swings of a fixed length, so it works day and night but must stay still and be adjusted.
hints: Ask what a sundial needs to make a shadow
Point to the pendulum swinging in the dark too
Prompt: the sundial fails at ___; the pendulum keeps working if left ___
Assert: sundials need sunshine; pendulum clocks need steady swings

verified.solverAnswer: Sundial depends on the Sun's shadow (fails at night, cloudy days); pendulum clock depends on steady swinging with gravity and length (fails when it stops, needs winding, or length changes/temperature).

items.prompt_en: At the park, there is a long swing and a short swing. If children just sit and let each swing go to and fro by itself, which one goes to and fro more times in a minute?
items.prompt_hi: Park mein ek lamba jhoola hai aur ek chhota jhoola. Agar bachche bas baith jaayein aur jhoola apne aap aage-peeche ho, toh ek minute mein kaunsa zyada baar aage-peeche jaayega?
items.answer: The short swing, because a shorter length gives a shorter time period; how heavy each child is does not matter much.
hints: Ask what the swing has in common with a pendulum
Point to the length of the chains
Prompt: ___ chains give a shorter time period
Assert: the short swing swings more times per minute

verified.solverAnswer: The short swing.

items.prompt_en: An old grandfather clock has started running slow, losing time. Should the pendulum bob be moved up, making the pendulum shorter, or moved down? Explain.
items.prompt_hi: Ek purani pendulum wali badi ghadi dheere chalne lagi hai, samay peeche ho raha hai. Pendulum ke bob ko upar karna chahiye, yaani pendulum chhota karna, ya neeche? Samjhao.
items.answer: Move it up to shorten the pendulum; a shorter pendulum has a shorter time period, so it swings faster and the clock runs faster.
hints: Ask whether the clock needs to tick faster or slower
Point to length controlling the time period
Prompt: a ___ pendulum swings faster
Assert: shorten the pendulum so the clock speeds up

verified.solverAnswer: Move the bob up (shorten) so it swings faster.

items.prompt_en: Akash counted 'one' every time the bob reached the other side. He counted 20 in 15 seconds and wrote the time period as 0.75 s. What is the mistake?
items.prompt_hi: Akash har baar 'ek' ginta tha jab bob doosri taraf pahunchta tha. Usne 15 second mein 20 gine aur time period 0.75 s likha. Galti kya hai?
items.answer: He counted half-oscillations: 20 one-way swings are only 10 complete oscillations, so the time period is 15 ÷ 10 = 1.5 s.
hints: Ask what one complete oscillation is
Point to 'there and back' as one
Prompt: 20 one-way swings = ___ oscillations, so T = ___
Assert: T is 1.5 s; one oscillation is there and back

verified.solverAnswer: One oscillation is a to-and-fro (there and back); his 20 counts are 10 oscillations, so T = 15/10 = 1.5 s.

items.prompt_en: Here is a table. Thread length 25 cm, 50 cm, 100 cm; time for 10 oscillations 10 s, 14 s, 20 s. Describe in words what the table shows, and find each time period.
items.prompt_hi: Ye table dekho. Dhaage ki lambaai 25 cm, 50 cm, 100 cm; 10 oscillations ka samay 10 s, 14 s, 20 s. Shabdon mein batao table kya dikhaati hai, aur har ek ka time period nikaalo.
items.answer: Time periods: 1.0 s, 1.4 s and 2.0 s. The longer the thread, the longer the time period.
hints: Invite them to divide each time by 10
Point to how the period grows as length grows
Prompt: periods are ___, ___, ___; longer thread means ___ period
Assert: 1.0, 1.4 and 2.0 s; longer pendulums swing more slowly

verified.solverAnswer: Periods 1.0 s, 1.4 s, 2.0 s; the longer the thread, the longer the period.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend what changes a pendulum's time period and what does not, using your key-and-thread experiment.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chaabi-dhaage wale experiment se dost ko samjhao ki pendulum ka time period kis cheez se badalta hai aur kis se nahi.
items.answer: Changing the length changes the time period: shorter swings faster, longer swings slower. Changing the mass of the bob (one key or two) does not, and a slightly bigger small swing hardly does either.
hints: Invite them to start with what they changed in the experiment
Point to the two keys and the shorter thread
Prompt: ___ changes the period; ___ does not
Assert: length matters; mass and small swing size do not

verified.solverAnswer: Length changes it (longer = slower); mass of bob and small swing size don't.

items.prompt_en: From last time: what was the giant sundial at Jantar Mantar used for?
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Jantar Mantar ki vishaal sundial kis kaam aati thi?
items.answer: To tell the time of day from the position of its shadow (it is called the Samrat Yantra).
hints: Ask what a sundial uses to show time
Point to the moving shadow
Prompt: it tells the time from the position of its ___
Assert: it tells the time of day from its shadow

verified.solverAnswer: It told the time of day from the shadow of its gnomon (and was used for astronomy).

skills.title: Define speed as the distance covered in a unit of time, with units m/s and km/h
Calculate speed = distance ÷ time, and use it to find distance or time
Compare speeds of objects that travel different distances in different times
Convert between km/h and m/s (1 km/h = 5/18 m/s) and read a speedometer and an odometer

expectations: Speed tells how fast something moves: the distance it covers in a unit of time.
Speed = distance ÷ time; the SI unit is metres per second (m/s), and kilometres per hour (km/h) is also common.
To compare speeds, compare the distance covered in the same time (or the time taken for the same distance); something that travels farther is not faster if it took longer.
Speed often changes during a journey, so we usually calculate average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
A speedometer shows the speed at that moment; an odometer shows the total distance travelled.
1 km/h = 1000 m ÷ 3600 s = 5/18 m/s; for example, 36 km/h = 10 m/s.

misconceptions.belief: The vehicle that travels farther is always faster.
signs: Chooses the bigger distance without looking at time
Says the bus that went 120 km must be faster than the car that went 100 km

diagnostic.prompt_en: A bus travels 120 km in 3 hours. A car travels 100 km in 2 hours. Which is faster?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek bus 3 ghante mein 120 km jaati hai. Ek car 2 ghante mein 100 km jaati hai. Kaun tez hai?

options.text: The bus, because it went farther
The car: 50 km/h is faster than the bus's 40 km/h
Both are equally fast

remediation.representation: A two-lane race track that shows both vehicles after each hour, with distance markers
remediation.moveShape: Freeze the animation at the 1-hour mark and ask who is ahead then

misconceptions.belief: Speed and distance mean the same thing.
signs: Reads 40 km/h on a speedometer as '40 km travelled'
Answers a speed question with a distance

diagnostic.prompt_en: A scooter's speedometer shows 40 km/h. What does this mean?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Scooter ka speedometer 40 km/h dikha raha hai. Iska matlab kya hai?

options.text: The scooter has travelled 40 km so far
If it kept this speed for one hour, it would cover 40 km
It will take 40 hours to reach

remediation.representation: A dashboard picture with the speedometer and the odometer side by side, each labelled with what it measures
remediation.moveShape: Point to each dial in turn and ask the child to say 'how fast' or 'how far'

misconceptions.belief: Speed is found by dividing time by distance, or by multiplying them.
signs: Writes speed = time ÷ distance
Multiplies distance by time to get speed

diagnostic.prompt_en: A cyclist goes 30 km in 2 hours. Which calculation gives the speed?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek cyclist 2 ghante mein 30 km jaata hai. Kaunsa hisaab speed dega?

remediation.representation: A unit check: km/h means 'km per h', so the km number goes on top and the hours below
remediation.moveShape: Have the child read the unit aloud, then build the division from it

items.prompt_en: A train covers 240 km in 3 hours. What is its average speed?
items.prompt_hi: Ek train 3 ghante mein 240 km tay karti hai. Uski average speed kitni hai?
hints: Ask what speed means in words
Point to distance and time
Prompt: speed = 240 ÷ ___
Assert: 240 ÷ 3 = 80 km/h

verified.solverAnswer: 80 km/h.

items.prompt_en: Rani walks 600 m in 10 minutes. What is her speed in metres per minute, and in metres per second?
items.prompt_hi: Rani 10 minute mein 600 m chalti hai. Uski speed metre per minute mein kitni hai, aur metre per second mein kitni?
items.answer: 600 ÷ 10 = 60 m per minute; 60 m in 60 seconds = 1 m/s.
hints: Ask how many seconds are in a minute
Point to dividing distance by time
Prompt: 600 ÷ 10 = ___ m/min; that is ___ m/s
Assert: 60 m per minute, which is 1 m/s

verified.solverAnswer: 60 m/min; 1 m/s.

items.prompt_en: Before calculating, predict who is faster: Ajay, who runs 100 m in 20 s, or Bina, who runs 60 m in 10 s. Then check by calculating.
items.prompt_hi: Hisaab lagaane se pehle guess karo kaun tez hai: Ajay, jo 100 m 20 second mein daudta hai, ya Bina, jo 60 m 10 second mein daudti hai. Phir hisaab se check karo.
items.answer: Bina: her speed is 60 ÷ 10 = 6 m/s, while Ajay's is 100 ÷ 20 = 5 m/s.
hints: Ask for a guess before any calculation
Point to their distances in the same time
Prompt: Bina's speed is ___ m/s; Ajay's is ___ m/s
Assert: Bina is faster at 6 m/s against 5 m/s

verified.solverAnswer: Bina is faster: 6 m/s vs Ajay's 5 m/s.

items.prompt_en: A car's odometer reads 12,500 km before a trip and 12,680 km after. The trip took 3 hours. Predict: must the speedometer have shown 60 km/h the whole time?
items.prompt_hi: Ek car ka odometer safar se pehle 12,500 km aur baad mein 12,680 km dikhata hai. Safar 3 ghante ka tha. Guess karo: kya speedometer poore samay 60 km/h hi dikhata raha hoga?
items.answer: No. The average speed was 180 ÷ 3 = 60 km/h, but the speedometer showed different speeds at different moments: slower in traffic, faster on the highway.
hints: Ask what the odometer and the speedometer each measure
Point to traffic and highways on one trip
Prompt: 180 ÷ 3 = 60 is the ___ speed
Assert: 60 km/h is the average; the actual speed kept changing

verified.solverAnswer: No; 180 km / 3 h = 60 km/h is only the average speed; the actual speed varied.

items.prompt_en: Two trains leave at the same time for a city 300 km away. Train A's average speed is 100 km/h and train B's is 75 km/h. Predict how much earlier train A arrives, then calculate.
items.prompt_hi: Do trainein ek hi samay 300 km door ek shehar ke liye chalti hain. Train A ki average speed 100 km/h hai aur train B ki 75 km/h. Guess karo train A kitni pehle pahunchegi, phir hisaab lagao.
items.answer: Train A takes 300 ÷ 100 = 3 hours and train B takes 300 ÷ 75 = 4 hours, so A arrives 1 hour earlier.
hints: Ask how to find time from distance and speed
Point to time = distance ÷ speed
Prompt: A takes ___ h, B takes ___ h
Assert: 3 hours against 4 hours, so A is 1 hour earlier

verified.solverAnswer: A takes 3 h, B takes 4 h; A arrives 1 hour earlier.

items.prompt_en: Why does a speedometer reading of 50 km/h NOT mean the car has travelled 50 km?
items.prompt_hi: Speedometer pe 50 km/h dikhne ka matlab ye kyon NAHI hai ki car 50 km chal chuki hai?
items.answer: It shows how fast the car is going at that moment, meaning it would cover 50 km in one hour at that speed; the distance already travelled is shown by the odometer.
hints: Ask what 'per hour' means
Point to the odometer as the distance dial
Prompt: the speedometer shows how ___; the odometer shows how ___
Assert: speed is how fast; distance is how far, on the odometer

verified.solverAnswer: Speedometer shows how fast right now (rate per hour), not distance covered; distance is shown by the odometer; 50 km would only be covered after one hour at that speed.

items.prompt_en: Compare: a cheetah sprints 300 m in 12 s; a horse gallops 2 km (2000 m) in 2.5 minutes (150 s). Which moves at the greater speed?
items.prompt_hi: Tulna karo: ek cheetah 12 second mein 300 m daudta hai; ek ghoda 2.5 minute (150 second) mein 2 km (2000 m) daudta hai. Kiski speed zyada hai?
items.answer: The cheetah: 300 ÷ 12 = 25 m/s, while the horse's speed is 2000 ÷ 150 ≈ 13.3 m/s.
hints: Ask how to compare when distances and times both differ
Point to working out m/s for each
Prompt: cheetah ___ m/s, horse about ___ m/s
Assert: the cheetah is faster at 25 m/s

verified.solverAnswer: Cheetah: 300/12 = 25 m/s; horse: 2000/150 = about 13.3 m/s; cheetah is faster.

items.prompt_en: A school bus travels at an average speed of 30 km/h. The school is 15 km away. How long does the trip take?
items.prompt_hi: Ek school bus ki average speed 30 km/h hai. School 15 km door hai. Safar mein kitna samay lagega?
items.answer: Time = 15 ÷ 30 = 0.5 hour = 30 minutes.
hints: Ask which is unknown: distance, speed or time
Point to time = distance ÷ speed
Prompt: time = 15 ÷ ___
Assert: 0.5 hour, which is 30 minutes

verified.solverAnswer: 0.5 hour = 30 minutes.

items.prompt_en: In a cricket match, a fast bowler's delivery is shown as 144 km/h. How many metres does the ball travel in one second? About how long does it take to cover the 20 m pitch?
items.prompt_hi: Cricket match mein ek tez gendbaaz ki ball 144 km/h dikhaayi gayi. Ball ek second mein kitne metre jaati hai? 20 m ki pitch tay karne mein lagbhag kitna samay lagta hai?
items.answer: 144 × 5/18 = 40 m/s; 20 ÷ 40 = 0.5 s, about half a second.
hints: Ask how to change km/h into m/s
Point to multiplying by 5/18
Assert: 40 m/s, so about 0.5 s down the pitch

verified.solverAnswer: 144 km/h = 40 m/s; about 0.5 s to cover 20 m.

items.prompt_en: Kiran calculated: 'A cyclist goes 45 km in 3 hours, so the speed is 3 ÷ 45 = 0.067 km/h.' Find the mistake.
items.prompt_hi: Kiran ne hisaab lagaaya: 'Ek cyclist 3 ghante mein 45 km jaata hai, toh speed 3 ÷ 45 = 0.067 km/h.' Galti dhoondo.
items.answer: She divided time by distance. Speed = distance ÷ time = 45 ÷ 3 = 15 km/h.
acceptable: doori ko samay se bhaag dena tha
hints: Ask what the unit km/h tells you to put on top
Point to km over hours
Prompt: speed = ___ ÷ ___
Assert: 45 ÷ 3 = 15 km/h

verified.solverAnswer: Speed = distance/time, so 45 km / 3 h = 15 km/h; Kiran inverted it.

items.prompt_en: Draw a number line from 0 to 200 km and mark where a car moving at a steady 50 km/h will be after 1, 2, 3 and 4 hours. What do you notice about the gaps between the marks?
items.prompt_hi: 0 se 200 km tak ek number line banao aur mark karo ki 50 km/h ki ek-si speed se chalti car 1, 2, 3 aur 4 ghante baad kahaan hogi. Marks ke beech ke gaps ke baare mein kya dikhta hai?
items.answer: At 50, 100, 150 and 200 km; the gaps are all equal, 50 km for each hour, because the speed stays the same.
hints: Invite them to mark the first hour first
Point to adding 50 each hour
Prompt: marks at 50, ___, ___, 200, with gaps of ___ km
Assert: equal 50 km gaps each hour show a steady speed

verified.solverAnswer: Marks at 50, 100, 150, 200 km; gaps equal (50 km each) since steady speed.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger sibling how to decide which of two runners is faster when they ran different distances in different times.
items.prompt_hi: Apne chhote bhai ya behen ko samjhao ki agar do runners ne alag-alag doori alag-alag samay mein daudi ho, toh kaun tez hai ye kaise tay karein.
items.answer: Work out each runner's speed by dividing the distance by the time, for example in metres per second, and compare those; the one with the bigger speed is faster, not the one who ran farther.
hints: Invite them to start with the formula
Point to comparing the same unit for both
Prompt: speed = ___ ÷ ___ for each runner, then compare
Assert: compare speeds, not distances

verified.solverAnswer: Compute speed = distance / time for each in the same units and compare; the larger speed is faster.

items.prompt_en: From last time: write the formula for speed and its SI unit.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: speed ka formula aur uski SI unit likho.
items.answer: Speed = distance ÷ time; the SI unit is metres per second (m/s).
hints: Ask what speed measures
Point to 'per second'
Prompt: speed = ___ ÷ ___, in ___
Assert: speed = distance ÷ time, in m/s

verified.solverAnswer: Speed = distance / time; SI unit m/s.

workedExample.problem: A car travels 150 km in 2 hours 30 minutes. Find its average speed.
steps: Write what is known: distance = 150 km, time = 2 hours 30 minutes
Change the time into hours: 30 minutes = 0.5 hour, so the time is 2.5 hours
Use speed = distance ÷ time
The average speed is 60 km/h
fadedVersion: Write what is known: distance = ___ km, time = 2 h 30 min
30 minutes = ___ hour, so the time is 2.5 hours
Use speed = ___ ÷ ___
The average speed is ___ km/h

skills.title: Define uniform linear motion (equal distances in equal intervals of time along a straight line) and non-uniform motion
Decide from a distance-time table or position marks whether a motion is uniform
Recognise that most everyday motion is non-uniform and use average speed to describe it

expectations: An object in uniform linear motion moves along a straight line covering equal distances in equal intervals of time, so its speed stays the same.
In non-uniform motion the object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time; its speed changes.
To decide, look at the distance covered in each equal time interval (from a table or from position marks), not just at whether the object keeps moving or at the total distance.
Most everyday motion is non-uniform, such as an auto in city traffic, a falling ball or a marble slowing down; a train on a long straight track at steady speed is nearly uniform.
For non-uniform motion we use average speed = total distance ÷ total time.

misconceptions.belief: Motion is uniform whenever an object keeps moving without stopping.
signs: Calls an auto in traffic uniform because it never stopped
Ignores speeding up and slowing down

diagnostic.prompt_en: An auto keeps moving for 10 minutes without stopping, but it speeds up and slows down in traffic. Is its motion uniform?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek auto 10 minute bina ruke chalta hai, par traffic mein tez aur dheere hota rehta hai. Kya uski gati ek-samaan (uniform) hai?

options.text: Yes, because it never stopped
No, because it covers different distances in equal intervals of time
Yes, because it is on a road

remediation.representation: A strobe picture of a car's positions every second: evenly spaced dots for uniform, bunched and stretched dots for non-uniform
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to measure the gaps between dots rather than just look at whether dots continue

misconceptions.belief: If two objects cover the same total distance in the same total time, both must be in uniform motion.
signs: Looks only at the totals in a table
Says the same average speed means the same kind of motion

diagnostic.prompt_en: Two cyclists both cover 600 m in 3 minutes. Cyclist A covers 200 m each minute. Cyclist B covers 100 m, then 200 m, then 300 m. Which one is in uniform motion?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Do cyclist dono 3 minute mein 600 m chalte hain. Cyclist A har minute 200 m chalta hai. Cyclist B pehle 100 m, phir 200 m, phir 300 m chalta hai. Kaun uniform gati mein hai?

options.text: Both, because both covered 600 m in 3 minutes
Only A
Only B

remediation.representation: A table with a highlighted 'distance in this minute' column next to the cumulative column
remediation.moveShape: Have the child fill the per-minute column before deciding

misconceptions.belief: Uniform motion means slow motion; fast motion cannot be uniform.
signs: Says a plane is too fast to be uniform
Links 'uniform' with 'gentle'

diagnostic.prompt_en: A plane flies at a steady 900 km/h in a straight line. Is that uniform motion?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek hawaai jahaaz seedhi line mein ek-si 900 km/h ki speed se udta hai. Kya ye uniform gati hai?

options.text: No, it is far too fast to be uniform
Yes, because its speed stays the same along a straight line
Only if it flies slowly

remediation.representation: Two strobe strips, one with tiny equal gaps (slow) and one with huge equal gaps (fast)
remediation.moveShape: Ask what both strips have in common, separating 'how fast' from 'steady or changing'

items.prompt_en: What is uniform linear motion?
items.prompt_hi: Uniform linear motion kya hoti hai?
items.answer: Motion along a straight line in which an object covers equal distances in equal intervals of time, so its speed stays the same.
acceptable: constant speed in a straight line
hints: Ask what 'uniform' means in a school uniform
Point to 'the same every time'
Prompt: equal ___ in equal intervals of ___
Assert: equal distances in equal times along a straight line

verified.solverAnswer: Motion in a straight line covering equal distances in equal intervals of time (constant speed).

items.prompt_en: A car's total distance from the start after each minute is 1 km, 2 km, 3 km and 4 km. Is its motion uniform? How do you know?
items.prompt_hi: Ek car ki shuruaat se kul doori har minute ke baad 1 km, 2 km, 3 km aur 4 km hai. Kya uski gati uniform hai? Kaise pata?
items.answer: Yes, it covers 1 km in every minute, which is equal distances in equal times.
hints: Ask how far it went in each single minute
Point to subtracting one reading from the next
Prompt: each minute it covers ___ km
Assert: uniform, because it covers 1 km every minute

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, uniform: covers 1 km each minute (equal distances in equal times).

items.prompt_en: A marble is rolled along a long, smooth floor and slowly comes to a stop. Before measuring, predict: will it cover the same distance in every second?
items.prompt_hi: Ek kanche ko lambe, chikne farsh pe ludhkaaya jaata hai aur wo dheere dheere ruk jaata hai. Naapne se pehle guess karo: kya wo har second barabar doori tay karega?
items.answer: No: it covers less distance each second as it slows down, so its motion is non-uniform.
hints: Ask for a guess before the roll
Point to it slowing down
Prompt: as it slows, it covers ___ distance each second
Assert: no; a slowing marble is in non-uniform motion

verified.solverAnswer: No; it slows, so covers less distance each second (non-uniform).

items.prompt_en: Predict which is closer to uniform motion: a metro train between two far-apart stations at its steady top speed, or a cricket ball from the moment it leaves the bowler's hand until the batter hits it.
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo kaun uniform gati ke zyada kareeb hai: do door-door stations ke beech apni ek-si top speed pe chalti metro, ya bowler ke haath se nikalne se batsman ke maarne tak cricket ki ball.
items.answer: The metro at its steady top speed on a straight stretch; the ball slows down, bounces and changes direction, so its motion is non-uniform.
hints: Ask for a guess and a reason
Point to the bounce of the ball
Prompt: the ___ keeps a steady speed; the ball ___ and bounces
Assert: the metro at steady speed is nearly uniform; the ball is not

verified.solverAnswer: The metro at steady speed is closer to uniform; the ball slows down, bounces, changes speed.

items.prompt_en: Imagine dropping a small ball and taking a photo every tenth of a second as it falls. Predict: will the gaps between the ball's positions be equal, growing or shrinking?
items.prompt_hi: Socho ek chhoti ball giraayi aur girte waqt har second ke dasve hisse mein uski photo li. Guess karo: ball ki jagahon ke beech ke gap barabar honge, badhte jaayenge ya ghatte jaayenge?
items.answer: Growing: the falling ball speeds up, covering more distance in each equal interval, so its motion is non-uniform.
hints: Ask for a guess before showing the strobe picture
Point to the ball speeding up as it falls
Prompt: it covers ___ distance in each interval
Assert: the gaps grow; a falling ball speeds up

verified.solverAnswer: Gaps grow; the ball speeds up as it falls.

items.prompt_en: Why do we use 'average speed' to describe a bus journey from Delhi to Agra?
items.prompt_hi: Delhi se Agra ki bus yaatra batane ke liye 'average speed' kyon use karte hain?
items.answer: The bus's speed keeps changing because of traffic, stops and open highway, so its motion is non-uniform; average speed, total distance ÷ total time, sums up the whole trip in one number.
hints: Ask whether the bus moves at one speed the whole way
Point to stops and highways
Prompt: the motion is ___, so we use total ___ ÷ total time
Assert: speed changes, so average speed describes the whole trip

verified.solverAnswer: The bus's speed changes (stops, traffic, highway), so average speed (total distance / total time) describes the whole journey.

items.prompt_en: Runner P is at 50 m, 100 m, 150 m and 200 m after each 10 s. Runner Q is at 30 m, 90 m, 150 m and 200 m after each 10 s. Both finish 200 m in 40 s. Compare their motions.
items.prompt_hi: Runner P har 10 second baad 50 m, 100 m, 150 m aur 200 m pe hai. Runner Q har 10 second baad 30 m, 90 m, 150 m aur 200 m pe hai. Dono 200 m 40 second mein poora karte hain. Dono ki gati ki tulna karo.
items.answer: P is in uniform motion, covering 50 m in every 10 s. Q is in non-uniform motion, covering 30 m, 60 m, 60 m and 50 m. They have the same average speed of 5 m/s.
hints: Ask how far each runner went in each 10 s
Point to subtracting each reading from the next
Prompt: P covers ___ each time; Q covers ___
Assert: P is uniform, Q is not, though both average 5 m/s

verified.solverAnswer: P covers 50 m every 10 s: uniform. Q covers 30, 60, 60, 50 m: non-uniform. Both average 5 m/s.

items.prompt_en: An auto in city traffic and a train on a long straight track at steady speed: which is in uniform motion and which is not? Why?
items.prompt_hi: Shehar ke traffic mein auto aur lambi seedhi patri pe ek-si speed se chalti train: kaun uniform gati mein hai aur kaun nahi? Kyon?
items.answer: The train is (nearly) uniform because it covers equal distances in equal times on a straight track; the auto is non-uniform because it keeps speeding up, slowing and stopping.
hints: Ask what the auto does at every signal
Point to the train's steady speed
Prompt: the train covers ___ distances in equal times; the auto does ___
Assert: train nearly uniform, auto non-uniform

verified.solverAnswer: Train at steady speed nearly uniform; auto in traffic non-uniform (stops and starts).

items.prompt_en: A car's cruise control keeps it at exactly 80 km/h on a straight highway. Then it reaches a toll plaza. Describe how its motion changes from uniform to non-uniform.
items.prompt_hi: Ek car ka cruise control use seedhe highway pe theek 80 km/h pe rakhta hai. Phir wo toll plaza pe pahunchti hai. Batao uski gati uniform se non-uniform kaise ho jaati hai.
items.answer: On the straight highway at a steady 80 km/h it is in uniform motion; slowing down to stop at the toll and then speeding up again is non-uniform motion.
acceptable: steady then slowing and speeding up
hints: Ask what the car does approaching the toll
Point to braking and speeding up again
Prompt: steady 80 km/h is ___; slowing and speeding up is ___
Assert: uniform on cruise control, non-uniform at the toll

verified.solverAnswer: On cruise control it covers equal distances in equal times (uniform); approaching toll it slows, stops, accelerates, so unequal distances (non-uniform).

items.prompt_en: Rina says: 'The bus went 60 km in 2 hours, so it must have gone exactly 30 km in each hour; that is uniform motion.' What is the mistake?
items.prompt_hi: Rina kehti hai: 'Bus ne 2 ghante mein 60 km tay kiye, toh har ghante theek 30 km gayi hogi; ye uniform gati hai.' Galti kya hai?
items.answer: Total distance and total time give only the average speed; the bus might have gone 40 km in the first hour and 20 km in the second. You need the distance in each interval to decide.
hints: Ask whether another split of 60 km is possible
Point to 40 km then 20 km
Prompt: totals only give the ___ speed
Assert: you need each hour's distance; totals cannot show uniform motion

verified.solverAnswer: Totals only give average speed; may have been 40 km then 20 km; need each hour's distance to show uniform motion.

items.prompt_en: On a distance-time graph, one line is perfectly straight and rising; another line curves. Which shows uniform motion and why? Describe what a table of readings would look like for each.
items.prompt_hi: Ek distance-time graph pe ek line bilkul seedhi upar jaati hai; doosri line mudi hui hai. Kaun uniform gati dikhati hai aur kyon? Har ek ke liye readings ki table kaisi dikhegi, batao.
items.answer: The straight line shows uniform motion: distance increases by the same amount in each equal time, so the table shows equal jumps. The curved line shows non-uniform motion: the jumps in distance change from one interval to the next.
hints: Invite them to read off distances at equal time steps
Point to equal versus changing jumps
Prompt: a straight line means ___ jumps; a curve means ___ jumps
Assert: straight line is uniform; curved line is non-uniform

verified.solverAnswer: Straight rising line: uniform (equal distance in equal time; table with equal jumps); curved line: non-uniform (changing jumps).

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend how you could check, using a stopwatch and chalk marks, whether a toy car moves uniformly.
items.prompt_hi: Apne dost ko samjhao ki stopwatch aur chalk ke nishaan se kaise check karoge ki ek khilauna car uniform gati se chalti hai ya nahi.
items.answer: Mark the car's position on the floor every equal interval of time (for example every 2 seconds), then measure the distances between the marks; if they are all equal along a straight line, the motion is uniform, otherwise it is non-uniform.
hints: Invite them to say what to mark and when
Point to measuring between marks
Prompt: mark every ___ seconds and compare the ___ between marks
Assert: equal gaps for equal times means uniform motion

verified.solverAnswer: Mark positions of car at every 1 second (or after equal time intervals) with chalk and measure gaps; equal gaps = uniform.

items.prompt_en: From last time: give one example of non-uniform motion from everyday life.
items.prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: rozmarra ki zindagi se non-uniform gati ka ek example do.
items.answer: For example: an auto or bus in traffic, a ball falling or thrown up, a marble slowing down, a cyclist on a hilly road, a train leaving a station.
hints: Ask about a bus near a bus stop
Point to speeding up and slowing down
Prompt: anything that ___ up or slows down
Assert: an auto in traffic is non-uniform motion

verified.solverAnswer: Auto/bus in traffic, a car stopping at a signal, a falling ball, a ball rolling to stop.

workedExample.problem: Decide whether this scooter moves uniformly. Its distance from the start after each minute: 0.5 km, 1.0 km, 1.6 km, 2.0 km.
steps: Find the distance covered in each single minute: 0.5, 0.5, 0.6 and 0.4 km
Compare the distances covered in these equal time intervals
They are not all equal
So the scooter's motion is non-uniform
Its average speed = 2.0 km ÷ 4 min = 0.5 km per minute, which is 30 km/h
fadedVersion: Find the distance in each minute: 0.5, 0.5, ___ and ___ km
Compare the distances in ___ time intervals
They are not all ___
So the motion is ___
Average speed = 2.0 km ÷ ___ min = 0.5 km per minute

skills.title: Name the parts of the digestive tract in order: mouth, food pipe (oesophagus), stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus
Describe what happens to food at each stage (chewing and saliva, churning and stomach juices, completion of digestion and absorption in the small intestine, water absorption in the large intestine)
Explain the role of digestive juices from the liver (bile) and pancreas, and why digestion is needed

expectations: Digestion breaks complex food into simple, soluble substances that the body can absorb and use.
Digestion begins in the mouth: teeth break food into small pieces and saliva starts changing starch into sugar, which is why a roti chewed for long tastes sweet.
The food pipe (oesophagus) pushes food down to the stomach by wave-like squeezing movements of its walls.
In the stomach, food is churned and mixed with acid and digestive juices that begin digesting proteins; a layer of mucus protects the stomach wall.

Most digestion is completed in the small intestine, using juices from its own walls, bile from the liver and juice from the pancreas; digested food is absorbed into the blood through finger-like villi on its inner wall.
The large intestine absorbs water and some salts from the undigested remains; waste is stored in the rectum and passed out through the anus.

misconceptions.belief: Food goes straight from the mouth to the stomach unchanged; nothing happens in the mouth.
signs: Says chewing only makes food smaller and has no chemical effect
Is surprised that a long-chewed roti tastes sweet
Skips the food pipe when listing the path

diagnostic.prompt_en: You chew a piece of plain roti for a full minute without swallowing. It starts tasting slightly sweet. Why?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tum saadi roti ka tukda ek minute tak chabaate ho bina nigle. Woh thoda meetha lagne lagta hai. Kyun?

options.text: Saliva starts changing the starch in roti into sugar
Nothing happens in the mouth; the sweet taste is imagination
The teeth add sugar to the roti

remediation.representation: A three-panel strip: roti (starch), chewing with saliva, sugar, with a taste meter rising
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to try the long-chew test at their next meal and report the taste, then link it to saliva

misconceptions.belief: All digestion happens in the stomach.
signs: Says 'the stomach digests the food' and stops there
Cannot say what the small intestine does
Thinks the intestines only carry waste

diagnostic.prompt_en: Where is the digestion of food completed and the digested food absorbed into the blood?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Khaane ka digestion kahaan poora hota hai aur digested khaana khoon mein kahaan absorb hota hai?

options.text: In the stomach
In the small intestine
In the large intestine

remediation.representation: A labelled tract diagram with a progress bar of 'how much digested' that fills only partly in the stomach and fully in the small intestine
remediation.moveShape: Walk the food bite through each organ; at each, ask what is still left undigested

misconceptions.belief: The stomach's acid would burn the stomach itself, or the stomach is just a storage bag.
signs: Asks why the stomach does not dissolve itself
Describes the stomach only as a bag that holds food

diagnostic.prompt_en: The stomach contains acid, yet the stomach wall is not harmed. Why?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Pet (stomach) mein acid hota hai, phir bhi stomach ki deewar ko nuksaan nahi hota. Kyun?

options.text: The stomach has no acid at all
A layer of mucus lines and protects the stomach wall
The stomach is only a storage bag, so acid does not matter

remediation.representation: A cross-section of the stomach wall with a mucus layer shown as a shield
remediation.moveShape: Contrast the stomach's jobs: churn, mix with acid and juices, protect itself with mucus

items.prompt_en: Take a small piece of plain roti or boiled rice and chew it slowly for one full minute before swallowing. Before you try, predict: will the taste stay the same, become sour, or become sweet?
items.prompt_hi: Saadi roti ya ubla chaawal ka chhota tukda lo aur nigalne se pehle ek poora minute dheere-dheere chabaao. Try karne se pehle guess karo: swaad waisa hi rahega, khatta ho jaayega, ya meetha?
items.answer: It becomes slightly sweet, because saliva changes some of the starch into sugar.
hints: Ask for a guess and a reason first
Point to the saliva mixing with the food
Prompt: saliva changes starch into ___
Assert: sweet, because saliva turns starch into sugar

verified.solverAnswer: It becomes sweet; saliva (amylase) turns starch into sugar.

items.prompt_en: Put these in the order food travels: stomach, mouth, large intestine, food pipe, small intestine.
items.prompt_hi: Inhe us order mein lagaao jismein khaana chalta hai: stomach, munh, large intestine, food pipe, small intestine.
items.answer: Mouth, food pipe (oesophagus), stomach, small intestine, large intestine (then rectum and anus).
acceptable: mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine, large intestine
hints: Ask where food enters first
Point to the tube that connects the mouth to the stomach
Prompt: mouth, ___, stomach, ___, large intestine
Assert: mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine, large intestine

verified.solverAnswer: Mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine, large intestine.

items.prompt_en: Astronauts in space, with no 'down', can still swallow food and it reaches their stomach. Predict how, before you hear the answer.
items.prompt_hi: Space mein astronauts ke liye koi 'neeche' nahi hota, phir bhi woh khaana nigal lete hain aur woh pet tak pahunchta hai. Jawaab sunne se pehle guess karo kaise.
items.answer: The walls of the food pipe squeeze in waves and push the food along, so food moves even without gravity.
hints: Ask what could push food if gravity does not pull it
Point to the muscles in the food pipe wall
Prompt: the food pipe walls ___ the food along
Assert: wave-like squeezing of the food pipe pushes food down

verified.solverAnswer: Food pipe walls squeeze in waves (peristalsis) pushing food along, so gravity is not needed.

items.prompt_en: Why do elders tell us to chew food well before swallowing?
items.prompt_hi: Bade kyun kehte hain ki khaana achchhe se chaba ke khao?
items.answer: Chewing breaks food into small pieces and mixes it with saliva, which starts digestion and makes swallowing and further digestion easier.
acceptable: small pieces and saliva start digestion
hints: Ask what the teeth do to a big bite
Point to saliva mixing in
Prompt: chewing makes pieces ___ and mixes in ___
Assert: smaller pieces plus saliva start digestion

verified.solverAnswer: Chewing breaks food into small pieces and mixes saliva, which starts digestion of starch, making later digestion easier.

items.prompt_en: Compare the small intestine and the large intestine: which is longer, and what is the main job of each?
items.prompt_hi: Small intestine aur large intestine ki tulna karo: kaun lamba hai, aur dono ka main kaam kya hai?
items.answer: The small intestine is much longer (about 7 metres in an adult) though narrower; it completes digestion and absorbs digested food. The large intestine is shorter (about 1.5 metres) and wider; it absorbs water and some salts from undigested food.
acceptable: small is longer; small absorbs food, large absorbs water
hints: Ask which one sounds bigger but is actually longer
Point to 'small' meaning narrow, not short
Prompt: small intestine absorbs ___, large intestine absorbs ___
Assert: small intestine is longer and absorbs food; large intestine absorbs water

verified.solverAnswer: Small intestine is longer (about 6-7 m): completes digestion and absorbs digested food; large intestine shorter and wider: absorbs water and salts, forms faeces.

items.prompt_en: Kabir says: 'Once food reaches the stomach, digestion is finished. The intestines just carry waste out.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Kabir kehta hai: 'Khaana stomach pahunchte hi digestion khatam. Intestines bas kachra bahar le jaati hain.' Kya galat hai?
items.answer: Digestion is only partly done in the stomach; it is completed in the small intestine, which also absorbs the digested food into the blood. The large intestine absorbs water before waste leaves.
hints: Ask what happens to proteins, fats and starch after the stomach
Point to bile and pancreatic juice joining in the small intestine
Prompt: digestion is completed in the ___
Assert: the small intestine finishes digestion and absorbs food

verified.solverAnswer: Digestion isn't finished in stomach; it is completed in the small intestine with bile and pancreatic juice, and digested food absorbed there; large intestine absorbs water.

items.prompt_en: Why must food be digested before the body can use it? Why can't a piece of dal go straight into the blood?
items.prompt_hi: Khaane ka digestion pehle kyun zaroori hai? Dal ka tukda seedha khoon mein kyun nahi ja sakta?
items.answer: Food is made of large, complex substances that cannot pass into the blood; digestion breaks them into small, simple, soluble substances that can be absorbed through the intestine wall and carried to all cells.
acceptable: big molecules must be broken into small soluble ones
hints: Ask whether a whole grain of dal could fit through a tiny wall
Point to breaking big into small, dissolvable bits
Prompt: digestion makes food ___ and ___ so it can be absorbed
Assert: only small, soluble substances can be absorbed

verified.solverAnswer: Food has large insoluble molecules which can't pass through intestine wall; digestion breaks them into small soluble substances that can be absorbed into blood.

items.prompt_en: On a body outline, show (or describe) where the liver and the pancreas are, and say where their juices go and what they help digest.
items.prompt_hi: Shareer ke chitra pe dikhaao (ya batao) liver aur pancreas kahaan hain, aur unke juices kahaan jaate hain aur kya digest karne mein madad karte hain.
items.answer: The liver is the large organ in the upper right of the abdomen; it makes bile, stored in the gall bladder, which goes to the small intestine and helps digest fats. The pancreas lies below the stomach; its juice goes to the small intestine and helps digest starch, proteins and fats.
acceptable: liver bile for fats; pancreas juice into small intestine
hints: Ask which is the biggest organ near the stomach
Point to both juices flowing into the same place
Prompt: both juices go into the ___
Assert: bile from the liver and pancreatic juice enter the small intestine

verified.solverAnswer: Liver: upper right abdomen near stomach, makes bile; pancreas behind stomach, makes pancreatic juice; both flow into the small intestine; bile helps digest fats, pancreatic juice digests carbohydrates, proteins and fats.

items.prompt_en: During a bout of loose motions (diarrhoea), a person loses a lot of water. Which part of the digestive tract is not doing its job properly, and why is ORS given?
items.prompt_hi: Dast (loose motions) mein insaan ka bahut paani nikal jaata hai. Digestive tract ka kaunsa hissa apna kaam theek se nahi kar raha, aur ORS kyun dete hain?
items.answer: Water is not being absorbed properly (normally the large intestine absorbs water), so a lot of water and salts are lost; ORS (salt and sugar in clean water) replaces the lost water and salts.
acceptable: large intestine not absorbing water; ORS replaces water and salts
hints: Ask which part absorbs water
Point to what is lost in the stool
Prompt: ORS replaces lost ___ and ___
Assert: water absorption fails; ORS replaces water and salts

verified.solverAnswer: Large intestine (and small intestine) fail to absorb water; ORS replaces lost water and salts (sugar helps absorption).

items.prompt_en: A person's gall bladder has been removed, so bile is not stored. The doctor tells them to avoid very oily food for a while. Explain the reason.
items.prompt_hi: Ek insaan ka gall bladder nikaal diya gaya hai, toh bile store nahi hota. Doctor kuch samay bahut tela-bhuna khaana avoid karne ko kehte hain. Kaaran samjhao.
items.answer: Bile helps digest fats; without stored bile, a large oily meal gets less bile at once, so fats are harder to digest.
hints: Ask what bile helps digest
Point to oily food being rich in fat
Prompt: bile is needed for ___
Assert: less bile means fatty food is hard to digest

verified.solverAnswer: Bile helps digest fats; without gall bladder storing/releasing bile, fatty food is harder to digest and causes discomfort.

items.prompt_en: Imagine you are a bite of aloo paratha. Tell the story of your journey through the body, saying what happens to you at each stop.
items.prompt_hi: Socho tum aloo parathe ka ek kaur ho. Shareer mein apne safar ki kahaani sunao, har stop pe tumhare saath kya hota hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: mouth (chewed, saliva starts on starch); food pipe (pushed down); stomach (churned, acid and juices, proteins begin to digest); small intestine (bile and pancreatic juice, digestion completed, absorbed through villi into blood); large intestine (water absorbed); rectum and anus (waste leaves).
acceptable: mouth, food pipe, stomach, small intestine absorbs, large intestine water, out
hints: Ask where the journey starts and what happens there
Point to the stop where you finally enter the blood
Prompt: in the small intestine I am fully ___ and ___
Assert: each stop named with its job

verified.solverAnswer: Mouth: chewed, saliva starts digesting starch; food pipe: squeezed down; stomach: acid and enzymes digest protein, churn; small intestine: bile/pancreatic juice complete digestion, absorb nutrients via villi; large intestine absorbs water; leftover exits as waste.

items.prompt_en: The stomach makes hydrochloric acid strong enough to help digest meat and to kill many germs in food. Why does it not digest its own wall?
items.prompt_hi: Pet hydrochloric acid banaata hai jo itna strong hota hai ki maans pachaane mein madad kare aur khaane ke kai germs maar de. Phir woh apni hi deewar ko kyun nahi pacha leta?
items.answer: The inner wall of the stomach is covered by a thick layer of mucus that it keeps making; the mucus protects the wall from the acid and digestive juices.
hints: Ask what might coat and shield the wall
Point to a slimy protective layer
Prompt: a layer of ___ protects it
Assert: mucus lines and protects the stomach wall

verified.solverAnswer: A layer of mucus lines the stomach wall and protects it from acid.

items.prompt_en: Without looking: what are the finger-like projections in the small intestine called, and what do they do?
items.prompt_hi: Bina dekhe batao: small intestine ke ungli jaise ubhaar kya kehlaate hain, aur kya karte hain?
items.answer: Villi; they increase the surface area for absorbing digested food into the blood.
hints: Ask about the inner wall of the small intestine
The word starts with 'v'
Prompt: ___ increase the area for absorption
Assert: villi, for absorption

verified.solverAnswer: Villi; they increase the surface area for absorbing digested food into blood.

workedExample.problem: What happens to the starch in a mouthful of rice?
steps: Mouth: teeth break the rice into small pieces; saliva starts changing some starch into sugar
Food pipe: wave-like squeezing pushes the food down to the stomach
Stomach: food is churned with acid and juices (these mainly work on proteins)
Small intestine: pancreatic juice and intestinal juice complete the breakdown of starch into simple sugar
Absorption: the simple sugar passes through the villi into the blood and reaches all cells
fadedVersion: Mouth: teeth break the rice; ___ starts changing starch into sugar
Food pipe: wave-like ___ pushes food down
Stomach: food is churned with ___ and juices
Small intestine: juices complete the breakdown of starch into ___
Absorption: sugar passes through the ___ into the blood

skills.title: Describe ways animals take in food (biting and chewing, sucking, swallowing whole, engulfing)
Explain how ruminants like cows digest grass by chewing the cud
Describe how a single-celled amoeba takes in and digests food

expectations: Different animals take in food in different ways suited to their food: a cow grinds grass, a mosquito or butterfly sucks liquids, a snake swallows its prey whole, an amoeba engulfs tiny food particles.

Cows, buffaloes, goats and other ruminants quickly swallow grass and store it in the first part of the stomach (rumen), where it is partly digested; later they bring small lumps (cud) back to the mouth and chew them again.
Grass is rich in cellulose; humans cannot digest cellulose, but ruminants have helpful microbes in their stomach that break it down.
An amoeba is a single-celled organism; it pushes out finger-like pseudopodia to surround food, traps it in a food vacuole, and digests it there with digestive juices.
The basic idea is the same in all: food is taken in, broken down, absorbed and the waste removed, but the structures differ.

misconceptions.belief: All animals digest food exactly the way humans do.
signs: Expects a cow to digest grass with a stomach like ours
Thinks every animal has teeth and chews
Says an amoeba must have a mouth and stomach

diagnostic.prompt_en: An amoeba is a single cell with no mouth or stomach. How does it eat?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Amoeba ek single cell hai, na munh hai na pet. Woh khaata kaise hai?

options.text: It cannot eat at all
It surrounds food with pseudopodia, traps it in a food vacuole and digests it there
It chews with tiny teeth like us

remediation.representation: Side-by-side cards: human, cow, amoeba, each showing take in, break down, absorb, remove waste
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to fill the same four steps for each animal and spot what differs

misconceptions.belief: A cow chewing when it is not eating is just playing, or chewing gum-like habit; it has nothing to do with digestion.
signs: Says the cow is 'just moving its mouth'
Does not connect chewing cud with digesting grass

diagnostic.prompt_en: A cow sitting under a tree keeps chewing even though no grass is in front of it. What is happening?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek gaay ped ke neeche baithi hai aur chabaati jaa rahi hai jabki saamne ghaas nahi hai. Kya ho raha hai?

options.text: It is chewing the cud: partly digested grass brought back from its stomach to chew again
It is bored and just moving its mouth
It is chewing its own teeth

remediation.representation: Animated cow stomach: rumen fills, cud returns to the mouth, goes to the next chambers
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to watch a cow or buffalo (from a safe distance) and count chews per lump

misconceptions.belief: Humans can digest grass and leaf fibre just like cows if they chew enough.
signs: Thinks people could live on grass
Does not know about cellulose or the microbes

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why can a cow live on grass while we cannot?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Gaay ghaas khaake jee leti hai, hum kyun nahi?

options.text: Cows have microbes in the rumen that break down cellulose; we cannot digest cellulose
We could, if we chewed grass long enough
Grass has no food value for anyone

remediation.representation: A grass blade split into 'cellulose wall' and 'contents', with a microbe 'key' that only the cow has
remediation.moveShape: Contrast what each stomach can break down; link to why roughage passes through us

items.prompt_en: Match each animal to how it takes in food: butterfly, snake, cow, eagle. Ways: (a) sucks nectar (b) swallows prey whole (c) grinds grass (d) tears flesh with a hooked beak.
items.prompt_hi: Har jaanvar ko uske khaane ke tareeke se milaao: titli, saanp, gaay, cheel. Tareeke: (a) nectar choosti hai (b) shikaar poora nigalta hai (c) ghaas peesti hai (d) mudi chonch se maans faadti hai.
items.answer: Butterfly (a), snake (b), cow (c), eagle (d).
acceptable: butterfly a, snake b, cow c, eagle d
hints: Ask which one has no teeth to chew at all
Point to the butterfly's long coiled tube
Prompt: the snake ___ its food whole
Assert: butterfly-sucks, snake-swallows, cow-grinds, eagle-tears

verified.solverAnswer: Butterfly: sucks nectar (a); snake: swallows prey whole (b); cow: grinds grass (c); eagle: tears flesh with hooked beak (d).

items.prompt_en: Watch a cow or buffalo resting after grazing (from a safe distance). Before you look, predict: will its jaw be still, or will it be chewing? If chewing, what is it chewing?
items.prompt_hi: Charne ke baad aaraam karti gaay ya bhains ko door se dekho. Dekhne se pehle guess karo: uska jabda ruka hoga ya chal raha hoga? Agar chal raha hai toh kya chaba rahi hai?
items.answer: It will usually be chewing: it brings back lumps of partly digested grass (cud) from its stomach and chews them again.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to the lump moving up its throat
Prompt: it is chewing the ___
Assert: chewing the cud, partly digested grass from the rumen

verified.solverAnswer: It will be chewing the cud: partly digested food brought back from its stomach (rumen) to chew again (rumination).

items.prompt_en: Why does a cow swallow grass quickly while grazing and chew it properly later?
items.prompt_hi: Gaay charte waqt ghaas jaldi-jaldi kyun nigal leti hai aur baad mein aaraam se chabaati hai?
items.answer: It can collect a lot of food quickly in its rumen, where microbes start breaking it down; later, resting, it brings the cud back and chews it thoroughly, which helps digest the tough grass.
acceptable: collect food fast, chew later to digest tough grass
hints: Ask where the grass goes first
Point to tough grass needing extra grinding
Prompt: it stores grass in the ___ and chews the ___ later
Assert: store fast in the rumen, re-chew the cud to digest it

verified.solverAnswer: It swallows quickly into the first stomach chamber (rumen) to store it, then later brings it back as cud to chew thoroughly and digest the tough cellulose.

items.prompt_en: Under a microscope, an amoeba is near a tiny food particle. Predict what the amoeba will do in the next few minutes.
items.prompt_hi: Microscope mein ek amoeba ek chhote khaane ke kan ke paas hai. Guess karo agle kuch minute mein amoeba kya karega.
items.answer: It will push out pseudopodia around the particle, enclose it in a food vacuole, and digest it there with digestive juices; the digested food is absorbed into the cell.
acceptable: surround it with pseudopodia and form a food vacuole
hints: Ask for a guess: how would a blob with no mouth eat?
Point to its changing, finger-like arms
Prompt: it surrounds food and makes a food ___
Assert: pseudopodia engulf food into a food vacuole

verified.solverAnswer: It will surround the food with pseudopodia (false feet), engulf it in a food vacuole and digest it, absorbing nutrients.

items.prompt_en: Compare how a human and a snake deal with a big piece of food.
items.prompt_hi: Insaan aur saanp bade khaane ke tukde ke saath kya karte hain, compare karo.
items.answer: A human cuts and chews food into small pieces using teeth before swallowing; a snake swallows prey whole, stretching its jaws, and digests it slowly in its body.
hints: Ask what the snake does not do with its teeth
Point to its stretchy jaws
Prompt: humans ___; snakes ___ whole
Assert: we chew; the snake swallows whole and digests slowly

verified.solverAnswer: Humans chew food into small pieces with teeth, digest in stomach/intestine; snake swallows prey whole with flexible jaws and digests slowly with strong juices.

items.prompt_en: Why do we say grass is food for a cow but mostly 'roughage' for humans?
items.prompt_hi: Hum kyun kehte hain ki ghaas gaay ke liye khaana hai par insaan ke liye zyada-tar 'roughage' (rasha)?
items.answer: Grass is mostly cellulose; cows have microbes in their rumen that digest cellulose, but humans cannot digest it, so in us plant fibre passes through as roughage that helps bowel movement.
acceptable: cows digest cellulose with microbes; humans cannot
hints: Ask what grass is mostly made of
Point to the cow's helpers in the rumen
Prompt: we cannot digest ___
Assert: cellulose is digested by cow's microbes, not by us

verified.solverAnswer: Cows have microbes in their rumen that digest cellulose in grass; humans can't digest cellulose so it acts as roughage (fibre) helping bowel movement.

items.prompt_en: Sneha writes: 'Every animal needs a mouth, teeth and a stomach to digest food.' Find two counter-examples.
items.prompt_hi: Sneha likhti hai: 'Har jaanvar ko khaana pachaane ke liye munh, daant aur pet chahiye.' Do ulte example dhoondho.
items.answer: Amoeba has no mouth, teeth or stomach (it engulfs and digests in a food vacuole); birds and snakes have no teeth for chewing.
hints: Ask about the single-celled animal you met
Think of an animal with a beak
Prompt: ___ has no mouth at all
Assert: amoeba (no mouth), birds and snakes (no chewing teeth)

verified.solverAnswer: Amoeba has no mouth/teeth/stomach (food vacuole); birds have no teeth (use beak and gizzard); snakes swallow whole; butterfly sucks via proboscis.

items.prompt_en: Goats and camels also chew the cud. What can you say about their stomachs compared with ours?
items.prompt_hi: Bakri aur oont bhi jugaali karte hain. Unke pet ke baare mein, hamaare pet ke mukable, kya keh sakte ho?
items.answer: They are ruminants too, with a stomach of several chambers including a rumen where grass is stored and partly digested by microbes; ours is a single simple stomach.
hints: Ask what chewing the cud tells you about where grass was stored
Point to the cow's stomach design
Prompt: they have a ___ like a cow
Assert: a multi-chambered stomach with a rumen
