skills.title: State that light travels in straight lines and that a shadow forms where an opaque object blocks light
Predict how a shadow's size and shape change with the object's position and orientation
Distinguish a shadow from a reflection or image

expectations: Light travels in straight lines.
A shadow forms when an opaque object blocks the path of light; the region behind it, where light cannot reach, is dark.
To see a shadow you need a source of light, an opaque object and a screen (wall, ground) on which the shadow falls.
A shadow is always dark; it shows the outline (shape) of the object but not its colour or details.
Bringing an object closer to the light source makes its shadow bigger; turning the object can change the shadow's shape.

misconceptions.belief: A shadow is a reflection of the object, like a mirror image.
signs: Says a shadow shows the face or details of a person
Calls a shadow an image or reflection

diagnostic.prompt_en: You stand between a lamp and a wall. What do you see on the wall?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tum lamp aur deewar ke beech khade ho. Deewar pe kya dikhta hai?

options.text: A dark outline of your shape, because your body blocks the light
A reflection showing your face and clothes
Nothing, because shadows only form in sunlight

remediation.representation: Shadow vs mirror image side by side: the shadow is a dark outline, the mirror image shows colour and detail
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to list three things the mirror shows that the shadow does not

misconceptions.belief: A shadow has the colour of the object (a red ball gives a red shadow).
signs: Predicts a coloured shadow for a coloured object
Expects a green leaf to cast a green shadow

diagnostic.prompt_en: A bright red ball is placed in front of a torch. What colour is its shadow on a white wall?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Ek chamakdaar laal ball torch ke saamne rakhi hai. Safed deewar pe uski parchhaai kis rang ki hogi?

options.text: Red
Dark (black or grey), whatever the ball's colour
Pink

remediation.representation: Shadow-puppet tray with objects of many colours casting the same dark shadows
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to predict, then test with two differently coloured objects of the same shape

misconceptions.belief: A shadow is always the same size as the object, whatever the distances.
signs: Expects a hand puppet's shadow never to change size
Cannot explain giant shadows in a puppet show

diagnostic.prompt_en: In a shadow-puppet show, how can the puppeteer make a small paper elephant's shadow huge on the screen?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Parchhaai ke puppet show mein kalaakaar ek chhote kaagaz ke haathi ki parchhaai screen pe bahut badi kaise bana sakta hai?

options.text: Move the puppet closer to the lamp (farther from the screen)
It is impossible; a shadow is always the object's size
Use a red elephant

remediation.representation: Straight-line ray diagram from a point source past an object to a screen, with a slider for object distance
remediation.moveShape: Move the object toward the lamp step by step and ask the child to predict the shadow each time

items.prompt_en: In a dark room, hold your hand between a torch and the wall. Before you move it, predict: what happens to the shadow when you move your hand closer to the torch?
items.prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein torch aur deewar ke beech haath rakho. Hilaane se pehle guess karo: haath ko torch ke paas le jaane pe parchhaai ka kya hoga?
items.answer: The shadow gets bigger (and more blurred at the edges), because the hand blocks a wider cone of light.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to the light spreading out from the torch
Prompt: closer to the source, the shadow gets ___
Assert: closer to the torch means a bigger shadow

verified.solverAnswer: Shadow gets bigger (and fuzzier) as hand moves closer to the torch.

items.prompt_en: A green leaf and a black stone of similar size are held in front of a torch. Predict the colour of each shadow on a white wall.
items.prompt_hi: Ek hara patta aur ek kaala patthar, lagbhag ek size ke, torch ke saamne rakhe hain. Safed deewar pe dono ki parchhaai ka rang guess karo.
items.answer: Both shadows are dark; a shadow shows the shape, not the colour of the object.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to what a shadow really is: missing light
Prompt: a shadow is where light is ___
Assert: both are dark; shadows have no colour of the object

verified.solverAnswer: Both shadows look dark (black/grey); shadow is absence of light; no colour of object.

items.prompt_en: What three things are needed to see a shadow?
items.prompt_hi: Parchhaai dekhne ke liye kaunsi teen cheezein chahiye?
items.answer: A source of light, an opaque object and a screen (surface) for the shadow to fall on.
hints: Ask where the light comes from
What blocks it?
Prompt: source, opaque object and a ___
Assert: source, opaque object, screen

verified.solverAnswer: A source of light, an opaque object and a screen (wall/surface).

items.prompt_en: Why does a shadow form at all? Use the idea of how light travels.
items.prompt_hi: Parchhaai banti hi kyun hai? Roshni kaise chalti hai, us idea se batao.
items.answer: Light travels in straight lines and cannot bend around an opaque object, so the region behind the object gets no light and looks dark.
acceptable: light travels in straight lines and is blocked
hints: Ask whether light can curve around your hand
Point to the straight path from torch to wall
Prompt: light travels in ___ lines
Assert: straight-line light is blocked, leaving a dark region

verified.solverAnswer: Light travels in straight lines; an opaque object blocks it, so the region behind receives no light.

items.prompt_en: Compare your shadow on the ground and your image in a mirror: give three differences.
items.prompt_hi: Zameen pe tumhari parchhaai aur sheeshe mein tumhari image ki tulna karo: teen farak batao.
items.answer: The shadow is dark and shows only the outline; the image shows colours and details. The shadow forms where light is blocked; the image forms by reflection. The shadow's size changes with distance from the source; the plane mirror image is the same size as you.
acceptable: shadow dark outline; image coloured with details; different causes
hints: Ask what you can see on your face in the mirror
Can you see your face in your shadow?
Prompt: shadow: blocked light; image: ___ light
Assert: dark outline vs detailed image; blocking vs reflection

verified.solverAnswer: Shadow: dark outline, no detail or colour, formed by blocked light, can be bigger; image: shows detail and colour, formed by reflection, same size, laterally inverted.

items.prompt_en: Ravi writes: 'My shadow is my reflection on the ground.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Ravi likhta hai: 'Meri parchhaai zameen pe meri reflection hai.' Kya galat hai?
items.answer: A shadow is not a reflection; it is the dark area where his body blocks sunlight. A reflection needs light bouncing back from a shiny surface and would show colours and details.
acceptable: shadow is blocked light, not reflection
hints: Ask whether the ground is like a mirror
What does his body do to the light?
Prompt: a shadow forms when light is ___
Assert: a shadow is blocked light, not a reflection

verified.solverAnswer: A shadow is formed by blocked light, not reflected light; ground is not a mirror; it shows no detail.

items.prompt_en: A cricket stump is fixed upright on the ground. How does its shadow on the ground change from morning to noon to evening on a sunny day?
items.prompt_hi: Ek cricket stump zameen pe seedha gada hai. Dhoop wale din subah, dopahar aur shaam ko uski parchhaai kaise badalti hai?
items.answer: Morning: long, pointing west (away from the Sun in the east). Noon: shortest (and in India it may point almost north). Evening: long again, pointing east.
acceptable: long in morning and evening, shortest at noon, opposite to the Sun
hints: Ask where the Sun is in the morning
Shadows point away from the Sun
Prompt: shortest at ___
Assert: long in morning and evening, shortest at noon, always away from the Sun

verified.solverAnswer: Long in the morning (pointing west), shortest at noon, long in evening (pointing east); always on the side away from the Sun.

items.prompt_en: Draw (or describe) a ray diagram: a torch, a ball, and a wall. Show the straight lines of light and where the shadow forms.
items.prompt_hi: Ek ray diagram banao (ya batao): torch, ball aur deewar. Roshni ki seedhi lines aur parchhaai kahaan banti hai dikhaao.
items.answer: Straight lines from the torch go past the top and bottom edges of the ball to the wall; the region on the wall between these two lines gets no light and is the shadow.
acceptable: straight lines past the edges; dark region between them on the wall
hints: Ask where to draw the lines from
Point to the edges of the ball
Prompt: the shadow is between the two ___ lines
Assert: rays grazing the edges mark the shadow boundary

verified.solverAnswer: Torch with straight rays reaching edges of the ball and continuing to wall; dark region between the edge rays is the shadow.

items.prompt_en: In a traditional shadow-puppet show (like Tholu Bommalata of Andhra Pradesh), how does the puppeteer make a character seem to walk toward the audience and grow bigger?
items.prompt_hi: Paramparik shadow-puppet show mein (jaise Andhra Pradesh ka Tholu Bommalata), kalaakaar kirdaar ko darshakon ki taraf aata aur bada hota kaise dikhaata hai?
items.answer: By moving the puppet closer to the lamp and away from the screen, so the shadow on the screen grows; moving it back toward the screen shrinks it.
acceptable: move puppet closer to the lamp
hints: Ask what changes shadow size
Point to the puppet's distance from the lamp
Prompt: closer to the lamp, the shadow grows ___
Assert: move toward the lamp to enlarge the shadow

verified.solverAnswer: Move the puppet closer to the lamp (and away from screen) so the shadow gets larger; moving toward the screen makes it smaller and sharper.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a younger child how a shadow forms, why it is dark, and how to make it bigger.
items.prompt_hi: Chhote bachche ko samjhao parchhaai kaise banti hai, kaali kyun hoti hai, aur badi kaise karein.
items.answer: Key ideas: light travels in straight lines; an opaque object blocks light; the region behind gets no light so the shadow is dark; it shows shape not colour; moving the object closer to the source makes the shadow bigger.
acceptable: straight lines, blocked light, dark, closer to source bigger
hints: Ask what light does when it meets your hand
Why is the shadow not coloured?
Prompt: to make it bigger, move the object ___ the light
Assert: blocking, darkness, closer means bigger

verified.solverAnswer: Opaque object blocks straight-travelling light, so dark region (no light) behind; shadow has no colour because it is absence of light; move object closer to the light or farther from screen to enlarge.

items.prompt_en: From memory: can a transparent sheet of glass make a dark shadow? Why or why not?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: kya saaf kaanch ki sheet kaali parchhaai bana sakti hai? Kyun ya kyun nahi?
items.answer: No (at most a very faint one), because it lets almost all light pass through; dark shadows need opaque objects.
hints: Ask what transparent means
What kind of object makes a dark shadow?
Prompt: dark shadows need ___ objects
Assert: no; glass lets light through

verified.solverAnswer: No (not dark); transparent glass lets most light pass, so no dark shadow (maybe faint).

workedExample.problem: Why does a pencil held near a lamp make a bigger shadow than when held near the wall?
steps: Light from the lamp spreads out in straight lines in all directions
Near the lamp, the pencil blocks a wide cone of these lines
The blocked region keeps widening until it reaches the wall, giving a big shadow
Near the wall, the pencil blocks only a narrow cone, so the shadow is about its own size
So: closer to the source means a bigger shadow

skills.title: Describe reflection as light bouncing off a surface, best from smooth shiny surfaces
Describe the image in a plane mirror: upright, same size, as far behind as the object is in front, laterally inverted
Apply lateral inversion and the equal-angles rule of reflection to real situations

expectations: Reflection is the bouncing back of light from a surface; smooth shiny surfaces such as mirrors, still water and polished steel reflect light regularly and form clear images.
The image in a plane mirror is upright and the same size as the object.
The image appears to be as far behind the mirror as the object is in front of it; it is not on the surface of the mirror and cannot be caught on a screen.
The image is laterally inverted: left and right are swapped, so your right hand appears as the image's left hand and writing appears reversed.
When light reflects, the angle at which it strikes the mirror equals the angle at which it bounces off (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection).

misconceptions.belief: The image in a mirror is on the surface of the mirror.
signs: Says the image is 'painted on the glass'
Expects the image to stay the same distance when you step back

diagnostic.prompt_en: You stand 2 metres in front of a big mirror. How far from you does your image appear to be?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Tum ek bade sheeshe se 2 meter door khade ho. Tumhari image tumse kitni door dikhti hai?

options.text: 2 metres, on the mirror surface
4 metres: 2 metres behind the mirror, so 2 + 2 from you
It has no distance

remediation.representation: Top-view diagram: person, mirror line and image the same distance on the other side
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to step back one step and say how far the image moved

misconceptions.belief: A plane mirror turns things upside down, or swaps top and bottom.
signs: Predicts an upside-down image
Confuses lateral inversion with vertical inversion

diagnostic.prompt_en: You raise your right hand in front of a mirror. What does your image do?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Sheeshe ke saamne tum apna daahina haath uthaate ho. Tumhari image kya karti hai?

options.text: Raises what looks like its left hand, and stays upright
Turns upside down
Raises its right hand exactly like you

remediation.representation: A paper with 'B' and an arrow pointing right held up to a mirror
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to predict before showing, then trace which direction got swapped

items.prompt_en: Write the word TAXI in capital letters on paper and hold it facing a mirror. Before you look, predict how it will appear.
items.prompt_hi: Kaagaz pe bade aksharon mein TAXI likho aur use sheeshe ki taraf rakho. Dekhne se pehle guess karo kaisa dikhega.
items.answer: It looks the same as TAXI, because T, A, X and I are symmetric left to right, so lateral inversion does not change how they look; a word like BUS would look reversed.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to each letter's left and right halves
Prompt: these letters are ___ left to right
Assert: it looks the same because the letters are symmetric

verified.solverAnswer: It looks the same (TAXI); letters T, A, X, I are symmetrical left-right.

items.prompt_en: You stand 1 metre in front of a mirror, then step back 1 more metre. Predict how far away your image now appears from you.
items.prompt_hi: Tum sheeshe se 1 meter door khade ho, phir 1 meter aur peeche hat jaate ho. Guess karo ab tumhari image tumse kitni door dikhegi.
items.answer: 4 metres: you are 2 m in front, and the image is 2 m behind the mirror.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to the image being as far behind as you are in front
Prompt: 2 in front plus 2 ___
Assert: 4 metres

verified.solverAnswer: 4 metres (2 m in front plus image 2 m behind the mirror).

items.prompt_en: List three features of the image formed by a plane mirror.
items.prompt_hi: Plane mirror se bani image ki teen visheshtaayein batao.
items.answer: Any three: upright; same size as the object; as far behind the mirror as the object is in front; laterally inverted; cannot be caught on a screen.
hints: Ask whether it is upside down
Is it bigger or smaller?
Prompt: upright, same ___, and left-right ___
Assert: upright, same size, laterally inverted

verified.solverAnswer: Upright, same size as object, virtual (behind the mirror), same distance behind as object in front, laterally inverted.

items.prompt_en: Why is AMBULANCE written in mirror writing on the front of an ambulance?
items.prompt_hi: Ambulance ke aage AMBULANCE ulta (mirror writing mein) kyun likha hota hai?
items.answer: So that drivers ahead, looking in their rear-view mirrors, see it laterally inverted back into the correct readable word and give way quickly.
acceptable: so it reads correctly in rear-view mirrors
hints: Ask how a driver in front sees the ambulance
Point to the mirror swapping left and right
Prompt: the mirror ___ it back
Assert: the rear-view mirror inverts it to read correctly

verified.solverAnswer: Driver ahead sees it in rear-view mirror, which laterally inverts the word so it reads correctly.

items.prompt_en: Why do you see your face clearly in a steel plate but not in a wooden table, though light falls on both?
items.prompt_hi: Steel ki plate mein chehra saaf dikhta hai par lakdi ki mez mein nahi, jabki roshni dono pe padti hai. Kyun?
items.answer: The polished steel is smooth and shiny, so it reflects light regularly in one direction and forms a clear image; the rough wood scatters light in many directions, so no clear image forms.
acceptable: smooth shiny reflects regularly; rough surface scatters
hints: Ask how the two surfaces feel
Point to light bouncing in one direction vs many
Prompt: smooth surfaces reflect ___
Assert: smooth surfaces give clear images; rough ones scatter light

verified.solverAnswer: Steel is smooth, regular reflection gives clear image; wood is rough, scatters light in many directions (diffuse reflection).

items.prompt_en: Dev says: 'In a mirror, my image is upside down because mirrors flip everything.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Dev kehta hai: 'Sheeshe mein meri image ulti (sir neeche) hoti hai kyunki sheesha sab palat deta hai.' Kya galat hai?
items.answer: A plane mirror image is upright; only left and right appear swapped (lateral inversion), not top and bottom.
acceptable: image is upright; only left-right swapped
hints: Ask where his head appears in the mirror
What does get swapped?
Prompt: only ___ and ___ swap
Assert: upright image, left-right swapped

verified.solverAnswer: Mirror image is upright; only left and right are swapped (lateral inversion).

items.prompt_en: A ray of light strikes a mirror at 30° to the normal (the line perpendicular to the mirror). Draw (or describe) the reflected ray and give its angle.
items.prompt_hi: Ek prakash ki kiran mirror pe normal (mirror pe lamb rekha) se 30° ke kon pe padti hai. Paraavartit kiran banao (ya batao) aur uska kon do.
items.answer: The reflected ray leaves on the other side of the normal at 30°, because the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence.
acceptable: 30 degrees on the other side of the normal
hints: Ask what the rule of reflection says
Point to the normal as the middle line
Prompt: angle of reflection = angle of ___
Assert: 30°, mirrored across the normal

verified.solverAnswer: Reflected ray makes 30° with the normal on the other side (angle of reflection = angle of incidence).

items.prompt_en: Ria combs her hair with her right hand in front of a mirror. Which hand does her image seem to use, and why?
items.prompt_hi: Ria sheeshe ke saamne daahine haath se baal sanwaarti hai. Uski image kis haath ka use karti dikhti hai, aur kyun?
items.answer: The image seems to use its left hand, because a plane mirror laterally inverts the image, swapping left and right.
hints: Ask which side of the mirror her right hand is on
Point to the swap
Prompt: lateral inversion swaps ___ and ___
Assert: the image seems to use its left hand

verified.solverAnswer: Left hand, due to lateral inversion (left-right swap).

items.prompt_en: A barber's shop has two mirrors on opposite walls, facing each other. Customers see many images going far back. Explain.
items.prompt_hi: Naai ki dukaan mein aamne-saamne deewaron pe do sheeshe hain. Graahakon ko bahut saari images door tak dikhti hain. Samjhao.
items.answer: Light reflects back and forth between the two parallel mirrors many times; each reflection forms another image farther behind, so a long row of images is seen, getting dimmer as some light is lost each time.
hints: Ask what happens when an image is reflected again
Point to each bounce making a new image
Prompt: light bounces ___ and ___
Assert: multiple reflections between parallel mirrors make many images

verified.solverAnswer: Light reflects back and forth between the two parallel mirrors, forming many images, each reflected again, getting fainter.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend where your image is when you look into a plane mirror, and what is special about it.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ki plane mirror mein dekhne pe tumhari image kahaan hoti hai, aur usmein kya khaas hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: the image appears behind the mirror, as far behind as you are in front; it is upright and the same size; left and right are swapped (lateral inversion); it cannot be caught on a screen.
acceptable: behind the mirror, same distance, upright, same size, laterally inverted
hints: Ask where the image seems to be
How big is it?
Prompt: and left-right is ___
Assert: behind, same distance and size, upright, laterally inverted

verified.solverAnswer: Image appears behind the mirror at same distance as you are in front; same size, upright, laterally inverted, cannot be caught on screen (virtual).

items.prompt_en: From memory: what is the swapping of left and right in a mirror image called?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: mirror image mein left aur right ka badal jaana kya kehlaata hai?
items.answer: Lateral inversion.
hints: Think of AMBULANCE
'Lateral' means sideways
Prompt: lateral ___
Assert: lateral inversion

verified.solverAnswer: Lateral inversion.
verified.note: HINT LEAK (mild): hint 2 (''Lateral' means sideways') gives half of the answer.

workedExample.problem: How far is the image of a cat sitting 50 cm in front of a mirror from the cat?
steps: Rule: the image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front
The cat is 50 cm in front of the mirror
So the image is 50 cm behind the mirror
Distance from cat to image = 50 cm + 50 cm
= 100 cm (1 metre)

skills.title: Explain how a pinhole camera forms an inverted image because light travels in straight lines
Explain how a periscope uses two plane mirrors at 45° to see over obstacles
Explain how a kaleidoscope uses multiple reflections to make repeating patterns

expectations: A pinhole camera is a closed box with a tiny hole at one end and a translucent screen (like butter paper) at the other.

Because light travels in straight lines, rays from the top of an object pass through the pinhole and reach the bottom of the screen, and rays from the bottom reach the top; so the image is inverted (upside down) and also left-right reversed.
Moving the screen closer to the pinhole makes the image smaller; a bigger hole makes the image brighter but blurred.

A periscope has two plane mirrors facing each other, each tilted at 45°, at the two ends of a tube; light from above reflects off the top mirror down to the bottom mirror and into the eye, letting you see over walls or from submarines.
A kaleidoscope has mirror strips at an angle (usually 60°) to each other; repeated reflections of a few coloured bits create beautiful symmetrical patterns.
Never look at the Sun through a pinhole camera or any device.

misconceptions.belief: The image in a pinhole camera is upright, like in a mirror.
signs: Draws an upright image on the screen
Is surprised when the tree appears upside down

diagnostic.prompt_en: Through a pinhole camera you view a tall tree. How does the tree appear on the butter-paper screen?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Pinhole camera se tum ek lamba ped dekhte ho. Butter paper screen pe ped kaisa dikhta hai?

options.text: Upright, just like the real tree
Upside down, because rays from the top go straight through the hole to the bottom of the screen
Only as a bright spot with no shape

remediation.representation: Ray diagram with two crossing rays from the top and bottom of a tree through a pinhole
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to draw the ray from the treetop through the hole and say where it lands

misconceptions.belief: A bigger hole in the pinhole camera gives a better, sharper picture.
signs: Pokes a large hole to 'let in more light' and expects a clearer image
Cannot explain blurring

diagnostic.prompt_en: What happens to the pinhole camera image if the pinhole is made much bigger?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Agar pinhole ko bahut bada kar diya toh pinhole camera ki image ka kya hoga?

options.text: It gets brighter but blurred
It gets sharper and clearer
It turns upright

remediation.representation: Overlapping-images picture: a big hole is like many pinholes, each making its own image, all overlapping
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to imagine two pinholes side by side and what two overlapping images look like

misconceptions.belief: A periscope works by bending light around corners inside the tube.
signs: Says the tube bends light
Cannot say what the mirrors are for

diagnostic.prompt_en: How does light get from above a wall to your eye in a periscope?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Periscope mein deewar ke upar se roshni tumhari aankh tak kaise pahunchti hai?

options.text: The tube bends the light like a pipe bends water
It reflects off a top mirror at 45° down the tube, then off a bottom mirror at 45° into the eye
Light goes through the wall

remediation.representation: Cut-away periscope diagram with straight ray segments between two 45° mirrors
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to trace the ray with a finger, saying 'straight, bounce, straight, bounce, eye'

items.prompt_en: You make a pinhole camera and point it at a bright lit bulb in a dark room (never at the Sun). Before you look, predict how the bulb's image will appear on the screen.
items.prompt_hi: Tumne pinhole camera banaaya aur andhere kamre mein jalte bulb ki taraf kiya (Sooraj ki taraf kabhi nahi). Dekhne se pehle guess karo screen pe bulb ki image kaisi dikhegi.
items.answer: Small and upside down (inverted), because light travels in straight lines through the pinhole.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Trace light from the top of the bulb through the hole
Prompt: rays from the top land at the ___
Assert: an inverted image

verified.solverAnswer: Inverted (upside down) image of the bulb on the screen, small and dim.

items.prompt_en: Predict: if you make the pinhole bigger, how will the image change?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: pinhole bada karne pe image kaise badlegi?
items.answer: It becomes brighter but blurred, because a big hole is like many small holes each making an image, and these overlap.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Imagine many tiny holes side by side
Prompt: overlapping images look ___
Assert: brighter but blurred

verified.solverAnswer: Brighter but blurred.

items.prompt_en: In a periscope, the top mirror faces down at 45°. Predict what you would see if the top mirror were removed.
items.prompt_hi: Periscope mein upar wala sheesha 45° pe neeche ki taraf hai. Guess karo agar upar wala sheesha hata do toh kya dikhega.
items.answer: You would not see over the wall; you would only see the inside of the tube (or straight up through the top opening via the bottom mirror), because light from the scene is no longer reflected down.
hints: Ask what the top mirror does to light from the scene
Without it, where does that light go?
Prompt: the top mirror sends light ___ the tube
Assert: you lose the view over the wall

verified.solverAnswer: You'd lose the view of the scene beyond the obstacle; light from the object wouldn't get turned down the tube, so you'd see only what's above/in front through the top opening.

items.prompt_en: At what angle are the two mirrors in a periscope placed, and are they parallel to each other?
items.prompt_hi: Periscope mein dono sheeshe kis kon pe lagte hain, aur kya ek doosre ke parallel hote hain?
items.answer: Each at 45° to the tube, parallel to each other and facing each other.
hints: Ask what angle turns light by a right angle
Half of 90 is?
Prompt: ___ degrees each
Assert: 45°, parallel and facing each other

verified.solverAnswer: 45 degrees each, parallel to each other, facing each other.

items.prompt_en: Why is the image in a pinhole camera upside down?
items.prompt_hi: Pinhole camera mein image ulti kyun hoti hai?
items.answer: Light travels in straight lines: rays from the top of the object pass through the hole and reach the bottom of the screen, and rays from the bottom reach the top, so the image is inverted.
acceptable: straight lines cross at the pinhole
hints: Ask how light travels
Trace the top ray and the bottom ray
Prompt: the rays ___ at the pinhole
Assert: straight rays cross at the hole, inverting the image

verified.solverAnswer: Light travels straight; rays from the top of object go through the hole to the bottom of the screen and rays from bottom go to top, so rays cross at the pinhole, inverting.

items.prompt_en: Compare the image in a plane mirror and in a pinhole camera: upright or inverted? Can it be seen on a screen?
items.prompt_hi: Plane mirror aur pinhole camera ki image ki tulna karo: seedhi ya ulti? Kya screen pe dikh sakti hai?
items.answer: Plane mirror: upright, cannot be caught on a screen. Pinhole camera: inverted, formed on the screen.
acceptable: mirror upright not on screen; pinhole inverted on screen
hints: Ask which one appears on butter paper
Which one is upside down?
Prompt: pinhole is ___; mirror is ___
Assert: pinhole inverted on screen; mirror upright, not on a screen

verified.solverAnswer: Pinhole: inverted real image, formed on a screen. Plane mirror: upright, virtual, can't be caught on a screen.

items.prompt_en: Neha writes: 'A periscope bends light round corners with its tube.' Correct her.
items.prompt_hi: Neha likhti hai: 'Periscope apni tube se roshni ko mod deta hai.' Use sahi karo.
items.answer: The tube does not bend light; light travels in straight lines and is turned by reflection off two plane mirrors placed at 45°.
acceptable: mirrors reflect, tube does not bend light
hints: Ask what is inside the tube
Does light travel straight in the tube?
Prompt: light is turned by ___
Assert: two 45° mirrors reflect the light

verified.solverAnswer: The tube doesn't bend light; two mirrors at 45 degrees reflect it; light travels straight between reflections.

items.prompt_en: Draw (or describe) a ray diagram for a pinhole camera viewing a candle-shaped cut-out lit from behind: show two rays from the top and bottom.
items.prompt_hi: Pinhole camera ke liye ray diagram banao (ya batao), peeche se roshan mombatti ke aakar ke cut-out ko dekhte hue: upar aur neeche se do kirne dikhaao.
items.answer: A straight ray from the top of the object passes through the pinhole to the bottom of the screen; a ray from the bottom passes through to the top; the image is inverted between them.
acceptable: two straight rays crossing at the pinhole
hints: Ask where to start each ray
Both rays pass through one point
Prompt: they ___ at the pinhole
Assert: crossing rays make an inverted image

verified.solverAnswer: Candle cutout, pinhole, screen; ray from top travels straight through hole and strikes lower part of screen, ray from bottom hits upper part; rays cross at hole; image inverted.

items.prompt_en: A kaleidoscope uses three mirror strips at 60° to each other. Why do a few broken bangle pieces inside look like a big, repeating pattern?
items.prompt_hi: Kaleidoscope mein teen sheeshe ki pattiyaan 60° pe lagi hoti hain. Andar tooti chooriyon ke kuch tukde bade, dohraate pattern jaise kyun dikhte hain?
items.answer: The bangle pieces are reflected again and again between the mirrors, making many images arranged symmetrically, which form the pattern; turning the tube rearranges the pieces and changes the pattern.
hints: Ask how many times light can bounce between mirrors
Each bounce makes another image
Prompt: many ___ make the pattern
Assert: multiple reflections create symmetric repeating images

verified.solverAnswer: Mirrors at 60 degrees create multiple reflections of the bangle pieces, giving symmetrical, repeating patterns (6-fold).

items.prompt_en: Soldiers in trenches and sailors in submarines use periscopes. In a crowd at a cricket match, how could a simple periscope help you, and how would you hold it?
items.prompt_hi: Khandakon mein sainik aur pandubbi mein naavik periscope use karte hain. Cricket match ki bheed mein simple periscope tumhari kaise madad kar sakta hai, aur use kaise pakdoge?
items.answer: Hold it upright with the top opening above people's heads facing the field; light from the field reflects off the top mirror down to the bottom mirror and into your eye, so you can see over the crowd.
acceptable: hold it up above heads; mirrors reflect view down
hints: Ask where the top opening must be
Which way should it face?
Prompt: top opening above the ___
Assert: hold it above the crowd facing the field

verified.solverAnswer: Hold periscope vertically with top opening above the people in front, lower opening at your eye so you can see the field; mirrors reflect light down.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend how to make a pinhole camera at home from a box and butter paper, and what they will see.
items.prompt_hi: Dost ko samjhao ghar pe dabbe aur butter paper se pinhole camera kaise banaayein, aur kya dikhega.
items.answer: Key ideas: a closed box (or two sliding tubes) with a tiny hole at one end and butter paper at the other; point at a bright object (not the Sun) and look at the screen in shade; the image is small and inverted because light travels straight; screen nearer gives a smaller image.
acceptable: tiny hole, butter paper screen, inverted image, never the Sun
hints: Ask what goes at each end
What will the image look like?
Prompt: never point it at the ___
Assert: hole, screen, inverted image, safety

verified.solverAnswer: Make a small pinhole on one end of a dark box, butter-paper screen on the other end; point at a bright lit object (not Sun); you see an inverted image on the screen.

items.prompt_en: From memory: what kind of image (upright or inverted) does a periscope give, and how many mirrors does it use?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: periscope kaisi image deta hai (seedhi ya ulti), aur kitne sheeshe use karta hai?
items.answer: An upright image, using two plane mirrors.
hints: Think of a submarine view
Two reflections bring the image back the right way up
Prompt: ___ mirrors
Assert: upright, two mirrors

verified.solverAnswer: Upright image; two mirrors.

workedExample.problem: Make and use a pinhole camera.
steps: Take two paper tubes that slide into each other; cover one end of the outer tube with paper and make a tiny pinhole in it

skills.title: Explain day and night as caused by the Earth's rotation on its axis from west to east in about 24 hours
Explain the apparent east-to-west motion of the Sun and stars, and why places in the east see sunrise earlier
Explain the year as one revolution of the Earth around the Sun in about 365¼ days, and the leap year

expectations: The Earth spins (rotates) on its axis, an imaginary line through the North and South Poles, from west to east, once in about 24 hours.
At any moment the half of the Earth facing the Sun has day and the other half has night; as the Earth rotates, places move from night into day and back.
Because the Earth rotates from west to east, the Sun, Moon and stars appear to rise in the east and set in the west; the Sun does not really go around the Earth each day.
Places farther east turn into sunlight first, so the Sun rises in Arunachal Pradesh nearly two hours before it rises in western Gujarat.

The Earth also moves (revolves) around the Sun in an orbit; one revolution takes about 365¼ days, which is one year. The extra quarter day is collected into an extra day (29 February) every fourth year, a leap year.

misconceptions.belief: The Sun moves around the Earth each day, causing day and night.
signs: Says 'the Sun goes to the other side at night'
Explains sunset as the Sun moving down behind hills
Cannot explain why it is night in the USA when it is day in India

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why do we have day and night?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Din aur raat kyun hote hain?

options.text: The Sun goes around the Earth every day
The Earth spins on its axis, so each place faces the Sun for part of the day and faces away for the rest
The Moon covers the Sun at night

remediation.moveShape: Spin the globe slowly west to east and ask the child to call out sunrise, noon, sunset and midnight for the sticker

signs: Uses 'rotation' and 'revolution' interchangeably
Says one revolution gives one day

diagnostic.prompt_en: What does one full revolution of the Earth around the Sun give us?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Earth ka Sooraj ke chaaron or ek poora chakkar (revolution) humein kya deta hai?

options.text: One day
One year, about 365¼ days
One month

remediation.representation: Child as Earth: spin on the spot (rotation, day) while walking slowly around a chair (Sun) (revolution, year)
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to count spins during one walk around the chair and link it to about 365

items.prompt_en: In a dark room, shine a torch on a globe (or a ball with a dot marking India). Before you turn it, predict: if you spin the globe slowly from west to east, from which direction will the 'Sun' first appear for the dot?
items.prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein globe (ya ball jispe India ka nishaan ho) pe torch daalo. Ghumaane se pehle guess karo: globe ko pashchim se poorab dheere ghumaane pe, nishaan ke liye 'Sooraj' kis disha se pehle dikhega?
items.answer: From the east: the dot turns into the light from the eastern side, which is why the Sun appears to rise in the east.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to the direction the dot is moving
Prompt: turning west to east, the Sun appears in the ___
Assert: from the east, so the Sun rises in the east

verified.solverAnswer: From the east; the Sun appears from the east side as the Earth spins west to east.

items.prompt_en: Predict: does the Sun rise earlier in Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh) or in Dwarka (Gujarat)? By roughly how much?
items.prompt_hi: Guess karo: Sooraj Itanagar (Arunachal Pradesh) mein pehle ugta hai ya Dwarka (Gujarat) mein? Lagbhag kitna pehle?
items.answer: Itanagar, nearly two hours earlier, because it is far to the east and the Earth rotates from west to east, so it turns into sunlight first.
hints: Ask for a guess and a reason
Which place is farther east?
Prompt: places to the ___ see sunrise first
Assert: Arunachal, nearly two hours earlier

verified.solverAnswer: Itanagar (Arunachal) sees sunrise first, about 1.5 to 2 hours earlier than Dwarka, since it is farther east.
verified.note: ACCURACY (minor): 'nearly two hours earlier' overstates; Itanagar vs Dwarka is about 1.5 to 1.75 h (about 25 degrees of longitude, 4 min per degree).

items.prompt_en: How long does the Earth take to rotate once on its axis, and in which direction does it rotate?
items.prompt_hi: Earth apni axis pe ek baar ghoomne mein kitna samay leti hai, aur kis disha mein ghoomti hai?
items.answer: About 24 hours, from west to east.
hints: Ask how long a day and night together last
Think of where the Sun rises
Prompt: about ___ hours, from ___ to east
Assert: about 24 hours, west to east

verified.solverAnswer: About 24 hours; west to east.

items.prompt_en: Why do we have a 29 February only once every four years?
items.prompt_hi: 29 February chaar saal mein sirf ek baar kyun aati hai?
items.answer: One revolution takes about 365¼ days; the extra quarter day each year adds up to one full day every four years, which is added as 29 February in a leap year.
acceptable: quarter day each year adds up
hints: Ask how long one revolution takes exactly
Add up four quarters
Prompt: four quarter days make ___ day
Assert: 365¼ days per year; the extra day every four years is 29 February

verified.solverAnswer: Earth takes about 365 and a quarter days to go round the Sun; four quarters add up to an extra day, added as 29 February in leap years.

items.prompt_en: If the Earth is spinning so fast, why do we not feel it moving, and why does the Sun seem to move across the sky instead?
items.prompt_hi: Agar Earth itni tezi se ghoom rahi hai, toh hum use mehsoos kyun nahi karte, aur ulta Sooraj aasmaan mein chalta kyun dikhta hai?
items.answer: We move along with the Earth smoothly at a steady speed, so we do not feel it; from the moving Earth, the Sun appears to move from east to west, just as trees seem to move backwards from a smooth-running train.
acceptable: we move with the Earth; Sun only appears to move
hints: Ask what a smooth train ride feels like
What do trees outside seem to do?
Prompt: the Sun only ___ to move
Assert: we move with Earth; the Sun's motion is apparent

verified.solverAnswer: We move along with Earth (smooth, constant motion, like in a train); the Sun's motion is apparent, caused by Earth's rotation.

items.prompt_en: Compare rotation and revolution of the Earth: what each is, how long it takes, and what it gives us.
items.prompt_hi: Earth ke rotation aur revolution ki tulna karo: dono kya hain, kitna samay lete hain, aur humein kya dete hain.
items.answer: Rotation: spinning on its axis, about 24 hours, gives day and night. Revolution: moving around the Sun, about 365¼ days, gives the year.
acceptable: rotation 24 hours day-night; revolution 365 days year
hints: Ask which one is spinning in place
Which one is going around?
Prompt: rotation gives ___; revolution gives ___
Assert: rotation-day and night; revolution-year

verified.solverAnswer: Rotation: spinning on its axis, about 24 hours, gives day and night. Revolution: going around the Sun, about 365 1/4 days, gives a year (and with tilt, seasons).

items.prompt_en: Ishaan says: 'At night the Sun goes under the Earth and comes back up in the morning.' What is wrong?
items.prompt_hi: Ishaan kehta hai: 'Raat ko Sooraj Earth ke neeche chala jaata hai aur subah wapas upar aata hai.' Kya galat hai?
items.answer: The Sun does not go around the Earth daily; the Earth rotates, so our side turns away from the Sun at night and back towards it in the morning.
acceptable: Earth rotates; Sun does not go under
hints: Ask what is actually moving
Use the globe and torch again
Prompt: our side turns ___ from the Sun
Assert: Earth's rotation causes night, not the Sun moving

verified.solverAnswer: The Sun doesn't move under the Earth; the Earth rotates, so our side turns away from the Sun at night.

items.prompt_en: Draw (or describe) the Earth and Sun from above the North Pole. Mark the day side and night side, and an arrow for the Earth's spin.
items.prompt_hi: North Pole ke upar se Earth aur Sooraj banao (ya batao). Din wala hissa aur raat wala hissa, aur Earth ke ghoomne ka teer dikhaao.
items.answer: The half facing the Sun is day; the far half is night; seen from above the North Pole, the Earth spins anticlockwise (west to east).
acceptable: half facing Sun is day; spins anticlockwise from above North Pole
hints: Ask which half the light falls on
Which way does it spin seen from above the North Pole?
Prompt: from above the North Pole it spins ___
Assert: Sun-facing half is day; anticlockwise spin

verified.solverAnswer: Sun at one side; Earth circle with half facing Sun lit (day) and other half dark (night); arrow showing anticlockwise spin from above North Pole.

items.prompt_en: Your uncle in New York calls at 8 pm Indian time and says he is having breakfast. Explain how this can be.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhare chacha New York se Indian time raat 8 baje phone karte hain aur kehte hain ki woh nashta kar rahe hain. Ye kaise ho sakta hai?
items.answer: New York is on the other side of the Earth; when India has turned away from the Sun (evening/night), New York is turning into sunlight (morning), because the Earth rotates.
acceptable: opposite side of Earth is in morning
hints: Ask where New York is on the globe compared to India
Which side faces the Sun at India's night?
Prompt: when it is night here it is ___ there
Assert: rotation means different places have different times of day

verified.solverAnswer: Earth is rotating; when it is night in India (8 pm), New York faces the Sun side in morning (about 10 am), time zones differ by about 9.5-10.5 hours.

items.prompt_en: Ancient Indian astronomer Aryabhata wrote that the stars seem to move west because the Earth spins, like stationary objects on the bank seem to move backward to a person in a moving boat. Explain his comparison.
items.prompt_hi: Prachin bhaarteeya khagolshaastri Aryabhata ne likha ki taare pashchim ki or chalte dikhte hain kyunki Earth ghoomti hai, jaise chalti naav mein baithe insaan ko kinaare ki sthir cheezein peeche jaati dikhti hain. Unki tulna samjhao.
items.answer: In a moving boat, the still trees on the bank appear to move the opposite way; similarly, as the Earth spins from west to east, the still stars appear to move from east to west.
acceptable: apparent motion opposite to our motion
hints: Ask what the trees on the bank seem to do
Which way is the Earth moving?
Prompt: things seem to move ___ to our motion
Assert: apparent motion of stars is opposite to Earth's spin

verified.solverAnswer: Stars appear to move westward just like trees on the riverbank appear to move backward from a boat; apparent motion due to our own motion (Earth rotating west to east).

items.prompt_en: Explain to your younger cousin, using a ball and a torch, why we have day and night and why the Sun rises in the east.
items.prompt_hi: Chhote cousin ko ball aur torch se samjhao ki din aur raat kyun hote hain aur Sooraj poorab mein kyun ugta hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: the Earth is a ball lit by the Sun on one half; it spins on its axis from west to east in about 24 hours; the lit half has day, the other night; turning eastward into the light makes the Sun appear to rise in the east.
acceptable: Earth spins, lit half day, west to east, Sun appears to rise in east
hints: Ask what the torch stands for
Which way do you turn the ball?
Prompt: turning into the light from the ___
Assert: rotation causes day-night and the eastern sunrise

verified.solverAnswer: Torch = Sun, ball = Earth; spin ball west to east; the side facing torch has day, away has night; since Earth spins west to east, the Sun appears first from the east.

items.prompt_en: From memory: how long does the Earth take to go once around the Sun?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: Earth ko Sooraj ka ek chakkar lagaane mein kitna samay lagta hai?
items.answer: About 365¼ days (one year).
hints: Think of a calendar
And the leap year clue
Prompt: about ___ days
Assert: about 365¼ days

verified.solverAnswer: About 365 1/4 days (one year).

skills.title: State that the Earth's axis is tilted (about 23.5°) and points in the same direction in space as the Earth revolves
Explain how the tilt causes seasons through the angle of sunlight and the length of day
Explain why the two hemispheres have opposite seasons and why distance from the Sun is not the cause

expectations: The Earth's axis is tilted by about 23.5° and keeps pointing the same way in space while the Earth goes around the Sun.
When the northern half is tilted towards the Sun, the Sun's rays fall on it more directly (more concentrated) and days are longer, so it gets more heat: this is summer in the north (around June).
When the northern half is tilted away from the Sun, rays fall at a slant (spread out) and days are shorter, so it is winter (around December).
The southern hemisphere is tilted the opposite way, so its seasons are opposite: when it is summer in India it is winter in Australia.
Seasons are not caused by changes in distance from the Sun; the Earth is actually closest to the Sun in early January, during the northern winter.

misconceptions.belief: Seasons happen because the Earth is closer to the Sun in summer and farther in winter.
signs: Says 'summer is when we are near the Sun'
Draws a very stretched orbit with summer at the near end
Cannot explain opposite seasons in Australia

diagnostic.prompt_en: In early January the Earth is at its closest to the Sun. What season is it then in India?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: January ki shuruaat mein Earth Sooraj ke sabse paas hoti hai. Tab India mein kaunsa mausam hota hai?

options.text: Summer, because we are closest to the Sun
Winter, so distance cannot be the cause of seasons
Monsoon

remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to find the closest point and the season there, then look for what actually changes: the tilt towards or away

misconceptions.belief: The tilt of the axis changes back and forth during the year, or the Earth 'leans towards the Sun' by turning its axis.
signs: Draws the axis pointing at the Sun at every position
Says the Earth tilts in summer and straightens in winter

diagnostic.prompt_en: As the Earth goes around the Sun, what happens to the direction its axis points in space?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Earth jab Sooraj ka chakkar lagaati hai, toh uski axis space mein kis disha mein point karti hai?

options.text: It keeps pointing in the same direction (towards the Pole Star)
It always points at the Sun

diagnostic.prompt_en: A torch shines straight down on a sheet of paper, making a small bright circle. Then it is tilted so the light falls at a slant. What changes?

items.prompt_hi: Torch ko squared paper pe seedha neeche chamkaao aur lagbhag gino kitne khaane roshan hain. Phir usi oonchaai se torch ko tircha karo. Karne se pehle guess karo: roshan hissa bada hoga ya chhota, chamakdaar ya dhundhla?
items.answer: Bigger and dimmer: the same light spreads over more squares, so each square gets less light and heat, like slanting winter sunlight.

items.prompt_en: In June it is summer in Delhi. Predict the season in Sydney, Australia, at the same time, and explain.
items.prompt_hi: June mein Delhi mein garmi hoti hai. Usi samay Sydney, Australia mein kaunsa mausam hoga, guess karo aur samjhao.

items.prompt_en: By about how many degrees is the Earth's axis tilted?
items.prompt_hi: Earth ki axis lagbhag kitne degree jhuki hui hai?
items.answer: About 23.5° (from the perpendicular to its orbit).

It is 'twenty-three and a half'
Prompt: about ___ degrees
Assert: about 23.5°

items.prompt_en: Why are days longer than nights in Delhi in June?
items.prompt_hi: June mein Delhi mein din raaton se lambe kyun hote hain?
items.answer: In June the northern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, so places like Delhi spend more of each rotation in the lit half, giving longer days.

Picture the lit half on a tilted globe
Prompt: tilted ___ the Sun means longer days
Assert: northern tilt towards the Sun lengthens days

verified.solverAnswer: In June the northern hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, so more than half of Delhi's circle of latitude is in sunlight, making longer days.

items.prompt_en: Compare summer and winter in India: the angle of the Sun's rays at noon and the length of the day.
items.prompt_hi: India mein garmi aur sardi ki tulna karo: dopahar mein Sooraj ki kirnon ka kon aur din ki lambaai.
items.answer: Summer: the noon Sun is high, rays fall more directly, days are longer. Winter: the noon Sun is lower, rays slant and spread out, days are shorter.
acceptable: summer direct rays long days; winter slanting rays short days
hints: Ask how high the noon Sun is in May vs December
And how long the days are

Assert: direct rays and long days in summer; slanting rays and short days in winter

items.prompt_en: A website says: 'We have summer because the Earth moves closer to the Sun.' Give two pieces of evidence that this is wrong.
items.prompt_hi: Ek website kehti hai: 'Garmi isliye hoti hai kyunki Earth Sooraj ke paas aa jaati hai.' Do saboot do ki ye galat hai.
items.answer: 1) The Earth is closest to the Sun in early January, during northern winter. 2) The two hemispheres have opposite seasons at the same time, which distance cannot explain since both are at the same distance.

hints: Ask when the Earth is closest to the Sun
What season is it in Australia when it is summer here?
Prompt: both halves are at the same ___
Assert: closest in January (winter) and opposite seasons disprove it

verified.solverAnswer: Earth is closest to Sun in early January (our winter); when it is summer in India it is winter in Australia (both are the same distance).

items.prompt_en: Draw (or describe) the Earth at two places in its orbit, June and December, with the tilted axis. Show which hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun in each.
items.prompt_hi: Orbit mein do jagah Earth banao (ya batao), June aur December, jhuki axis ke saath. Dikhaao har ek mein kaunsa hemisphere Sooraj ki taraf jhuka hai.
items.answer: June: the axis tilts the North Pole towards the Sun, so the northern hemisphere is tilted towards it. December (opposite side of the orbit): the axis still points the same way, so now the South Pole side is towards the Sun.
acceptable: June north towards Sun; December south towards Sun; axis parallel
hints: Ask whether the axis direction changes
Draw both axes parallel
Prompt: in December the ___ hemisphere faces the Sun
Assert: same axis direction; north towards Sun in June, south in December

verified.solverAnswer: Orbit as an ellipse; June: axis tilted with northern hemisphere toward Sun; December: same axis direction but southern hemisphere toward Sun.

items.prompt_en: Near the equator, in places like Singapore, there is little difference between summer and winter. Using the tilt idea, suggest why.
items.prompt_hi: Bhoomadhya rekha ke paas, jaise Singapore mein, garmi aur sardi mein zyada farak nahi hota. Tilt ke idea se kaaran socho.
items.answer: Near the equator the Sun is high in the sky all year and day length stays close to 12 hours, so the heating changes little through the year.
acceptable: Sun high all year, days about 12 hours
hints: Ask how the noon Sun moves at the equator through the year
And day length?
Prompt: days stay about ___ hours
Assert: steady high Sun and equal days mean small seasonal change

verified.solverAnswer: Near the equator the noon Sun is always high and days are about 12 hours all year, so little seasonal change.

items.prompt_en: Indian Antarctic stations Maitri and Bharati see the Sun not setting for weeks in December-January. Explain using the tilt.
items.prompt_hi: Bhaarat ke Antarctic station Maitri aur Bharati par December-January mein hafton tak Sooraj nahi doobta. Tilt se samjhao.
items.answer: In December-January the southern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, so the region near the South Pole stays in the lit half throughout each rotation, giving continuous daylight.
acceptable: south tilted towards Sun, polar region always lit
hints: Ask which way the south is tilted in December

Prompt: it stays in the ___ half all day
Assert: southern tilt keeps the polar region lit all day

verified.solverAnswer: In December the southern hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, so the region within the Antarctic circle stays in sunlight for 24 h (midnight Sun) as Earth rotates.

items.prompt_en: Explain to a friend, with a ball and a torch, why India has summer in May-June and winter in December-January.
items.prompt_hi: Ek dost ko ball aur torch se samjhao ki India mein May-June mein garmi aur December-January mein sardi kyun hoti hai.
items.answer: Key ideas: Earth's axis is tilted and keeps pointing the same way; in May-June the north is tilted towards the Sun, giving direct rays and long days; in December-January it is tilted away, giving slanting rays and short days; distance is not the reason.
acceptable: tilt, same direction, direct vs slanting rays, day length, not distance
hints: Ask how to hold the ball's axis
What changes as you go around the torch?
Prompt: it is not about ___
Assert: tilt, ray angle and day length, not distance

verified.solverAnswer: Axis tilted 23.5 degrees pointing the same way; in May-June the north is tilted toward torch: direct rays and longer days; in December away: slanting rays, shorter days; not distance.

items.prompt_en: From memory: in which month is the Earth closest to the Sun?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: Earth kis mahine mein Sooraj ke sabse paas hoti hai?
items.answer: Early January.

It is during India's winter
Prompt: early ___
Assert: early January

verified.solverAnswer: Early January.

skills.title: Explain a solar eclipse: the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth and its shadow falls on the Earth
Explain a lunar eclipse: the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon and its shadow falls on the Moon
Explain why eclipses do not happen every month and how the phases of the Moon differ from eclipses
Describe how to view a solar eclipse safely

expectations: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon comes between the Sun and the Earth in a straight line, and the Moon's shadow falls on part of the Earth; it can happen only on a new moon day.
A lunar eclipse happens when the Earth comes between the Sun and the Moon, and the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon; it can happen only on a full moon night.
Eclipses do not happen every month because the Moon's orbit is tilted (about 5°) to the Earth's orbit, so usually the three are not exactly in line.
The phases of the Moon are caused by how much of the Moon's sunlit half we see as it goes around the Earth, not by the Earth's shadow.

Never look at the Sun directly, even during an eclipse, nor through ordinary sunglasses, binoculars or a pinhole: view it safely by projecting its image through a pinhole onto a screen, or with certified eclipse-viewing glasses. A lunar eclipse is safe to watch with the naked eye.

misconceptions.belief: Eclipses happen every new moon and every full moon.
signs: Expects a solar eclipse every month
Cannot explain why eclipses are rare events

diagnostic.prompt_en: There is a full moon about every month. Why is there not a lunar eclipse every month?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Lagbhag har mahine poornima hoti hai. Toh har mahine chandra grahan kyun nahi hota?

options.text: Because the Moon's orbit is tilted, so usually the Moon passes above or below the Earth's shadow
There is a lunar eclipse every full moon; we just don't notice
The Earth's shadow is too small to ever reach the Moon

remediation.representation: Two hula-hoops tilted slightly to each other (Earth's orbit and Moon's orbit), crossing at two points
remediation.moveShape: Show the Moon passing above the shadow most months and through it only when near a crossing point

misconceptions.belief: The phases of the Moon are caused by the Earth's shadow falling on it.
signs: Explains a half moon as half covered by Earth's shadow
Thinks a lunar eclipse and a crescent moon are the same thing

diagnostic.prompt_en: Why does the Moon look like a thin crescent a few days after new moon?
diagnostic.prompt_hi: Amaavasya ke kuch din baad Chaand patli kalaa (crescent) jaisa kyun dikhta hai?

options.text: The Earth's shadow is covering most of it
We see only a small part of the Moon's sunlit half from the Earth
The Moon has actually become smaller

remediation.representation: Ball-on-a-stick moon held by the child and moved around their head in a room with one lamp
remediation.moveShape: Ask the child to describe the lit part they see at each position; no shadow of the head is needed for phases

misconceptions.belief: It is safe to look at a solar eclipse with sunglasses, or because the Sun is partly covered.

Says 'the Sun is dim during an eclipse so it is safe'

diagnostic.prompt_en: What is a safe way to watch a partial solar eclipse?

options.text: Look at it with dark sunglasses
Project the Sun's image through a pinhole onto a sheet of paper and look at the paper, or use certified eclipse glasses
Look directly, since the Sun is partly covered

remediation.representation: Pinhole projection picture: a card with a small hole making a crescent Sun image on the ground, viewer's back to the Sun
remediation.moveShape: Have the child state the rule 'look at the paper, never at the Sun' before every eclipse activity

items.prompt_en: In a dark room, put a torch (Sun), a small ball (Moon) and a big ball (Earth) in a straight line with the small ball in the middle. Before you look, predict what falls on the big ball.
items.prompt_hi: Andhere kamre mein torch (Sooraj), chhoti ball (Chaand) aur badi ball (Earth) ek seedhi line mein rakho, chhoti ball beech mein. Dekhne se pehle guess karo badi ball pe kya padega.
items.answer: The small ball's shadow falls on a small part of the big ball: this models a solar eclipse, seen only from the places where the Moon's shadow falls.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to the small ball blocking light
Prompt: the Moon's ___ falls on Earth
Assert: the Moon's shadow on part of the Earth, a solar eclipse

verified.solverAnswer: The Moon's shadow falls on part of the Earth: a solar eclipse.

items.prompt_en: Now place the big ball (Earth) in the middle, between the torch and the small ball. Predict what happens to the small ball, and which eclipse this is.
items.prompt_hi: Ab badi ball (Earth) ko beech mein rakho, torch aur chhoti ball ke beech. Guess karo chhoti ball ka kya hoga, aur ye kaunsa grahan hai.
items.answer: The small ball goes into the big ball's shadow and becomes dark: this models a lunar eclipse.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Point to the Earth blocking sunlight
Prompt: the Earth's shadow falls on the ___
Assert: Earth's shadow darkens the Moon, a lunar eclipse

verified.solverAnswer: The Earth's shadow falls on the Moon: lunar eclipse.

items.prompt_en: With one lamp in a room, hold a ball on a stick at arm's length and slowly turn around on the spot. Predict how much of the lit part of the ball you will see when it is between you and the lamp, and when the lamp is behind you.
items.prompt_hi: Kamre mein ek lamp ho, ek ball ko danda pe haath bhar door pakdo aur dheere-dheere apni jagah ghoomo. Guess karo ball ka roshan hissa kitna dikhega jab ball tumhare aur lamp ke beech ho, aur jab lamp tumhare peeche ho.
items.answer: Between you and the lamp: almost none (like a new moon). Lamp behind you (ball held up so your head's shadow does not fall on it): the whole lit face (like a full moon). In between you see partly lit shapes, which are the phases.
hints: Ask for a guess first
Which side of the ball faces the lamp?
Prompt: phases depend on how much of the ___ half we see
Assert: dark at new-moon position, fully lit at full-moon position

verified.solverAnswer: Between you and the lamp: you see the dark side (new moon); lamp behind you: whole face lit (full moon); in between, partial phases.

items.prompt_en: On which day can a solar eclipse happen: new moon (amavasya) or full moon (purnima)?
items.prompt_hi: Surya grahan kis din ho sakta hai: amaavasya ya poornima?
items.answer: New moon (amavasya).
hints: Ask where the Moon must be for a solar eclipse
Between the Sun and Earth, we see its dark side
Prompt: the ___ moon
Assert: new moon

verified.solverAnswer: New moon (amavasya).

items.prompt_en: On which day can a lunar eclipse happen?
items.prompt_hi: Chandra grahan kis din ho sakta hai?
items.answer: Full moon (purnima).
hints: Ask where the Moon is when the Earth is between it and the Sun
Then the Moon's lit face points at us
Prompt: the ___ moon
Assert: full moon

verified.solverAnswer: Full moon (purnima).

items.prompt_en: Why does an eclipse not happen every month?
items.prompt_hi: Har mahine grahan kyun nahi hota?
items.answer: The Moon's orbit is tilted by about 5° to the Earth's orbit, so in most months the Moon passes a little above or below the line joining the Sun and Earth, and no shadow falls exactly.
hints: Ask whether the Moon's path is exactly level with the Earth's
Picture two slightly tilted rings
Prompt: the Moon's orbit is ___
Assert: the tilted orbit usually misses the straight line

verified.solverAnswer: Moon's orbit is tilted by about 5 degrees to Earth's orbit, so the Sun, Earth, Moon rarely line up exactly; the shadow usually misses.

items.prompt_en: Compare a half moon and a partial lunar eclipse: what causes the dark part in each?
items.prompt_hi: Aadhe chaand aur aanshik chandra grahan ki tulna karo: dono mein kaala hissa kis wajah se hai?
items.answer: Half moon: we are seeing half of the Moon's sunlit side; the dark part is the Moon's own night side. Partial lunar eclipse: the Earth's shadow is falling on part of the Moon.
acceptable: half moon: we see half the lit side; eclipse: Earth's shadow
hints: Ask whether Earth's shadow is involved in phases
When is Earth's shadow on the Moon?
Prompt: phases come from viewing angle; eclipse from Earth's ___
Assert: phases are viewing angle; an eclipse is Earth's shadow

verified.solverAnswer: Half moon: we see half of its sunlit side due to viewing angle (phase). Partial lunar eclipse: Earth's shadow falls on part of the Moon.

items.prompt_en: A friend says: 'During a solar eclipse the Sun is covered, so I can look at it with my sunglasses.' Explain why this is dangerous and give a safe method.
items.prompt_hi: Ek dost kehta hai: 'Surya grahan mein Sooraj dhak jaata hai, toh main sunglasses se dekh sakta hoon.' Samjhao ye khatarnaak kyun hai aur surakshit tareeka batao.
items.answer: Even the uncovered part of the Sun is bright enough to damage the eyes permanently, and sunglasses do not block enough; use pinhole projection onto paper (looking at the paper, not the Sun) or certified eclipse glasses.
acceptable: sunglasses unsafe; use pinhole projection or eclipse glasses
hints: Ask how bright even a small part of the Sun is
Do sunglasses block enough?
Prompt: look at the ___, not at the Sun
Assert: never look directly; project through a pinhole or use certified glasses

verified.solverAnswer: Even a partly covered Sun can damage the retina (permanent blindness); sunglasses don't block enough. Safe: pinhole projection onto paper (back to Sun) or certified eclipse filters.

items.prompt_en: Draw (or describe) the positions of the Sun, Earth and Moon during a solar eclipse and during a lunar eclipse.
items.prompt_hi: Surya grahan aur chandra grahan ke samay Sooraj, Earth aur Chaand ki sthiti banao (ya batao).
items.answer: Solar eclipse: Sun, Moon, Earth in a line (Moon in the middle). Lunar eclipse: Sun, Earth, Moon in a line (Earth in the middle).
hints: Ask who is in the middle for a solar eclipse
And for a lunar eclipse?
Prompt: solar has the ___ in the middle
Assert: Moon in the middle for solar; Earth in the middle for lunar

verified.solverAnswer: Solar: Sun, Moon, Earth in a line with Moon in the middle (new moon). Lunar: Sun, Earth, Moon with Earth in the middle (full moon).

items.prompt_en: During a total lunar eclipse the Moon often looks a dull coppery red rather than completely black. Is the Moon making its own light now? What is the more likely reason?
items.prompt_hi: Poore chandra grahan mein Chaand aksar bilkul kaala nahi balki halka taambe jaisa laal dikhta hai. Kya Chaand ab khud roshni de raha hai? Zyada sambhav kaaran kya hai?
items.answer: No, the Moon is still non-luminous; a little sunlight is bent through the Earth's atmosphere into the shadow, and mostly reddish light gets through (like the red of sunsets), dimly lighting the Moon.
acceptable: no; sunlight bent through Earth's air, reddish
hints: Ask whether the Moon ever makes light
Think of red sunsets
Prompt: some sunlight passes through Earth's ___
Assert: the Moon is still non-luminous; reddish light from Earth's atmosphere reaches it

verified.solverAnswer: No, the Moon still reflects light; sunlight bent (refracted) by Earth's atmosphere, with blue scattered out, reaches Moon as red light.

items.prompt_en: Your school plans to watch a partial solar eclipse. Using only a sheet of cardboard and a white paper, describe a safe way for everyone to watch it.
items.prompt_hi: Tumhaara school aanshik surya grahan dekhna chahta hai. Sirf ek gatte aur safed kaagaz se sabke liye surakshit tareeka batao.
items.answer: Make a small hole in the cardboard; stand with your back to the Sun; let sunlight pass through the hole onto the white paper held a little away; look only at the paper, where a small image of the partly covered Sun appears. Never look at the Sun through the hole.
acceptable: pinhole projection, back to the Sun, look at the paper
hints: Ask which way you should face
Where should your eyes look?
Prompt: look only at the ___
Assert: pinhole projection with your back to the Sun

verified.solverAnswer: Make a small hole in the cardboard, stand with your back to the Sun and let sunlight pass through the pinhole to project an image onto the white paper; look only at the paper, never at the Sun.

items.prompt_en: Explain to your family the difference between a solar eclipse, a lunar eclipse and the phases of the Moon.
items.prompt_hi: Apne parivaar ko surya grahan, chandra grahan aur chaand ki kalaaon ka farak samjhao.
items.answer: Key ideas: solar eclipse, Moon between Sun and Earth, Moon's shadow on Earth, at new moon, never look directly; lunar eclipse, Earth between Sun and Moon, Earth's shadow on Moon, at full moon, safe to view; phases, how much of the Moon's sunlit half we see, every month, not a shadow; eclipses are rare because the Moon's orbit is tilted.
acceptable: positions, shadows, new vs full moon, phases are not shadows, safety
hints: Ask who is in the middle for each eclipse
What causes the phases?
Prompt: phases are not caused by a ___
Assert: two eclipse alignments, phases from viewing angle, safety rule

verified.solverAnswer: Solar eclipse: Moon between Sun and Earth; lunar: Earth between Sun and Moon; phases: how much of the Moon's lit half we see as it orbits, not shadow; solar needs eye protection.

items.prompt_en: From memory: is it safe to watch a lunar eclipse with your naked eyes?
items.prompt_hi: Yaad se batao: kya chandra grahan nangi aankhon se dekhna surakshit hai?
items.answer: Yes, a lunar eclipse is safe to watch with the naked eye, because we are looking at the Moon, not the Sun.
hints: Ask what you are looking at in a lunar eclipse
Is the Moon dangerously bright?
Prompt: we look at the ___, not the Sun
Assert: yes, it is safe

verified.solverAnswer: Yes, safe to watch lunar eclipse with naked eyes (the Moon only reflects sunlight, not dangerous).

workedExample.problem: Why can a solar eclipse happen only on a new moon day?
steps: For a solar eclipse, the Moon must be between the Sun and the Earth in a straight line
When the Moon is between the Sun and the Earth, its sunlit half faces away from us
That position, with the dark side facing Earth, is the new moon
So a solar eclipse can happen only at new moon
It does not happen every new moon because the Moon's orbit is tilted and usually misses the exact line

Its sunlit half faces ___ from us
This position is the ___ moon
So a solar eclipse can happen only at ___
